sec02-card-f01.front: When does applying for a first Class C instructional permit trigger Georgia's secure-identity paperwork?
sec02-card-f01.expected_back: A first Class C instructional permit requires the secure-identity documentation standards if the applicant has not already met them.

sec02-card-f02.front: What is the earliest age you can apply for a Georgia Class C instructional permit?
sec02-card-f02.expected_back: The Class C instructional-permit application is available beginning at age fifteen.

sec02-card-f03.front: Which four personal or status proofs must every Georgia instructional-permit applicant establish or know?
sec02-card-f03.expected_back: A permit applicant must establish identity, citizenship or lawful presence, and Georgia residence, and must know the Social Security number or document ineligibility for one.

sec02-card-f04.front: What two extra items must a permit applicant under eighteen bring beyond standard identity paperwork?
sec02-card-f04.expected_back: An applicant younger than eighteen must provide school-enrollment evidence and obtain a parent, guardian or responsible adult's signature consenting to the permit.

sec02-card-f05.front: What authority does the adult signer keep over a minor's instructional permit before age eighteen?
sec02-card-f05.expected_back: The adult who signs a minor's permit application can revoke that permit for any reason before the holder turns eighteen.

sec02-card-f06.front: Which two screenings or examinations must you pass to earn a Class C instructional permit?
sec02-card-f06.expected_back: Obtaining the instructional permit requires both a vision screening and the knowledge examination covering signs and driving rules.

sec02-card-f07.front: How much is the testing fee, when is it paid, and what happens if you fail?
sec02-card-f07.expected_back: The handbook lists a ten-dollar testing charge payable before testing, with no refund for a failed component and a new payment for each attempt.

sec02-card-f08.front: Who must sit right beside a Class C permit holder whenever the learner drives?
sec02-card-f08.expected_back: A CP holder may drive a Class C vehicle only with a Class C licensed supervisor aged at least twenty-one, seated alongside the learner and fit and capable of controlling the vehicle.

sec02-card-f09.front: At what age and after how long holding a valid permit can most teens seek Class D?
sec02-card-f09.expected_back: A Class D application ordinarily becomes possible at age sixteen after holding a valid instructional permit for at least one year and one day.

sec02-card-f10.front: What booking and old-permit step must a Class D applicant handle for the road exam?
sec02-card-f10.expected_back: A Class D applicant needs a road-test appointment and must surrender the CP or affirm on the application that surrender is impossible.

sec02-card-f11.front: What school, awareness, consent, and testing steps are required when applying for Class D?
sec02-card-f11.expected_back: For Class D, the applicant must document school enrollment and alcohol-and-drug-awareness education, obtain adult consent, and pass the road driving test.

sec02-card-f12.front: Can the consenting adult cancel a minor's Class D provisional license after it is issued?
sec02-card-f12.expected_back: The adult who consents to the minor's Class D application may revoke that license before the driver turns eighteen.

sec02-card-f13.front: Which two educational programs must every sixteen- or seventeen-year-old complete to get Class D?
sec02-card-f13.expected_back: At age sixteen or seventeen, Class D requires both DDS-approved driver education and the alcohol-and-drug-awareness program.

sec02-card-f14.front: What classroom and behind-the-wheel options make up an approved Georgia driver-education course?
sec02-card-f14.expected_back: The approved driver-education course includes thirty classroom hours or an equivalent online course, together with six hours of certified on-road instruction or completion of the DDS parent-teen guide.

sec02-card-f15.front: How many extra driving hours—including night driving—must Class D applicants certify by affidavit?
sec02-card-f15.expected_back: The Class D education requirement also includes at least forty hours of other driving experience, with at least six hours at night. A DDS affidavit signed at road testing certifies completion.

sec02-card-f16.front: What extra paperwork is needed at road testing when a certified instructor taught your on-road hours?
sec02-card-f16.expected_back: When a certified instructor provides the on-road driver-education component, a separate document confirming that component is required at the road test.

sec02-card-f17.front: Can a teen earn Class D without approved driver education, and where is ADAP offered?
sec02-card-f17.expected_back: Without the required driver education, a teen cannot obtain Class D. The awareness program is available through many schools and online.

sec02-card-f18.front: When may an active-duty military parent's teen use an out-of-state driver-education certificate?
sec02-card-f18.expected_back: A teen whose parent is serving on active United States military duty may use an out-of-state driver-education certificate if it falls within nine months of the teen's sixteenth birthday.

sec02-card-f19.front: What permit-holding exemption and license class apply to a seventeen-year-old who documents military enlistment?
sec02-card-f19.expected_back: A seventeen-year-old who documents military enlistment is exempt from the usual one-year-and-one-day learner-permit holding period; the handbook says this applicant receives Class C.

sec02-card-f20.front: During which overnight hours is a Class D driver barred from driving, and what exceptions exist?
sec02-card-f20.expected_back: A Class D holder is prohibited from driving from midnight until five a.m.; the handbook states that this restriction has no exceptions.

sec02-card-f21.front: Who may ride as a passenger during the first six months on a Class D license?
sec02-card-f21.expected_back: During the first six months of Class D, passengers are restricted to immediate family, including parents, stepparents, grandparents, siblings, stepsiblings, children and anyone living at the driver's residence.

sec02-card-f22.front: How many non-family passengers under twenty-one may ride during months seven through twelve of Class D?
sec02-card-f22.expected_back: In the second six months of Class D, the vehicle may carry at most one passenger younger than twenty-one who is outside the driver's immediate family.

sec02-card-f23.front: Once a driver holds Class D past twelve months, how many non-family passengers under twenty-one are allowed?
sec02-card-f23.expected_back: After the first twelve months of Class D, at most three passengers younger than twenty-one may be outside the driver's immediate family.

sec02-card-f24.front: What conviction record must a Class D holder keep for twelve months before upgrading to Class C?
sec02-card-f24.expected_back: Before seeking Class C, a Class D holder must have no conviction during the preceding twelve months for a major traffic offense that mandates license suspension.

sec02-card-r01.front: When must an applicant for a first Class C license present REAL ID documentation?
sec02-card-r01.expected_back: A first Class C license requires the REAL ID documentation standards if the applicant has not already satisfied them.

sec02-card-r02.front: When may an eighteen-year-old Class D holder upgrade to Class C?
sec02-card-r02.expected_back: At age eighteen, a Class D holder may seek Class C after holding a valid Class D until that age or for one year and one day, with no major-traffic-violation conviction during the preceding twelve months.

sec02-card-r03.front: What must a qualified U.S. citizen surrender or take when exchanging Class D for Class C?
sec02-card-r03.expected_back: A qualified United States citizen exchanging Class D for Class C must surrender the earlier credential or affirm inability to do so; the handbook requires no additional documents or testing for that exchange.

sec02-card-r04.front: What age, permit step, and exam are required to swap an instructional permit directly for Class C?
sec02-card-r04.expected_back: A CP holder must be at least eighteen to exchange the permit for Class C, surrender the permit or affirm inability to surrender it, and pass the road driving test.

sec02-card-r05.front: What driving-experience affidavit must an adult sign when upgrading from a permit to Class C?
sec02-card-r05.expected_back: The CP-to-Class-C applicant must sign an affidavit documenting forty hours of supervised driving, including six nighttime hours.

sec02-card-r06.front: How can an unlicensed adult aged eighteen or older earn Class C without holding a Georgia permit first?
sec02-card-r06.expected_back: An unlicensed applicant aged at least eighteen may apply directly for Class C by meeting document requirements, passing the knowledge and road examinations, and attesting to forty supervised driving hours including six at night.

sec02-card-r07.front: What credential may an adult get first if they want supervised on-road practice before full licensing?
sec02-card-r07.expected_back: An adult who wants supervised practice before full licensing may instead obtain a Class C instructional permit.

sec02-card-r08.front: Within how many days of establishing Georgia residency must a non-exempt new resident apply to drive?
sec02-card-r08.expected_back: A new Georgia resident who wants to drive must apply for the Georgia license or permit within thirty days of establishing residency, subject to the handbook's stated exceptions.

sec02-card-r09.front: Which licensing track applies when someone moves to Georgia holding no valid out-of-state driving card?
sec02-card-r09.expected_back: A new resident without a valid out-of-state permit or license follows Georgia's first-issuance process, with the appropriate teen or adult requirements.

sec02-card-r10.front: What three Georgia teen conditions must a transfer applicant under eighteen usually satisfy despite holding another state's card?
sec02-card-r10.expected_back: A transfer applicant younger than eighteen with a valid license or permit from another state or the District of Columbia normally qualifies for a comparable Georgia document only after meeting Georgia school, driver-education and awareness-program conditions.

sec02-card-r11.front: What surrender rule and expiration limit govern an adult's out-of-state license transfer?
sec02-card-r11.expected_back: For the adult state-to-state transfer route, the earlier license must be surrendered and must not have been expired for two years or more.

sec02-card-r12.front: What substitutes if an adult transfer applicant cannot physically surrender their valid out-of-state license?
sec02-card-r12.expected_back: If an adult transfer applicant cannot surrender the earlier valid license, the handbook requires a certified driving history from the issuing state, dated within thirty days and showing valid status.

sec02-card-r13.front: What is the standard transfer age, and when may a seventeen-year-old transfer an equivalent Class C?
sec02-card-r13.expected_back: The regular transfer minimum is age eighteen. A seventeen-year-old may transfer an equivalent valid Class C license only when it has no restrictions on time, route, driving purpose or passengers.

sec02-card-r14.front: Which documents, number, and screening must an adult state-transfer applicant complete at DDS?
sec02-card-r14.expected_back: An adult transfer applicant must provide the full Social Security number for verification, identity and citizenship or lawful-presence evidence, two Georgia residence documents, and pass a vision screening.

sec02-card-r15.front: In what physical form must transfer identity and lawful-presence records be presented, and are faxes accepted?
sec02-card-r15.expected_back: Transfer identity and lawful-presence documents must be originals or certified copies; a fax is not acceptable.

sec02-card-r16.front: What record does the handbook call for when an applicant's foreign driving credential is missing?
sec02-card-r16.expected_back: For a foreign credential missing from the applicant's possession, the handbook calls for an English-language driving history from the issuing country dated within the last thirty days.

sec02-card-r17.front: How do noncitizens and U.S. citizens differ on keeping foreign driving or ID cards after Georgia issuance?
sec02-card-r17.expected_back: Most noncitizens may keep a valid foreign driving or identification document after Georgia issues its equivalent. A United States citizen must surrender foreign-issued driving and identification credentials.

sec02-card-r18.front: How does Georgia generally process a license issued outside the U.S. states and District of Columbia?
sec02-card-r18.expected_back: A document issued outside the United States states and the District of Columbia is generally processed as a new Georgia issuance, including the examinations applicable to the requested class and required identity, lawful-presence, Social Security and residence evidence.

sec02-card-r19.front: Which three tests do foreign-country applicants ordinarily take, and what exception exists?
sec02-card-r19.expected_back: Foreign-country applicants ordinarily complete knowledge, road and vision examinations; some countries have testing exemptions listed by DDS. The handbook does not identify those countries on this page.

sec02-card-r20.front: What extra rules apply when an applicant younger than eighteen transfers from outside the United States?
sec02-card-r20.expected_back: Applicants younger than eighteen transferring from outside the country must also satisfy the additional teen-licensing requirements.

sec02-card-r21.front: What warning does the handbook give about private websites versus Georgia's government licensing portal?
sec02-card-r21.expected_back: The handbook warns that privately operated sites may charge for information or training. It identifies the DDS government website as the official Georgia licensing source.

sec03-card-f01.front: How is knowledge testing scheduled at DDS centers, and how early before closing must you start?
sec03-card-f01.expected_back: The handbook describes knowledge testing as a walk-in service at DDS centers; applicants must begin at least thirty minutes before closing.

sec03-card-f02.front: How should an applicant arrange reading or hearing assistance for a DDS examination?
sec03-card-f02.expected_back: Applicants needing reading or hearing assistance should contact a service center to arrange an oral examination or a hearing interpreter.

sec03-card-f03.front: Which DDS test parts may offer non-English options, and which stay strictly English-only?
sec03-card-f03.expected_back: Some road-rule examinations are offered in languages other than English, but the applicant still must understand the simple English used on road signs. Sign testing and the driving test are described as English-only.

sec03-card-f04.front: Which personal items and electronics are banned inside the DDS knowledge-testing area?
sec03-card-f04.expected_back: Do not bring writing tools, paper, phones, messaging devices or other wireless equipment into the knowledge-testing area.

sec03-card-f05.front: Whom may you speak with during knowledge testing, and what happens if you break testing rules?
sec03-card-f05.expected_back: During knowledge testing, speak only with the administering examiner. Breaking the testing rules is misconduct and makes the session a failure.

sec03-card-f06.front: How many questions must you answer right on the Road Signs section, and what does it cover?
sec03-card-f06.expected_back: The Road Signs component requires at least fifteen correct answers among its twenty questions. It covers recognition of road signs, signals and markers.

sec03-card-f07.front: What score is required separately on the twenty-question Road Rules component, and what does it test?
sec03-card-f07.expected_back: The Road Rules component separately requires at least fifteen correct answers among its twenty questions, covering responsibilities, laws and safe practices for the license class.

sec03-card-f08.front: Can you walk in for the road-skills driving test, or how must you set it up?
sec03-card-f08.expected_back: Road-skills testing requires an appointment, which the handbook directs applicants to arrange through DDS online services.

sec03-card-f09.front: May you bring a car with driver-assistance features to your road test, and under what condition?
sec03-card-f09.expected_back: A vehicle equipped with driver-assistance systems may be used for the test, but the applicant must show the ability to operate it without relying on that technology.

sec03-card-f10.front: Who provides the vehicle for a Class C or Class D road exam, and what wheel count applies?
sec03-card-f10.expected_back: For a Class C or D road test, the applicant supplies a four-wheel vehicle.

sec03-card-f11.front: When testing with a temporary tag instead of standard plates, what purchase-date limits apply?
sec03-card-f11.expected_back: The road-test vehicle needs valid registration and a plate. With a temporary dealer tag, the applicant must show purchase documentation within thirty days of purchase, or within seven days for a third-party purchase.

sec03-card-f12.front: What coverage, VIN proof, and check must your road-test vehicle clear before pulling out?
sec03-card-f12.expected_back: The road-test vehicle must have liability coverage, acceptable insurance or registration evidence showing its vehicle identification number, and pass a safety inspection.

sec03-card-f13.front: What must you demonstrate if your road-test vehicle does not have illuminated turn signals?
sec03-card-f13.expected_back: If the road-test vehicle lacks illuminated turn indicators, the applicant must be able to demonstrate the required hand signals.

sec03-card-f14.front: Which four contract, driver, and insurance rules apply if you bring a rental car for road testing?
sec03-card-f14.expected_back: A rental vehicle may be used only when the contract permits testing, the applicant is a named driver, and valid vehicle insurance is documented. The rental contract must be provided for review.

sec03-card-f15.front: What does DDS do when severe weather or another hazard makes road testing unsafe?
sec03-card-f15.expected_back: DDS does not conduct the road test when weather or another condition makes it unsafe for the examiner or applicant; affected appointments are to be rescheduled.

sec03-card-f16.front: What curb distance and box dimensions govern parallel parking on the Georgia road test?
sec03-card-f16.expected_back: For test parallel parking, center the vehicle between the standards and finish within eighteen inches of the curb. The stated test space is twenty-two feet long and ten feet deep.

sec03-card-f17.front: How far, how fast, and with what head position must you reverse during the backing exercise?
sec03-card-f17.expected_back: For the backing exercise, reverse approximately fifty feet smoothly and straight, at no more than ten miles per hour, looking behind with the head turned and staying within the boundaries.

sec03-card-f18.front: Where do you stop and how long do you wait for pedestrians at a road-test stop sign or signal?
sec03-card-f18.expected_back: At a test stop sign or signal, approach in the correct lane, signal appropriately, stop before the crosswalk, and remain stopped until pedestrians have cleared the side being traveled. Proceed only when safe.

sec03-card-f19.front: Which maneuver tests your ability to turn the vehicle around inside a confined space?
sec03-card-f19.expected_back: The road test includes turning the vehicle around in a confined space using a three-point turn.

sec03-card-f20.front: What two mechanical habits are graded if you take your road test in a manual-transmission car?
sec03-card-f20.expected_back: When testing in a manual-transmission vehicle, shift correctly and operate the clutch smoothly.

sec03-card-f21.front: How should you position your vehicle and scan when approaching an intersection or corner?
sec03-card-f21.expected_back: Approach an intersection or corner in the proper lane and check both directions.

sec03-card-f22.front: To whom must you yield and wait until clear at intersections during your driving test?
sec03-card-f22.expected_back: Yield during the test to pedestrians, bicyclists and other drivers already entering the intersection, stopping until they have cleared it.

sec03-card-f23.front: What two steps must happen well before starting a turn on your road test?
sec03-card-f23.expected_back: Before a test turn, enter the appropriate lane and give the turn signal far enough in advance.

sec03-card-f24.front: What tech gear and passenger are used during Georgia's remotely examined road test?
sec03-card-f24.expected_back: The handbook describes a remotely examined road test with a dual-facing camera and hands-free phone. A licensed parent, guardian or responsible adult aged at least twenty-one rides as the passenger.

sec03-card-f25.front: Where does the DDS examiner sit during a traditional in-person road test?
sec03-card-f25.expected_back: In the traditional road-test arrangement, the examiner rides in the passenger seat.

sec03-card-f26.front: What must you verify before passing another vehicle during the road test?
sec03-card-f26.expected_back: Before passing during the road test, check ahead and behind to ensure the maneuver will not interfere with traffic.

sec03-card-f27.front: How much following distance must you keep behind the vehicle ahead on your road exam?
sec03-card-f27.expected_back: Maintain enough following space to retain control if the vehicle ahead stops or turns abruptly.

sec03-card-f28.front: What hand, arm, and conversation habits are expected throughout the road test?
sec03-card-f28.expected_back: During the road test, use both hands on the wheel, avoid resting an elbow on the window, and avoid unnecessary conversation with the examiner.

sec03-card-f29.front: What minimum percentage passes the Class C or D road test, and what happens afterward?
sec03-card-f29.expected_back: The Class C or D road-test passing score is at least seventy-five percent. At the end, the examiner can review the score sheet and discuss the result with the applicant.

sec03-card-f30.front: What credential do you walk out with right after passing all exams, and how arrives the permanent card?
sec03-card-f30.expected_back: Passing all required examinations results first in a temporary license or permit; the permanent document is sent by mail.

sec03-card-f31.front: How long must you wait to retry a failed Class C or D test part after the first miss versus later misses?
sec03-card-f31.expected_back: After the first failure of a Class C or D knowledge or road component, wait until the following day before repeating the failed portion. After a second or later failure, the waiting period is seven days.

sec03-card-r01.front: Which away-from-home groups—and household members—qualify for Georgia's renewal-by-mail route?
sec03-card-r01.expected_back: The handbook's renewal-by-mail route covers eligible people temporarily away on active military duty and full-time out-of-state students, including spouses and dependents living with them.

sec03-card-r02.front: Which sole Georgia credential can a physically incapacitated person obtain remotely when unable to visit DDS?
sec03-card-r02.expected_back: An applicant who is physically incapacitated and cannot visit a DDS center may use the described remote service for an identification card only.

sec03-card-r03.front: What three items go into a mail-renewal packet, how long is the term, and what follows next?
sec03-card-r03.expected_back: Mail renewal requires the application, eligibility evidence and any required payment. The handbook describes an eight-year term followed by an in-person renewal.

sec03-card-r04.front: How long expired disqualifies a Georgia license from renewal by mail?
sec03-card-r04.expected_back: A license expired for at least two years cannot be renewed through the handbook's mail-renewal process.

sec03-card-r05.front: Can you change your legal name or residential address through Georgia's mail-renewal process?
sec03-card-r05.expected_back: The mail-renewal route does not allow name or address changes; those changes require an in-person DDS transaction under the described process.

sec03-card-r06.front: Does completing a license renewal by mail produce a federal REAL ID card?
sec03-card-r06.expected_back: The handbook states that a renewal completed by mail does not issue a REAL ID document.

sec03-card-r07.front: How does Georgia handle a legacy license or ID whose document number is a Social Security number?
sec03-card-r07.expected_back: Georgia does not issue driving or identification credentials whose document number is the Social Security number. At issuance or renewal, such an old number is replaced with a random document number.

sec03-card-r08.front: Whom should you notify once DDS replaces your old license or ID document number?
sec03-card-r08.expected_back: After the document number changes, notify insurers or other organizations that use the old license or identification number for verification.

sec03-card-r09.front: What two channels can replace a lost or stolen Georgia license or ID?
sec03-card-r09.expected_back: A lost or stolen credential may be replaced at a DDS center with proof of identity, or online through identity authentication when the online requirements are met.

sec03-card-r10.front: Which single documents can establish identity by themselves when replacing a lost citizen credential?
sec03-card-r10.expected_back: The handbook's single-document replacement identity choices include a sealed certified birth record, naturalization or citizenship certificate, expired Georgia credential, valid United States passport or passport card, consular birth-abroad report, or expired Georgia interim credential.

sec03-card-r11.front: Which immigration documents qualify as replacement identity proof for a noncitizen at DDS?
sec03-card-r11.expected_back: For a noncitizen's replacement identity evidence, the handbook lists a valid foreign passport with valid arrival record, a valid permanent-resident card, or a qualifying employment-authorization document with evidence of a pending status-adjustment application.

sec03-card-r12.front: How many secondary records are required under the alternative replacement route, and what examples count?
sec03-card-r12.expected_back: The alternative replacement route requires two documents from the listed group: Social Security card, original or certified marriage record, prior-year tax return or wage statement, current insurance policy, current vehicle-registration receipt, voter card, military identification or orders, Georgia gun permit, transport-worker identification, or pay stub.

sec03-card-r13.front: On the two-document replacement list, can a wallet insurance card stand in for a current insurance policy?
sec03-card-r13.expected_back: For the replacement alternative-document route, an insurance card does not substitute for the listed current insurance policy.

sec03-card-r14.front: When replacing a card, what is required to get a brand-new document number—and what is the one exception?
sec03-card-r14.expected_back: Changing the document number during replacement requires a police report showing theft, except when the existing number is the Social Security number.

sec03-card-r15.front: Which everyday transactions run through DDS online services, and do REAL ID eligibility rules still apply?
sec03-card-r15.expected_back: Online DDS services include such functions as appointments, eligible renewals and replacements, address changes, record requests and license-status checks. Eligibility requirements, including the applicable REAL ID requirements, still apply.

sec03-card-r16.front: Why can't you rely on postal mail forwarding instead of updating your address directly with DDS?
sec03-card-r16.expected_back: Keep the DDS address record current; postal forwarding does not redirect DDS correspondence.

sec03-card-r17.front: How soon after moving must you update your DDS address, and how do in-person versus online checks differ?
sec03-card-r17.expected_back: After moving, update the mailing or residential address within sixty days at a DDS center or through the online service. An in-person change needs evidence; an online change is checked through the postal service.

sec03-card-r18.front: Where and within how many days must you update a legal name change, and what fee perk applies?
sec03-card-r18.expected_back: A legal name change requires an in-person DDS visit and a corrected license within sixty days. The handbook allows one no-charge replacement for the existing term.

sec03-card-r19.front: Which legal records—including one specific Georgia marriage record—prove a legal name change at DDS?
sec03-card-r19.expected_back: For a name change, provide a certified acceptable marriage document or a court order. A Georgia marriage application is one of the listed document choices.

sec03-card-r20.front: When does a Georgia marriage allow a hyphenated surname on your license?
sec03-card-r20.expected_back: The handbook allows a hyphenated surname based on a Georgia marriage on or after November one, nineteen eighty-two, when the certified marriage application records that surname choice.

sec03-card-r21.front: Which three time spans are offered when ordering a Georgia driving-history report?
sec03-card-r21.expected_back: The handbook offers driving histories covering three years, seven years or the lifetime record.

sec03-card-r22.front: Where do you request a noncertified driving history versus an official certified history?
sec03-card-r22.expected_back: A noncertified driving history can be obtained through an online account; a certified history can be requested at a DDS center with identification or through the mail.

sec03-card-r23.front: What form and identification are required to pick up another driver's Georgia driving history?
sec03-card-r23.expected_back: Collecting another person's driving history requires that licensee's authorization on form DDS-eighteen naming the recipient and identifying the licensee. The recipient must also present identification.

sec03-card-r24.front: What may you mail—and which personal details plus payment are required—to order a driving history by mail?
sec03-card-r24.expected_back: A mailed driving-history request may use DDS-eighteen or a letter specifying the requested history period, full name, license number, birth date and complete mailing address, together with the required payment.

sec05-card-f01.front: What must a turning driver do when a green light runs at the same time as a pedestrian walk signal?
sec05-card-f01.expected_back: A turning driver's green light may coincide with a pedestrian's walk signal. Before turning, stop for pedestrians in the receiving road's crosswalk until they clear the lanes you will use.

sec05-card-f02.front: Where do signs or sightlines make turning around with a U-turn illegal?
sec05-card-f02.expected_back: Do not make a U-turn where a sign forbids it, or on a curve or near a hillcrest when approaching drivers from either direction cannot see you.

sec05-card-f03.front: What two rules govern turning left across the centerline of a multilane two-way road?
sec05-card-f03.expected_back: A left turn across the centerline of a multilane two-way road must comply with any controlling signs or signals and yield to opposing traffic.

sec05-card-f04.front: Which four pedestrian areas must clear before you complete a left turn?
sec05-card-f04.expected_back: Before turning left, wait for pedestrians to clear the traffic lanes, sidewalk, driveway or alley being entered.

sec05-card-f05.front: Is highway parking legal, and what must you aim for if your vehicle breaks down along one?
sec05-card-f05.expected_back: Parking on a highway is prohibited. If a vehicle becomes disabled, make practical efforts to move it off the highway while leaving traffic room and visibility of the vehicle for two hundred feet in both directions.

sec05-card-f06.front: Which four everyday street and corner locations ban stopping, standing, and parking completely?
sec05-card-f06.expected_back: Never stop, stand or park beside another parked vehicle on its street side, on a sidewalk, in an intersection or on a crosswalk.

sec05-card-f07.front: How do safety zones and street excavations restrict stopping, standing, and parking?
sec05-card-f07.expected_back: Do not stop, stand or park between a safety zone and its neighboring curb, or beside a street obstruction or excavation when that would obstruct traffic.

sec05-card-f08.front: Which four structures, rail corridors, and highway types forbid stopping, standing, and parking?
sec05-card-f08.expected_back: Stopping, standing and parking are prohibited on a bridge or overpass, inside a highway tunnel, on railroad tracks or on a controlled-access road.

sec05-card-f09.front: May you stop, stand, or park inside a divided-highway median, crossover, or signed no-parking zone?
sec05-card-f09.expected_back: Do not stop, stand or park in the area separating divided-highway roadways, including a crossover, or at a location signed against parking.

sec05-card-f10.front: What is the only brief stop the Georgia handbook allows directly in front of a driveway?
sec05-card-f10.expected_back: In front of a driveway, the handbook permits a stop only briefly to collect or discharge passengers.

sec05-card-f11.front: Within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant, what lone momentary stop does the Georgia handbook allow?
sec05-card-f11.expected_back: Within fifteen feet of a hydrant, the handbook permits stopping only momentarily for passengers.

sec05-card-f12.front: What rule governs the curb space within twenty feet of an intersection crosswalk?
sec05-card-f12.expected_back: Within twenty feet of an intersection crosswalk, a stop is permitted only momentarily to load or unload passengers.

sec05-card-f13.front: Within thirty feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal, what brief stop is permitted?
sec05-card-f13.expected_back: Within thirty feet of a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal, the handbook permits only a momentary passenger pickup or drop-off.

sec05-card-f14.front: Which two distances—same side and across the street—restrict parking at a fire-station driveway to momentary passenger stops?
sec05-card-f14.expected_back: Within twenty feet of a fire-station driveway, or within seventy-five feet of the point opposite it across the street, the handbook allows only a momentary stop for passengers.

sec05-card-f15.front: What brief stop is allowed within fifty feet of a railroad crossing or at a no-standing sign?
sec05-card-f15.expected_back: Within fifty feet of a rail crossing, or where official signs prohibit standing, the handbook permits only a brief passenger pickup or discharge.

sec05-card-f17.front: In a multilane passing lane, what must you do when faster traffic closes in from behind—even if you are driving the limit?
sec05-card-f17.expected_back: On the passing lane of a multilane road, move right for faster traffic approaching from behind, regardless of your own speed, unless a stated exception applies.

sec05-card-f18.front: Which road or weather conditions excuse staying in the left passing lane?
sec05-card-f18.expected_back: The passing-lane move-right rule allows exceptions when traffic, weather, an obstruction or another hazard makes staying in that lane necessary.

sec05-card-f19.front: Which routing, legal, or toll needs allow remaining in a multilane passing lane?
sec05-card-f19.expected_back: Staying in the passing lane may be necessary to comply with a law or traffic-control device, to leave the road or turn left, or to pay a toll or use a toll pass.

sec05-card-f20.front: Which two categories of official or work vehicles are exempt from the passing-lane move-right rule?
sec05-card-f20.expected_back: Authorized emergency vehicles on official duty and vehicles performing highway construction or maintenance are exceptions to the described passing-lane move-right rule.

sec05-card-f16.front: How do you position your car beside the forward vehicle to begin parallel parking?
sec05-card-f16.expected_back: To start parallel parking, pass the chosen space and stop approximately alongside the car in front of it, leaving about two feet between the vehicles.

sec05-card-f21.front: How do you steer at the start of reversing into a parallel space, and when do you straighten the wheels?
sec05-card-f21.expected_back: When reversing into a parallel space, initially steer sharply right and back slowly. As the front door clears the forward car's rear bumper, straighten the wheels and continue diagonally.

sec05-card-f22.front: When do you cut the steering wheel sharply left while backing into a parallel space?
sec05-card-f22.expected_back: Once the front bumper has cleared the car ahead during parallel parking, steer sharply left while reversing slowly, stopping before contact with the car behind.

sec05-card-f23.front: How do you straighten and center your vehicle once inside a parallel-parking stall?
sec05-card-f23.expected_back: To center the vehicle after reversing into the parallel space, select drive, steer right and pull forward carefully.

sec05-card-f24.front: At which two moments of parallel parking must you use your turn signal?
sec05-card-f24.expected_back: Use the proper turn signal before parallel parking and again before leaving the space.

sec05-card-f25.front: How must you check around the car before backing, and where should you look while moving in reverse?
sec05-card-f25.expected_back: Before reversing, check every side of the vehicle. While backing, turn to look over the right shoulder instead of relying only on mirrors.

sec05-card-f26.front: What extra precaution should drivers of buses or large vehicles use when backing up?
sec05-card-f26.expected_back: For a bus or other large vehicle, use all mirrors and a reliable person to observe and direct the backing maneuver.

sec05-card-r01.front: Which two speed thresholds trigger Georgia's Super Speeder classification upon conviction?
sec05-card-r01.expected_back: The handbook's Super Speeder threshold is a speeding conviction at seventy-five miles per hour or more on a two-lane road, or at eighty-five miles per hour or more on any Georgia road.

sec05-card-r02.front: How much is Georgia's state Super Speeder fee, and what happens if you fail to pay on time?
sec05-card-r02.expected_back: The handbook describes a separate two hundred-dollar state Super Speeder charge in addition to local fines. Late payment results in license suspension and an additional fifty-dollar reinstatement charge.

sec05-card-r03.front: Unless posted otherwise, what is Georgia's general maximum speed in an urban or residential district?
sec05-card-r03.expected_back: Unless a different limit is posted, the handbook's general maximum in an urban or residential district is thirty miles per hour.

sec05-card-r04.front: What default maximum speed applies on an unpaved Georgia county road without speed signs?
sec05-card-r04.expected_back: For an unpaved county road, the handbook's default maximum is thirty-five miles per hour unless posted otherwise.

sec05-card-r05.front: What is Georgia's general maximum speed limit on a rural interstate highway?
sec05-card-r05.expected_back: The handbook's general rural-interstate maximum is seventy miles per hour, subject to the posted limit.

sec05-card-r06.front: What general maximum speed applies on Georgia urban interstates and multilane divided highways unless posted otherwise?
sec05-card-r06.expected_back: On an urban interstate or a multilane divided highway, the handbook gives a general maximum of sixty-five miles per hour unless another limit is posted.

sec05-card-r07.front: What general maximum speed limit governs all other Georgia roads when no different limit is posted?
sec05-card-r07.expected_back: For other areas, the handbook's general maximum is fifty-five miles per hour unless posted otherwise.

sec05-card-r08.front: When must your speed drop down to match a temporary school-zone or construction-zone sign?
sec05-card-r08.expected_back: Road authorities can adjust limits for local conditions temporarily or permanently. Watch signs, including temporary school or construction-zone limits, and reduce speed before entering the zone.

sec05-card-r09.front: When is driving far below normal traffic speed unlawful versus justified?
sec05-card-r09.expected_back: Do not drive so slowly that normal, reasonable traffic is impeded, except when the lower speed is needed to operate safely.

sec05-card-r10.front: Which lane belongs to slower traffic on multi-lane roads, and when must you vacate the passing lane?
sec05-card-r10.expected_back: Where several lanes carry traffic in the same direction, slower traffic should stay right except to pass or turn left. Do not remain in the passing lane while a faster vehicle overtakes from behind.

sec05-card-r11.front: What should you do if your vehicle cannot maintain a highway's posted minimum speed?
sec05-card-r11.expected_back: Some highways have posted minimum speeds. If unable to meet the minimum, choose another route.

sec05-card-r12.front: Between what distances from the nearest rail must you stop when crossing warnings or approaching trains require it?
sec05-card-r12.expected_back: At a railroad crossing, stop between fifteen and fifty feet from the closest rail when warning lights flash, a gate is down, a flagger signals a stop, a posted stop sign requires it, or an approaching train presents an immediate hazard.

sec05-card-r13.front: Is driving around, under, or through a lowered railroad crossing gate ever permitted?
sec05-card-r13.expected_back: Never drive around, under or through a lowered railroad gate.

sec05-card-r14.front: What four conditions must all be true before moving forward after stopping for a train?
sec05-card-r14.expected_back: After stopping for a train, wait until every track is clear, warning lights have stopped, gates are raised and crossing is safe.

sec05-card-r15.front: How should you use speed, eyes, and ears as you approach and reach railroad tracks?
sec05-card-r15.expected_back: Approach tracks cautiously, prepare to stop, look and listen in both directions, then check again before crossing.

sec05-card-r16.front: When may you enter a railroad crossing, and how should you drive once safely committed?
sec05-card-r16.expected_back: Do not enter a railroad crossing without enough room to drive completely through it without stopping. Once safely committed, keep moving across the tracks.

sec05-card-r17.front: What immediate actions must you take if your car stalls directly on railroad tracks?
sec05-card-r17.expected_back: If the vehicle stalls on tracks, leave it immediately and move away. Find the emergency-notification sign and call for help, explaining that a vehicle is on the tracks.

sec07-card-f01.front: How many stages does Georgia's graduated licensing program use for ages fifteen through eighteen, and what four factors control moving ahead?
sec07-card-f01.expected_back: Georgia's described graduated licensing program moves teens aged fifteen through eighteen through three stages, with age, required preparation, demonstrated driving ability and responsible behavior controlling progression.

sec07-card-f02.front: Who must appear with an applicant under age eighteen, and what two actions must that person complete?
sec07-card-f02.expected_back: An applicant younger than eighteen needs a responsible adult present to sign the application and complete the required affidavit.

sec07-card-f03.front: What three qualifications must the responsible adult meet to sign a minor's license or permit application?
sec07-card-f03.expected_back: The signing responsible adult must be at least eighteen, be competent to verify the application and personally know the applicant.

sec07-card-f04.front: What types of records must a signing parent or guardian bring to prove their relationship to a minor applicant?
sec07-card-f04.expected_back: A parent or guardian signing as the responsible adult must provide acceptable records establishing the relationship, such as school or military records, tax information or a driving or identification credential.

sec07-card-f05.front: When can a social worker sign as a minor's responsible adult, and what proof must they present?
sec07-card-f05.expected_back: A social worker who has worked with the applicant may qualify as the responsible adult, with employee identification or an agency letter.

sec07-card-f06.front: Under what documentation condition may a certified driving instructor act on behalf of a minor's parent, guardian, or responsible adult?
sec07-card-f06.expected_back: A certified driving instructor may act for the parent, guardian or responsible adult when the authorization is supported by notarized documentation.

sec07-card-f07.front: How can an employee at the shelter where a teen lives qualify to sign as the responsible adult?
sec07-card-f07.expected_back: An employee of the shelter where an applicant lives may qualify as the responsible adult with employee identification or a shelter letter.

sec07-card-f08.front: Besides a parent, social worker, or shelter employee, who else may serve as a minor's responsible adult with proper records?
sec07-card-f08.expected_back: The handbook also allows a stepparent or another person identified through acceptable government or school evidence to serve as the responsible adult.

sec07-card-f09.front: Which five standard school-enrollment or completion credentials can satisfy a minor's school-evidence requirement?
sec07-card-f09.expected_back: A minor's school-related evidence may be a school-enrollment certificate, high-school diploma, special diploma, high-school-completion certificate or GED.

sec07-card-f10.front: What conditions must a college or vocational transcript meet to count as school evidence for a minor?
sec07-card-f10.expected_back: An official sealed college or vocational transcript dated within the last thirty days is another listed school-evidence choice for a minor.

sec07-card-f11.front: What two additional alternatives can replace a standard school-enrollment certificate for homeschooled teens or GED learners?
sec07-card-f11.expected_back: A homeschool declaration of intent or an adult-literacy certificate showing current GED study are also listed alternatives to the minor's school-enrollment certificate.

sec07-card-f12.front: At what ages must a teen complete DDS-approved driver education to earn a Class D provisional license?
sec07-card-f12.expected_back: DDS-approved driver education is required for a Class D provisional license at age sixteen or seventeen.

sec07-card-f13.front: Which permit begins Georgia's graduated licensing program, and what is the minimum age to apply for it?
sec07-card-f13.expected_back: The graduated program starts with CP, the Class C instructional permit, for which an applicant may apply beginning at age fifteen.

sec07-card-f14.front: What four categories of identity and residency proof are required for a teen's first Class C instructional permit?
sec07-card-f14.expected_back: A first CP issuance requires the applicable REAL ID documentation, identity and lawful-presence evidence, Georgia residency, and the full Social Security number or evidence of ineligibility.

sec07-card-f15.front: Which screening and two-part written exam must a Class C instructional permit applicant pass?
sec07-card-f15.expected_back: A CP applicant must pass the vision screening and the knowledge test covering signs and road rules.

sec07-card-f16.front: What ongoing authority does the adult who signs a minor's instructional permit application hold until the teen turns eighteen?
sec07-card-f16.memory_hook: Signing adult can revoke under eighteen
sec07-card-f16.expected_back: The adult signing a minor's CP application gives consent and can revoke the permit before the holder reaches eighteen.

sec07-card-f17.front: Who must sit right beside a Class C instructional permit holder whenever they drive?
sec07-card-f17.expected_back: A CP holder must be accompanied in the adjacent seat by a fit, capable Class C licensed driver aged at least twenty-one who can exercise control over the vehicle.

sec07-card-r01.front: What minimum age and instructional permit holding period apply to an ordinary Class D provisional license application?
sec07-card-r01.expected_back: The ordinary Class D application requires age sixteen or older and a valid instructional permit held for one year and one day, together with the applicable REAL ID requirements.

sec07-card-r02.front: What steps, documents, and exam are required to turn an instructional permit into a Class D license?
sec07-card-r02.expected_back: To obtain Class D, arrange the road test, surrender CP or affirm that surrender is impossible, provide school evidence and awareness-program completion, obtain adult consent and pass the road test.

sec07-card-r03.front: What classroom and behind-the-wheel components make up an approved Class D driver-education course?
sec07-card-r03.expected_back: The Class D education course uses thirty classroom hours or equivalent online study, plus six certified on-road hours or the approved parent-teen driving guide.

sec07-card-r04.front: How many supervised practice hours—and how many at night—are required for Class D preparation, and what can serve as the affidavit?
sec07-card-r04.expected_back: Class D preparation includes at least forty hours of other driving, with at least six hours at night. Completion of the approved parent-teen guide serves as an affidavit for that requirement.

sec07-card-r05.front: What extra paperwork is required at road testing when a certified instructor provided your on-road course hours?
sec07-card-r05.expected_back: When a certified instructor supplies the on-road course component, a separate confirming document is required at testing.

sec07-card-r06.front: When can a teen with an active-duty United States military parent use an out-of-state driver-education certificate in Georgia?
sec07-card-r06.expected_back: A teen with a parent on active United States military duty may use an out-of-state driver-education certificate when it is within nine months of the sixteenth birthday.

sec07-card-r07.front: How do licensing rules change for a seventeen-year-old who documents military enlistment and passes the road test?
sec07-card-r07.expected_back: A seventeen-year-old documenting military enlistment need not meet the usual one-year-and-one-day CP holding period and receives Class C after successfully completing the road test.

sec07-card-r08.front: During what overnight hours is a Class D driver barred from driving, and what exceptions does the handbook allow?
sec07-card-r08.expected_back: A Class D driver must not drive between midnight and five a.m.; the handbook gives no exception to this restriction.

sec07-card-r09.front: Who may ride with a Class D driver during the first six months, and who counts in that group?
sec07-card-r09.expected_back: Only immediate family may ride during the first six months of Class D. The handbook includes parents, stepparents, grandparents, siblings, stepsiblings, children and other household residents in that group.

sec07-card-r10.front: How many non-family passengers under twenty-one may ride with a Class D driver in months seven through twelve versus after one year?
sec07-card-r10.expected_back: During the second six months of Class D, at most one passenger younger than twenty-one may be outside the driver's immediate family. After the first year, that maximum becomes three.

sec07-card-r11.front: What clean driving-record rule applies during the twelve months before upgrading from Class D to Class C?
sec07-card-r11.expected_back: Class D progression to Class C requires no major-traffic-offense conviction causing mandatory suspension during the preceding twelve months.

sec07-card-r12.front: What rules apply to a teen who moves to Georgia without holding a valid license or permit from another state?
sec07-card-r12.expected_back: A teen moving to Georgia without a valid license or permit from another state must meet the requirements for a Georgia resident's initial credential.

sec07-card-r13.front: What happens when a teen moves to Georgia holding a valid out-of-state permit or license?
sec07-card-r13.expected_back: A teen with a valid out-of-state license or permit normally may seek a comparable Georgia document, but differing state requirements must be resolved with DDS.

sec07-card-r14.front: How does the adult who signed a minor's application officially request revocation before the teen's eighteenth birthday?
sec07-card-r14.expected_back: The adult who signed a minor's credential application can request revocation before the eighteenth birthday using the department's designated form with a notarized signature.

sec07-card-r15.front: Which specific violations—and what single-offense point threshold—trigger license suspension for a driver younger than twenty-one?
sec07-card-r15.expected_back: For a driver younger than twenty-one, the handbook lists suspension for hit-and-run, street racing, fleeing an officer, reckless or aggressive driving, and other offenses assessed at least four points.

sec07-card-r16.front: Which three specific traffic violations are highlighted as four-or-more-point offenses that suspend a young driver?
sec07-card-r16.expected_back: The listed high-point teen offenses include unlawfully passing a school bus, improper passing on a hill or curve, and speeding at least twenty-four miles per hour above the limit.

sec07-card-r17.front: How many total points within twelve months will suspend the license of a driver younger than eighteen?
sec07-card-r17.expected_back: A driver younger than eighteen also faces suspension for accumulating at least four points within a twelve-month period.

sec07-card-r18.front: Who is the only driver eligible for a limited driving permit during a listed non-DUI under-twenty-one suspension?
sec07-card-r18.expected_back: The handbook's limited-permit exception for the listed non-DUI teen suspension applies only to an applicant aged at least eighteen whose conviction was for speeding from twenty-four through thirty-three miles per hour above the limit.

sec07-card-r19.front: Is a limited driving permit available during a young driver's first DUI suspension in Georgia?
sec07-card-r19.expected_back: The teen DUI suspension summary states that no limited driving permit is available for the described first DUI suspension.

sec08-card-f01.front: Who must obey official road signs and traffic signals, and who is the only authority that can override them?
sec08-card-f01.expected_back: Drivers and bicyclists must obey official road signs and traffic signals unless an officer or emergency worker directs otherwise.

sec08-card-f02.front: How many basic sign shapes does the Georgia handbook teach, and why should you read shape and color early?
sec08-card-f02.expected_back: The handbook describes seven basic sign shapes and recommends recognizing shape and color early enough to respond from a distance.

sec08-card-f03.front: What kind of message does a tall rectangular road sign normally carry, and how must drivers treat it?
sec08-card-f03.expected_back: A tall rectangular sign generally gives a regulatory instruction that must be obeyed like a traffic law.

sec08-card-f04.front: What type of helpful road information is generally displayed on a wide rectangular sign?
sec08-card-f04.expected_back: A wide rectangular sign generally provides guidance such as a destination, direction or special information.

sec08-card-f05.front: What does a diamond-shaped sign warn about, and what are its standard background and marking colors?
sec08-card-f05.expected_back: A diamond-shaped warning sign identifies an actual or possible hazard on or beside the road; the described standard warning colors are yellow with black words or symbols.

sec08-card-f06.front: What does an eight-sided sign require, and where must you stop when a stop line or crosswalk is present?
sec08-card-f06.expected_back: An eight-sided sign means stop. Make a complete stop at the marked stop line, or before the near-side crosswalk when there is no line.

sec08-card-f07.front: Where must you bring your vehicle to a stop when a stop-sign approach has neither a stop line nor a crosswalk?
sec08-card-f07.expected_back: If a stop-controlled approach has neither a stop line nor a crosswalk, stop where approaching traffic can best be observed.

sec08-card-f08.front: After making your full stop, who must you wait for before pulling forward into the intersection?
sec08-card-f08.expected_back: After stopping, remain stopped for pedestrians crossing the side you will travel on and yield to traffic close enough to create a conflict before moving again.

sec08-card-f09.front: What hazard ahead does a round warning sign announce, and what actions help you check for a train?
sec08-card-f09.expected_back: A round warning sign indicates a railroad crossing ahead. Slow, look, listen and prepare to stop; opening a window may help you hear a train.

sec08-card-f10.front: How must you respond to an approaching train at a rail crossing, and what lane maneuver is banned there?
sec08-card-f10.expected_back: At a rail crossing, stop for an approaching train rather than trying to judge whether you can beat it. Passing at the crossing is prohibited.

sec08-card-f11.front: What speed and stopping duties apply when you approach a triangular yield sign?
sec08-card-f11.expected_back: A triangular yield sign requires a speed appropriate for conditions and a stop when needed, at the marked line if one is present.

sec08-card-f12.front: Which vehicles have priority over you after you slow or stop at a yield sign?
sec08-card-f12.expected_back: After slowing or stopping at a yield sign, give way to vehicles in the intersection or approaching closely on the intersecting road.

sec08-card-f14.front: How many feet ahead of school grounds or a school crossing is the school warning sign placed?
sec08-card-f14.expected_back: The handbook places the described school warning sign from one hundred fifty through seven hundred feet before the school grounds or crossing.

sec08-card-r01.front: What do regulatory signs tell road users, and must bicyclists obey them alongside motor-vehicle drivers?
sec08-card-r01.expected_back: Regulatory signs specify permitted and prohibited actions, and bicyclists as well as other drivers must obey them.

sec08-card-r02.front: What does a red circle with a diagonal slash from upper-left to lower-right mean on a regulatory sign?
sec08-card-r02.expected_back: A red circle crossed diagonally from its upper-left side toward its lower-right side means that the pictured action is prohibited.

sec08-card-r03.front: What dangerous situation does a wrong-way sign warn you about on a one-way road or ramp?
sec08-card-r03.expected_back: The wrong-way warning identifies an approach where travel in your present direction onto the one-way road or ramp is forbidden.

sec08-card-r04.front: How does a one-way regulatory sign restrict your direction of travel?
sec08-card-r04.expected_back: The one-way instruction permits travel only in the direction indicated by its arrow.

sec08-card-r05.front: When does a do-not-enter sign apply, and what must you avoid doing at that approach?
sec08-card-r05.expected_back: The do-not-enter meaning applies when traffic on the one-way road is coming toward your approach; do not continue onto that road.

sec08-card-r06.front: What maneuver is outlawed at an intersection posted with a no-U-turn restriction?
sec08-card-r06.expected_back: A no-U-turn restriction forbids reversing direction through a U-turn at that intersection.

sec08-card-r07.front: What action is barred at an intersection displaying a no-right-turn regulatory sign?
sec08-card-r07.expected_back: A no-right-turn restriction prohibits turning right at that intersection.

sec08-card-r08.front: Which side of a median island or roadway obstruction must you pass when a keep-right sign appears?
sec08-card-r08.expected_back: A keep-right instruction requires passing a median or obstruction on its right side.

sec08-card-r09.front: What change on the road ahead does a reduced-speed-ahead warning sign prepare you for?
sec08-card-r09.expected_back: A reduced-speed-ahead warning announces an approaching area with a lower established limit.

sec08-card-r10.front: Where must slower vehicles position themselves on a multi-lane road with a slower-traffic-keep-right sign?
sec08-card-r10.expected_back: When multiple lanes carry traffic in your direction, a slower-traffic-keep-right instruction directs slower vehicles toward the rightmost lanes.

sec08-card-r11.front: What does a posted fifty-five-mile-per-hour speed limit sign establish—and what misconception should you avoid?
sec08-card-r11.expected_back: The handbook's posted-limit example of fifty-five miles per hour identifies the maximum allowed in that signed area, not a statewide default for every road.

sec08-card-r12.front: When does the lower speed limit on a flashing school-zone sign take effect?
sec08-card-r12.expected_back: The school-zone example applies its reduced limit while the yellow lights are flashing.

sec08-card-r13.front: May you turn right after stopping at a red light when a no-right-turn-on-red sign is posted?
sec08-card-r13.expected_back: A no-right-turn-on-red restriction still prohibits that turn after the driver has come to a full stop.

sec08-card-r14.front: What restriction does a bicycle-prohibition regulatory sign place on riders?
sec08-card-r14.expected_back: The bicycle-prohibition sign bars bicycles from entering the indicated roadway.

sec08-card-r15.front: What restriction does a truck-prohibition regulatory sign enforce on the roadway ahead?
sec08-card-r15.expected_back: The truck-prohibition sign bars trucks from entering the indicated roadway.

sec09-card-f01.front: What two background-and-marking color pairs appear on warning signs, and what do warning signs announce?
sec09-card-f01.expected_back: Warning signs are generally yellow with black markings, sometimes fluorescent green with black markings. They announce a hazard or traffic change immediately ahead that may require action.

sec09-card-f02.front: What roadway alignment ahead does a successive right-then-left sharp-turn warning sign announce?
sec09-card-f02.expected_back: A warning for successive sharp turns to the right and then left announces that sequence of road direction.

sec09-card-f03.front: How do a sharp-right-turn warning and a right-curve warning compare when reading alignment signs?
sec09-card-f03.expected_back: A sharp-right-turn warning and a right-curve warning describe different changes of alignment ahead.

sec09-card-f04.front: What pattern of road geometry ahead does a winding-road warning sign alert you to?
sec09-card-f04.expected_back: A winding-road warning announces a series of bends ahead.

sec09-card-f05.front: What kind of junction ahead can a side-road warning sign identify?
sec09-card-f05.expected_back: A side-road warning can identify a joining road, including one entering at an angle.

sec09-card-f06.front: What intersection layout ahead does a four-way crossroad warning sign indicate?
sec09-card-f06.expected_back: A crossroad warning means another road intersects the highway ahead.

sec09-card-f07.front: How should you adjust your driving when a warning sign shows your road ending at a junction ahead?
sec09-card-f07.memory_hook: Slow, yield, turn left or right
sec09-card-f07.expected_back: Where the road ends ahead, slow and be ready to yield or stop before turning left or right.

sec09-card-f08.front: Why does a narrow-bridge warning sign call for extra caution as you approach?
sec09-card-f08.expected_back: A narrow-bridge warning calls for caution because the bridge ahead has room for only two traffic lanes.

sec09-card-f09.front: What road-surface feature does a dip warning sign mark, and what action does it call for?
sec09-card-f09.expected_back: A dip warning identifies a depression in the road ahead and calls for slowing.

sec09-card-f10.front: What pavement hazard does a bump warning sign identify, and how should you respond?
sec09-card-f10.expected_back: A bump warning identifies a raised irregularity ahead and calls for slowing.

sec09-card-f11.front: What does a soft-shoulder warning tell you about the road edge, and when may you pull onto it?
sec09-card-f11.expected_back: A soft-shoulder warning means the road edge cannot be treated like the regular traveled surface; use that shoulder only in an emergency.

sec09-card-f12.front: What roadway change ahead does a divided-highway-begins warning sign tell you to prepare for?
sec09-card-f12.expected_back: A divided-highway-begins warning advises preparation for a change of lane position as separated roadways begin.

sec09-card-f13.front: What transition ahead does a divided-highway-ends warning sign prepare drivers to handle?
sec09-card-f13.expected_back: A divided-highway-ends warning advises preparation for a lane-position change as the separation ends.

sec09-card-f14.front: What does a warning sign showing opposing arrows announce when a separated one-way roadway changes?
sec09-card-f14.expected_back: A warning that a separated one-way roadway becomes two-way means opposing traffic will soon share the highway.

sec09-card-f15.front: When must you stay out of an underpass marked with a low-clearance warning sign?
sec09-card-f15.expected_back: At a low-clearance warning, do not enter the underpass if either the vehicle or its load exceeds the posted maximum height.

sec09-card-f16.front: What two steps should you take when you spot a steep-hill warning sign ahead?
sec09-card-f16.expected_back: At a steep-hill warning, slow and prepare to use a lower gear to control speed and protect the brakes.

sec09-card-f17.front: What driving adjustment does a traffic-signal-ahead warning sign call for?
sec09-card-f17.expected_back: A traffic-signal-ahead warning calls for reducing speed before the intersection.

sec09-card-f18.front: What hazard does a slippery-when-wet warning highlight, and which rain window does the handbook call most dangerous?
sec09-card-f18.expected_back: A slippery-when-wet warning calls attention to reduced traction; the handbook identifies the first half hour of rain as especially hazardous.

sec09-card-f19.front: What should you prepare to do when a warning sign shows traffic merging from the right?
sec09-card-f19.expected_back: A merging-traffic warning from the right advises preparing to let that traffic join safely.

sec09-card-f20.front: Which three groups of road crossers can diamond crossing-warning signs alert you to watch for?
sec09-card-f20.expected_back: Crossing warnings can announce areas where animals, people or other vehicles may enter the road.

sec09-card-f21.front: How do your responsibilities compare at a yield-ahead warning sign versus a stop-ahead warning sign?
sec09-card-f21.expected_back: A yield-ahead warning calls for slowing and readiness to stop if necessary; a stop-ahead warning calls for slowing and preparing for the required stop.

sec09-card-f22.front: What must drivers do whenever pedestrians are occupying a crosswalk?
sec09-card-f22.expected_back: Drivers must stop and stay stopped while pedestrians occupy the crosswalk.

sec09-card-f23.front: Which side of the road holds the no-passing-zone warning sign, and where must any pass be finished?
sec09-card-f23.expected_back: The warning marking the start of a no-passing zone is placed on the road's left side; any passing maneuver must finish before that point.

sec09-card-f24.front: What does a small speed plaque mounted beneath a yellow warning sign tell drivers?
sec09-card-f24.expected_back: An advisory-speed plaque accompanying a warning identifies the speed advised for the warned condition.

sec09-card-r01.front: What two navigation jobs do guide signs perform, and which five sign types belong in that group?
sec09-card-r01.expected_back: Guide signs identify the current road or help a driver reach a destination. The handbook includes route, information, destination, distance and location signs in this group.

sec09-card-r02.front: What shape are guide signs usually, and how can companion plaques help you reach a road or facility?
sec09-card-r02.expected_back: Guide signs are often rectangular but may have another shape. A companion arrow or destination word can show how to reach a road or facility.

sec09-card-r03.front: What do the numbers printed on highway route shields or exit guide signs represent?
sec09-card-r03.expected_back: Numbers on route or exit guide signs identify a particular highway, interstate or exit rather than a speed requirement.

sec09-card-r04.front: What upcoming road connection does a junction guide assembly announce?
sec09-card-r04.expected_back: A junction guide can announce where named roads cross or meet the road being traveled.

sec09-card-r05.front: How far apart are roadside mileposts spaced, and where does Georgia start numbering them from zero?
sec09-card-r05.expected_back: Milepost markers occur at mile intervals beside the road. The handbook describes numbering from zero at the southern or western state boundary where the route begins.

sec09-card-r06.front: Below what speed does a vehicle travel when displaying the slow-moving-vehicle emblem?
sec09-card-r06.expected_back: The slow-moving-vehicle emblem identifies a vehicle traveling below twenty-five miles per hour under the handbook's definition.

sec09-card-r07.front: What does a designated-bicycle-route guide sign tell motorists about the road?
sec09-card-r07.expected_back: A designated-bicycle-route guide identifies a road used as an official bicycle route and calls for caution around riders.

sec09-card-r08.front: What does a public-parking guide sign direct drivers toward?
sec09-card-r08.expected_back: A public-parking guide points toward the available parking area.

sec09-card-r09.front: What must you do at a white railroad crossbuck, and what does a numbered plaque below it show?
sec09-card-r09.expected_back: At a railroad crossbuck, slow, look and listen and yield to an approaching train. A panel beneath the crossbuck identifies the number of tracks.

sec09-card-r10.front: What action is mandatory whenever red warning lights are flashing at a railroad crossing?
sec09-card-r10.expected_back: A flashing red warning at a railroad crossing requires a complete stop.

sec09-card-r11.front: What background and marking colors identify construction and maintenance warnings, and why are they posted early?
sec09-card-r11.expected_back: Construction and maintenance warning signs use orange backgrounds with black markings to announce dangers early enough for a speed adjustment.

sec09-card-r12.front: What color combination marks motorist service signs, and what kinds of stops do they point to?
sec09-card-r12.expected_back: Blue-and-white service signs direct travelers to facilities such as fuel, food, lodging, a hospital or camping.

sec09-card-r13.front: How does a Georgia express lane work, and how is the toll collected?
sec09-card-r13.expected_back: An express lane offers the option of paying a toll for an alternative to congested regular lanes; the source describes charges taken from a registered account.

sec09-card-r14.front: How does a reversible express lane operate across the day, and what do signs show while direction switches?
sec09-card-r14.expected_back: A reversible express lane changes direction during the day. The source says signs display a closed condition while the travel direction is being changed.

sec10-card-f01.front: Who must obey Georgia traffic signals — and what sole human authority overrides a lit signal?
sec10-card-f01.expected_back: Drivers, bicyclists and pedestrians must obey traffic signals unless an officer directs traffic differently.

sec10-card-f02.front: How must you treat an intersection when its ordinary traffic signal is completely dark and out of power?
sec10-card-f02.expected_back: When an intersection's ordinary traffic signal is completely inoperative, treat every approach as stop-controlled.

sec10-card-f03.front: When a malfunctioning intersection signal switches into flashing mode, how do flashing yellow and flashing red differ?
sec10-card-f03.expected_back: When an ordinary malfunctioning intersection signal flashes, follow its displayed color: flashing yellow calls for caution, while flashing red requires a stop before proceeding safely.

sec10-card-f04.front: Where must you stop for a steady red traffic light, and how long must you wait unless a legal turn-on-red applies?
sec10-card-f04.expected_back: A steady red traffic light requires stopping before entering the crosswalk or intersection and waiting for green, subject to separately stated permitted red-turn rules.

sec10-card-f05.front: What transition does a steady yellow traffic light announce, and what response does Georgia require?
sec10-card-f05.expected_back: A steady yellow signal warns that green is ending and red is next; slow and prepare to stop.

sec10-card-f06.front: Before rolling forward on a fresh green light, which two groups inside the intersection still hold priority?
sec10-card-f06.expected_back: A green signal permits movement only when safe after stopping for pedestrians and yielding to vehicles already in the intersection.

sec10-card-f07.front: What movement does a lit green arrow allow, and whom must you still yield to or stop for?
sec10-card-f07.expected_back: A green arrow permits careful travel only in the arrow's direction, after yielding to vehicles in the intersection and stopping for pedestrians.

sec10-card-f08.front: What warning does a yellow arrow send right after a green arrow turns off?
sec10-card-f08.expected_back: A yellow arrow following a green arrow warns drivers to clear the intersection.

sec10-card-f09.front: Which roadside sign matches a flashing red traffic light, and what three-step sequence must you follow?
sec10-card-f09.expected_back: Treat a flashing red traffic light like a stop sign: stop fully, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, then proceed cautiously when safe.

sec10-card-f10.front: How should you approach and pass through an intersection showing a flashing yellow light?
sec10-card-f10.expected_back: A flashing yellow traffic light requires slowing and caution before continuing through the junction.

sec10-card-f11.front: What does a flashing yellow left-turn arrow allow, and what signal faces oncoming traffic?
sec10-card-f11.expected_back: A flashing yellow left-turn arrow permits the left turn only after yielding to pedestrians and oncoming vehicles; opposing traffic still has green.

sec10-card-f12.front: What action does a steady WALK pedestrian signal authorize?
sec10-card-f12.expected_back: A walk indication permits a pedestrian to leave the curb and begin crossing.

sec10-card-f13.front: How does a DO NOT WALK signal govern pedestrians still on the curb versus someone already mid-crosswalk when it flashes?
sec10-card-f13.expected_back: A do-not-walk indication tells pedestrians not to begin crossing. During the flashing phase, someone already crossing should finish rather than start from the curb.

sec10-card-f14.front: Which turning or combined movement restrictions can overhead lane-control signs assign to a specific lane?
sec10-card-f14.expected_back: Overhead lane-use signs can restrict a lane to a left turn, right turn, or the stated combination of straight and left movement.

sec10-card-f15.front: How is a pedestrian hybrid beacon triggered, and what does it do for people on foot?
sec10-card-f15.expected_back: A pedestrian hybrid beacon is activated by a pedestrian's push button to stop road traffic and provide a walk indication for crossing.

sec10-card-f16.front: Why shouldn't you treat an unlit pedestrian hybrid beacon like a broken four-way traffic light?
sec10-card-f16.expected_back: A pedestrian hybrid beacon normally remains dark until a person activates it; this is the beacon's inactive state rather than an ordinary failed intersection signal.

sec10-card-f17.front: Right after a pedestrian presses the crossing button, what is the very first light a hybrid beacon shows drivers?
sec10-card-f17.expected_back: After pedestrian activation, the hybrid beacon first displays flashing yellow to approaching traffic.

sec10-card-f18.front: After flashing yellow, what second phase appears on a pedestrian hybrid beacon and what must drivers do?
sec10-card-f18.expected_back: The hybrid beacon next changes to steady yellow, advising drivers to slow and prepare for a stop.

sec10-card-f19.front: What driver action is required when a pedestrian hybrid beacon displays two steady red lights?
sec10-card-f19.expected_back: Double steady red indications at a pedestrian hybrid beacon require drivers to stop.

sec10-card-f20.front: During a hybrid beacon's wig-wag alternating flashing-red phase, what must each driver do before rolling?
sec10-card-f20.expected_back: During the following alternating flashing-red phase of the hybrid beacon, each driver must make a complete stop and proceed only after pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk.

sec10-card-f21.front: What display does a pedestrian hybrid beacon show once its crossing cycle finishes?
sec10-card-f21.expected_back: After the pedestrian hybrid beacon's crossing cycle ends, it returns to dark until another pedestrian activates it.

sec10-card-r01.front: Which three traffic-control jobs do pavement markings share with roadside signs?
sec10-card-r01.expected_back: Pavement markings warn, direct and regulate traffic, as signs do.

sec10-card-r02.front: Where must you halt when a white stop line crosses your lane, and roughly where does it sit in urban areas?
sec10-card-r02.expected_back: A transverse white stop line marks the stopping position for a traffic control. Stop at that line rather than beside the sign or signal; the handbook describes an urban placement about four feet before the crosswalk.

sec10-card-r03.front: How may white crosswalk lines be painted across pavement, and who holds right-of-way inside them?
sec10-card-r03.expected_back: White crosswalk markings may span all or part of the pavement or use a ladder pattern. Pedestrians in the crosswalk have priority over motor traffic.

sec10-card-r04.front: Do marked crosswalks appear only at street corners, and what extra device sometimes accompanies them?
sec10-card-r04.expected_back: A marked crosswalk can occur midblock as well as at an intersection, sometimes with a pedestrian signal at the crossing.

sec10-card-r05.front: What letters and symbol mark a railroad approach on the asphalt, and what passing and stopping rules apply?
sec10-card-r05.expected_back: A railroad approach may carry a large pavement X with the letters R on either side. A yellow centerline-side marking prevents passing, and active train warnings require a stop.

sec10-card-r06.front: What traffic flows does a centerline divide, and what does a single broken yellow line allow on a two-lane road?
sec10-card-r06.expected_back: A centerline separates opposing traffic. On a two-lane road, a broken yellow centerline permits passing in either direction only when safe.
