sec10-card-r07.front: How does a solid yellow stripe on your side of a two-lane centerline — or double solid yellow — restrict passing?
sec10-card-r07.expected_back: A solid yellow line on your side of a two-lane centerline prohibits passing there. If both centerlines are solid, neither direction may pass.

sec10-card-r08.front: How do dashed double white lane stripes contrast with solid double white lane stripes?
sec10-card-r08.expected_back: Dashed double white lane markings permit crossing into the neighboring lane; solid double white markings prohibit changing lanes across them.

sec10-card-r09.front: What does a solid white right edge line mark at night, and what can a yellow left edge line warn of?
sec10-card-r09.expected_back: Solid white edge lines show the side of the pavement, especially helpful after dark. A yellow left edge line can warn of a raised or narrow median.

sec10-card-r10.front: Which traffic direction flows on both sides of broken white lane lines?
sec10-card-r10.expected_back: Broken white lane lines divide lanes carrying traffic in the same direction.

sec10-card-r11.front: On an undivided road with four or more lanes, when is crossing the double solid yellow centerline legal?
sec10-card-r11.expected_back: On a road with at least four lanes and opposing flows, double solid yellow lines separate directions. The handbook permits crossing them only for a left turn into or from a street, driveway, private road or alley.

sec10-card-r12.front: Which lane position should you hold on a multilane road except when overtaking slower same-direction traffic?
sec10-card-r12.expected_back: On a multilane road, stay right except when passing traffic moving in the same direction.

sec10-card-r13.front: What road feature does diagonal yellow pavement striping mark, and on which side of it must you stay?
sec10-card-r13.expected_back: Diagonal yellow striping identifies a narrowing or obstruction area; keep to the right of that marked area.

sec10-card-r14.front: What maneuver is a shared center turn lane reserved for, and what is the maximum distance you may travel inside it?
sec10-card-r14.expected_back: A shared center turn lane is reserved for left turns, not general travel. Enter it no earlier than three hundred feet before the intended left turn.

sec10-card-r15.front: What specific conflict must you scan for right before pulling into a shared two-direction center turn lane?
sec10-card-r15.expected_back: Before entering a two-direction center turn lane, check carefully for an opposing driver entering it to turn left.

sec10-card-r16.front: How is a bike lane normally marked near the right edge, and where does it sit beside a right-turn-only lane?
sec10-card-r16.expected_back: A bicycle lane is usually separated by a solid white line near the right road edge; where a right-turn-only lane exists, the bicycle lane lies to its left to accommodate through cyclists.

sec10-card-r17.front: May motorists drive or park in a bicycle lane — and what rule governs crossing it for a turn?
sec10-card-r17.expected_back: Do not drive or park in a bicycle lane except when crossing it for a turn, and yield to bicyclists before that crossing.

sec10-card-r18.front: In what direction does roundabout traffic circulate, who holds right-of-way at entry, and which way do you turn to exit?
sec10-card-r18.expected_back: Enter a roundabout toward the right and circulate counterclockwise, yielding to traffic already circulating. Exit by turning toward the right.

sec10-card-r19.front: What three speed, pedestrian, and gap steps belong as you approach a single-lane roundabout?
sec10-card-r19.expected_back: At a single-lane roundabout, slow to the advisory speed, stop for pedestrians at the approach crosswalk and wait for an opening in circulating traffic.

sec10-card-r20.front: Before exiting a roundabout, what signal and pedestrian precautions are required?
sec10-card-r20.expected_back: Before the roundabout exit, signal the intended departure and stop for pedestrians in the exit crosswalk.

sec10-card-r21.front: When must you pick your lane for a multilane roundabout, and what guides your choice?
sec10-card-r21.expected_back: For a multilane roundabout, choose the correct lane before entering by following the lane signs and pavement arrows.

sec10-card-r22.front: Which lanes must you yield to when entering a multilane roundabout, and may you change lanes inside the circle?
sec10-card-r22.expected_back: Entering a multilane roundabout requires yielding to circulating vehicles in both lanes. Keep the chosen lane while entering and circulating; do not change lanes within the roundabout.

sec10-card-r23.front: How should pedestrians cross at a roundabout using splitter refuges, and where must they never walk?
sec10-card-r23.expected_back: A pedestrian should use the roundabout's crossing and refuge, checking that vehicles stop before each crossing stage, and must not walk to the center island.

sec10-card-r24.front: How may experienced cyclists ride a roundabout — and how should children or less comfortable riders cross instead?
sec10-card-r24.expected_back: An experienced cyclist may ride through a roundabout with traffic, using the center of the lane and stopping for crosswalk pedestrians. Children or riders uncomfortable in traffic should walk their bicycles and follow pedestrian rules.

sec10-card-r25.front: Do the roundabout diagrams in the Georgia manual cover every possible roundabout layout you will encounter?
sec10-card-r25.expected_back: The handbook's roundabout drawings are examples and do not represent every roundabout design.

sec14-card-f01.front: What is the very first thing you must do immediately after being involved in a crash?
sec14-card-f01.expected_back: After involvement in a crash, stop at once in a safe location.

sec14-card-f02.front: When must you immediately notify the nearest law-enforcement agency after a Georgia crash?
sec14-card-f02.expected_back: The handbook requires immediate notice to the nearest law-enforcement agency when a crash causes injury or death, or property damage exceeding five hundred dollars.

sec14-card-f03.front: What duty do you owe to anyone injured after a collision?
sec14-card-f03.expected_back: Provide reasonable assistance to an injured person after a crash.

sec14-card-f04.front: When and how should you warn approaching traffic at a crash scene?
sec14-card-f04.expected_back: Warn approaching traffic only when doing so does not put you or others at risk; use hazard lamps if possible and reflective triangles when available.

sec14-card-f05.front: Which four pieces of information must you both give and collect after a crash?
sec14-card-f05.expected_back: Exchange the driver's name, address, plate number and license number with others involved in the crash, and obtain the corresponding information from the other driver.

sec14-card-f06.front: What must you do—and what details belong on a note—if you damage an unattended parked vehicle?
sec14-card-f06.expected_back: If you damage a vehicle with nobody attending it, locate its owner or leave a note where that owner can readily find it. Include your contact name and address plus the name of your vehicle's owner.

sec14-card-f07.front: Why shouldn't you assume crash victims are fine just because they say they aren't hurt?
sec14-card-f07.expected_back: Do not assume someone is uninjured merely because the person says so; seek professional assistance promptly.

sec14-card-f08.front: Why should you avoid moving an injured person unnecessarily at a crash scene?
sec14-card-f08.expected_back: Avoid unnecessary movement of an injured person, since unskilled handling may worsen an injury.

sec14-card-f09.front: When must drivers move crash vehicles to a safe refuge after a multilane highway or expressway collision?
sec14-card-f09.expected_back: After a crash on a multilane highway or expressway with no apparent serious injury or death, drivers must move the involved vehicles to a safe refuge when the vehicles can be driven normally and safely.

sec14-card-f10.front: Under what safety condition should you move a crash-involved vehicle out of traffic?
sec14-card-f10.expected_back: Move a crash vehicle only if doing so will not create further danger or harm to people, the vehicles or the roadway.

sec14-card-f11.front: If you cannot move your drivable vehicle after a crash, who may you ask to move it for you?
sec14-card-f11.expected_back: If a crash participant cannot move the vehicle, that person may ask a nearby driver with a valid license of the appropriate class to move it.

sec14-card-f12.front: Does pulling your vehicle to a safe refuge admit fault or cancel your duty to stop and swap details?
sec14-card-f12.expected_back: Moving a vehicle to safety under the described crash rule does not by itself establish fault or eliminate the driver's duties to stop and provide information.

sec14-card-f13.front: What reporting option do you still keep after moving a crash vehicle out of traffic for safety?
sec14-card-f13.expected_back: A driver who moves a crash vehicle under the safety rule retains the ability to file a written report with the local police agency.

sec14-card-r01.front: How can a deer standing quietly beside the roadway react when an approaching car startles it?
sec14-card-r01.expected_back: Deer behavior is unpredictable; an animal standing beside the road may run toward traffic when startled rather than away from it.

sec14-card-r02.front: Where should your eyes continually scan when driving through areas known for deer?
sec14-card-r02.expected_back: In areas known for deer, continually scan both the traveled road and its shoulders for animals.

sec14-card-r03.front: Why must you slow down immediately when you spot one deer cross ahead of you or another car?
sec14-card-r03.expected_back: Slow when a deer crosses ahead of your vehicle or another vehicle, since deer often travel in groups and another may follow.

sec14-card-r04.front: What two immediate steps should you take if you spot a deer on or beside the road at night?
sec14-card-r04.expected_back: If a deer is seen beside or on the road at night, reduce speed immediately and use low beams to avoid dazzling it.

sec14-card-r05.front: What should you do—and avoid doing—when a deer suddenly runs directly into your path?
sec14-card-r05.expected_back: When an animal runs into the path, reduce speed as much as possible. The handbook warns against swerving for a deer because that can cause a collision with traffic or a departure from the roadway.

sec14-card-r06.front: Who should you notify as soon as possible after a collision involving a deer?
sec14-card-r06.expected_back: After a collision involving a deer, notify the police as soon as possible.

sec14-card-r07.front: During which two daily time windows should you stay extra alert for deer, while keeping watch all day?
sec14-card-r07.expected_back: Be especially alert for roadside deer in early morning and late evening, while remembering that deer can also appear at other times of day.

sec01-card-f01.front: What legal basis allows a Georgia law-enforcement officer to pull over a vehicle?
sec01-card-f01.expected_back: An officer may stop a vehicle on reasonable suspicion of a traffic or criminal violation.

sec01-card-f02.front: Which four actions should you take right away when an officer signals a traffic stop?
sec01-card-f02.expected_back: When an officer signals a stop, signal your own movement, pull safely beside or off the road, switch off the engine and audio, and remain inside unless directed otherwise.

sec01-card-f03.front: What cabin lighting and hand rules apply during a nighttime traffic stop?
sec01-card-f03.expected_back: During a nighttime traffic stop, turn on the passenger-compartment light. Keep hands visible and follow the officer's instructions.

sec01-card-f04.front: Which side of your car might an officer walk up to, and which window should you lower?
sec01-card-f04.expected_back: An officer may approach either side of the vehicle. Open the window on that side so the officer can communicate with you.

sec01-card-f05.front: What must you disclose at first contact during a stop, and when should you reach for papers?
sec01-card-f05.expected_back: At the first contact during a stop, tell the officer if a weapon is in the vehicle. Await instructions before reaching for documents.

sec01-card-f06.front: When may a stopped motorist ask an officer to show official identification?
sec01-card-f06.expected_back: A driver may request identification when an officer in plain clothes has not displayed credentials.

sec01-card-f07.front: What does an officer typically explain at a stop, and which three items must you have ready?
sec01-card-f07.expected_back: At a stop, the officer generally explains the reason and may ask about the trip. Be prepared to provide the driver's license, registration and insurance evidence.

sec01-card-f08.front: What should you do if your license, registration, or insurance proof sits beyond easy reach?
sec01-card-f08.expected_back: If requested documents are beyond easy reach, explain where they are and wait for the officer to acknowledge you before retrieving them.

sec01-card-f09.front: How should you position your hands and yourself if an officer instructs you to exit the vehicle?
sec01-card-f09.expected_back: When told to leave the vehicle, keep your hands visible and stand where the officer directs.

sec01-card-f10.front: What three outcomes can conclude a traffic stop?
sec01-card-f10.expected_back: A traffic stop can end with a warning, a traffic ticket that may carry a fine, or an arrest, and the officer usually explains the action being taken.

sec01-card-f11.front: Where should you challenge a disputed traffic citation instead of arguing on the shoulder?
sec01-card-f11.expected_back: Ask for clarification respectfully. A disputed citation can be contested in court; prolonging an argument at the roadside is discouraged.

sec01-card-f12.front: Does signing a Georgia traffic citation admit guilt, and what can happen if you refuse to sign?
sec01-card-f12.expected_back: Signing a traffic citation does not admit guilt. Refusing the signature may result in arrest.

sec01-card-f13.front: What does the Georgia handbook advise if you have concerns about an officer's conduct?
sec01-card-f13.expected_back: For concerns about an officer's conduct, the handbook recommends requesting a supervisor as soon as practicable after the stop.

sec01-card-f14.front: Within how many days must a new Georgia resident obtain a Georgia license or permit to drive?
sec01-card-f14.expected_back: A person who becomes a Georgia resident and wants to drive on Georgia roads must obtain the state's license or permit within thirty days.

sec01-card-f15.front: How does having a permanent home define Georgia residency when someone travels away?
sec01-card-f15.expected_back: Georgia residency includes having a permanent home in the state with an intention to return when away.

sec01-card-f16.front: Which three work, school, or stay milestones can establish Georgia residency under the handbook?
sec01-card-f16.expected_back: Accepting work or conducting a trade in Georgia, enrolling one's children in school there, or remaining in the state for at least thirty days can establish residency under the handbook's criteria.

sec01-card-f17.front: When is a federal employee exempt from needing a Georgia license, and what agency caveat applies?
sec01-card-f17.expected_back: A federal government employee driving a vehicle owned by or leased to the United States government, or driving on official business, is exempt from needing a Georgia license unless the federal government or one of its agencies requires a state license.

sec01-card-f18.front: At what minimum age may a nonresident visitor drive in Georgia with a valid home license?
sec01-card-f18.expected_back: A nonresident aged at least sixteen may drive with a valid home-state or home-country license in immediate possession, while remaining subject to applicable Georgia driving restrictions.

sec01-card-f19.front: Who in a nonresident active-duty military household may drive in Georgia using a valid home-state license?
sec01-card-f19.expected_back: A nonresident serving on active duty in the United States armed forces may use a valid home-state license. The same exception covers a spouse or dependent child with a valid home-state license.

sec01-card-f20.front: How long after returning stateside may active-duty personnel drive on a license issued abroad by the armed forces?
sec01-card-f20.expected_back: Someone serving on active duty in the United States armed forces who carries a valid license issued abroad by the United States armed forces may drive with it for up to forty-five days after returning to the United States.

sec01-card-f21.front: When is operating a tractor or farm implement on a Georgia highway exempt from driver licensing?
sec01-card-f21.expected_back: A person temporarily operating a tractor or other farm equipment on a highway for farm business is within the handbook's exception to obtaining a Georgia license.

sec01-card-f22.front: When may a military reserve member drive a government-owned or leased vehicle under the licensing exception?
sec01-card-f22.expected_back: A member of a United States military reserve component may operate a government-owned or leased motor vehicle under the licensing exception when performing reserve duties.

sec01-card-f23.front: Who must accompany an applicant during the driving exam to obtain a license?
sec01-card-f23.expected_back: During the driving examination to obtain a license, the applicant must be accompanied by a licensed responsible adult aged at least twenty-one, or by a certified examiner or department agent.

sec01-card-f24.front: Who qualifies for Georgia's migrant-farm-worker licensing exception?
sec01-card-f24.expected_back: The migrant-farm-worker exception applies to someone working in Georgia for fewer than ninety days in a calendar year who holds a valid license from another state.

sec01-card-f25.front: How may an unlicensed fifteen-year-old Georgia resident take in-car driving lessons, and what check comes first?
sec01-card-f25.expected_back: A Georgia resident aged at least fifteen may receive actual in-car instruction in a noncommercial training vehicle under the direct personal supervision of a DDS-licensed instructor. The instructor must check an unlicensed trainee's vision before driving instruction.

sec01-card-f26.front: Where does the personal-transportation-vehicle licensing exception apply?
sec01-card-f26.expected_back: The personal-transportation-vehicle licensing exception covers a roadway maintained only for those vehicles, or a crossing of another road at a location designated for motorized-cart crossings.

sec01-card-f27.front: What age, license, and translation rules govern the nonresident-student licensing exception?
sec01-card-f27.expected_back: The nonresident-student exception requires an age of at least sixteen, immediate possession of a valid home license, and an international driving permit when that license is not in English. Georgia's applicable license restrictions still govern.

sec01-card-f28.front: What enrollment and tuition proof must a student carry to use the nonresident licensing exception?
sec01-card-f28.expected_back: A student using the nonresident licensing exception must be enrolled now or in the immediately preceding enrollment period, have paid nonresident tuition for that period, and possess proof of payment.

sec01-card-r01.front: Who must accompany an applicant under eighteen to sign the application and adult affidavit?
sec01-card-r01.expected_back: An applicant younger than eighteen needs a parent, guardian or responsible adult present to sign the application and complete the required adult affidavit.

sec01-card-r02.front: Which two school and safety-course records must every applicant younger than eighteen document?
sec01-card-r02.expected_back: Applicants younger than eighteen must document completion of the alcohol and drug awareness program and satisfaction of the school-enrollment requirement.

sec01-card-r03.front: What education and supervised driving hours are required for Class D at age sixteen or seventeen?
sec01-card-r03.expected_back: For a Class D credential at age sixteen or seventeen, the handbook requires approved driver education and at least forty hours of supervised driving, including six hours after dark.

sec01-card-r04.front: What generally happens to your previous license, permit, or ID during renewal, replacement, or transfer?
sec01-card-r04.expected_back: Renewal, replacement and transfer generally require surrendering the earlier license, permit or identification card; some cases require surrendering all valid credentials.

sec01-card-r05.front: How do foreign-credential retention rules differ between most noncitizens and United States citizens?
sec01-card-r05.expected_back: Most noncitizens may retain a valid foreign credential when Georgia issues an equivalent document. United States citizens are not allowed to retain a foreign-issued license, permit or identification card in this process.

sec01-card-r06.front: What minimum visual acuity and horizontal field of view are required for initial noncommercial licensing?
sec01-card-r06.expected_back: For initial noncommercial licensing, the handbook specifies vision of at least twenty out of sixty in one eye, with or without corrective lenses, and a horizontal visual field of at least one hundred forty degrees.

sec01-card-r07.front: Which form goes to an eye doctor if you fail the DDS vision screen, and what special lenses can it cover?
sec01-card-r07.expected_back: An applicant who fails the DDS vision screening receives form DS-two hundred seventy-four for completion by a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist and submission to DDS for an eligibility evaluation. The form may also document a need for bioptic lenses.

sec01-card-r08.front: What happens when you need glasses or contacts to pass vision screening, and what must you disclose later?
sec01-card-r08.expected_back: Passing the vision screening with glasses or contact lenses results in a corrective-lens restriction. The driver must disclose corrective-lens use at each DDS transaction.

sec01-card-r09.front: What can happen if you change an earlier answer about needing corrective lenses, such as after eye surgery?
sec01-card-r09.expected_back: Changing an earlier answer about corrective-lens use may lead to another vision screening or a required vision-report form.

sec01-card-r10.front: How often must drivers sixty-four and older screen vision versus drivers using bioptic lenses?
sec01-card-r10.expected_back: Drivers aged sixty-four or older must complete a vision screening every eight years. Drivers using bioptic lenses need updated medical information every two years.

sec01-card-r11.front: What is Georgia's standard minimum age for noncommercial Class C, and which seventeen-year-old is exempted?
sec01-card-r11.expected_back: The handbook's regular noncommercial Class C minimum age is eighteen. It includes an exception for a seventeen-year-old new resident transferring a valid equivalent Class C license.

sec01-card-r12.front: Which ages hold provisional Class D, and what does adding the letter P to a class mean?
sec01-card-r12.expected_back: Class D is the provisional credential for ages sixteen and seventeen. Adding the letter P to a class designates an instructional permit, as in CP.

sec01-card-r13.front: Which payment methods does DDS accept, and which three paper instruments are rejected?
sec01-card-r13.expected_back: The listed DDS payment choices include cash, qualifying bank-logo cards and supported mobile payment. Checks, money orders and cashier's checks are excluded.

sec01-card-r14.front: How much can eligible online DDS transactions save, and is that reflected in printed fee tables?
sec01-card-r14.expected_back: An eligible online transaction may receive the handbook's five-dollar discount; the printed fee table does not incorporate that discount.

sec01-card-r15.front: How many free name or address updates do you get per license term, and what do later updates cost?
sec01-card-r15.expected_back: The handbook allows one free name or address change during an issuance term, with other changes made in that same transaction included. Later changes require the full renewal fee.

sec01-card-r16.front: What expiration date does a duplicate keep, and what happens inside one hundred fifty days of expiration?
sec01-card-r16.expected_back: A duplicate or replacement retains the original credential's expiration date. When the credential is within one hundred fifty days of expiration, a full renewal is required for this regular-license path.

sec01-card-r17.front: Can DDS place more than one safety restriction on a driver, and where do restrictions show?
sec01-card-r17.expected_back: DDS may impose multiple license restrictions when needed for safe operation; the applicable restrictions appear on the credential.

sec01-card-r18.front: What exams and documents are required to renew a Georgia license expired more than two years?
sec01-card-r18.expected_back: After a license has been expired for more than two years, renewal requires vision, driving, road-sign and road-rule examinations, plus REAL ID documents if those requirements were not previously satisfied.

sec01-card-r19.front: What must you carry whenever driving and present when law enforcement asks?
sec01-card-r19.expected_back: Carry the appropriate license or permit when driving, and display it when a law-enforcement officer requests it.

sec01-card-r20.front: What standard and document examples satisfy REAL ID primary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r20.expected_back: REAL ID identity evidence must be an acceptable original or certified document, such as a birth certificate, United States passport, naturalization certificate or qualifying immigration document.

sec01-card-r21.front: What Social Security knowledge and Georgia residence paperwork must a REAL ID applicant bring?
sec01-card-r21.expected_back: A REAL ID applicant must know the complete Social Security number so DDS can verify it electronically, and provide two Georgia residence documents dated within the preceding six months.

sec01-card-r22.front: What must you bring if your current legal name differs from your birth or identity document?
sec01-card-r22.expected_back: When the current legal name differs from the identity document, certified legal-name-change evidence bearing the required seal is necessary, even if the existing license already shows the correct name.

sec01-card-r23.front: Why isn't a minor's passport enough by itself to prove adult guardianship at DDS?
sec01-card-r23.expected_back: For a minor, a passport does not by itself establish guardianship; the handbook calls for a birth certificate or court document establishing that relationship.

sec01-card-r24.front: How often must an applicant relying on immigration records bring original immigration documents to DDS?
sec01-card-r24.expected_back: An applicant using immigration records must present the original immigration documents each time the handbook requires a license or identification service.

sec01-card-r25.front: What does the star on a Georgia card mark, and does it guarantee remote service forever?
sec01-card-r25.expected_back: The REAL ID star indicates the document's REAL ID status. The handbook describes possible later online or automated-service eligibility rather than guaranteeing that every future transaction can be completed remotely.

sec04-card-f01.front: Who wins when a police officer or firefighter waves you through a red light or stop sign?
sec04-card-f01.expected_back: Follow traffic signs and signals, but obey a police officer or firefighter directing traffic even when that direction differs from the devices.

sec04-card-f02.front: May you drive past barricades onto a road officially closed for roadwork or a special event?
sec04-card-f02.expected_back: Do not drive on a road officially closed for construction, an event or another authorized reason.

sec04-card-f03.front: What does right of way identify, and what must you do if someone ignores your priority?
sec04-card-f03.expected_back: Right of way identifies who may make a traffic movement. Give way to prevent a collision even when another person fails to respect your lawful priority.

sec04-card-f04.front: How must you handle a stop sign when cross-street traffic does not have a stop?
sec04-card-f04.expected_back: At a stop sign where cross traffic does not stop, first stop and then yield to people or vehicles already in the intersection or close enough to make entry dangerous.

sec04-card-f05.front: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who yields?
sec04-card-f05.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection, when vehicles arrive together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

sec04-card-f06.front: How do pedestrians, arrival order, and simultaneous ties work at an all-way stop?
sec04-card-f06.expected_back: At an all-way stop, yield to pedestrians and let vehicles proceed in arrival order. When vehicles arrive at about the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right.

sec04-card-f07.front: How promptly should you move on your turn at a stop sign—and what if someone jumps ahead?
sec04-card-f07.expected_back: Take your turn at a stop-controlled intersection when safe, without needless delay. If another driver takes it, allow that vehicle to proceed rather than insist on priority.

sec04-card-f08.front: Who must you yield to when turning left at an intersection or into a driveway or alley?
sec04-card-f08.expected_back: Turning left at a junction, or entering a driveway or alley on the left, requires yielding to opposing traffic.

sec04-card-f09.front: How should you adjust speed and readiness when approaching a yield sign?
sec04-card-f09.expected_back: At a yield sign, reduce speed enough for safety and be ready to stop. Stop when necessary and continue only with a safe opening.

sec04-card-f10.front: What should merging drivers do, and how should mainline drivers respond where another road joins?
sec04-card-f10.expected_back: When merging without a stop, adjust speed and position to join safely. When another road merges into yours, move away if safely possible; otherwise adjust your speed and position to let the traffic join.

sec04-card-f11.front: What must you do when your signal turns green while traffic conflict still occupies the intersection?
sec04-card-f11.expected_back: A green signal does not authorize entering an occupied or unsafe intersection. Wait until the traffic conflict has cleared.

sec04-card-f12.front: What two steps apply before pulling out of or crossing from a private road or alley?
sec04-card-f12.expected_back: Before entering or crossing a highway from a private road or alley, stop and yield to vehicles and pedestrians already using the road or sidewalk being crossed.

sec04-card-f13.front: How must you clear the way for an emergency vehicle using lights and siren without creating new hazards?
sec04-card-f13.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle using a siren and emergency lights, slow, move safely to the shoulder or as far right as practicable, and stop. Avoid endangering others or blocking an intersection or the emergency vehicle's turn.

sec04-card-f14.front: Who receives right-of-way inside a highway construction or maintenance area?
sec04-card-f14.expected_back: In a construction area, yield to highway-maintenance workers and their vehicles.

sec04-card-f15.front: When is turning right at a steady red traffic light legal in Georgia?
sec04-card-f15.expected_back: A right turn at a red traffic light is permitted unless the intersection has a sign prohibiting that turn.

sec04-card-f16.front: What three requirements must you satisfy before completing a permitted turn on red?
sec04-card-f16.expected_back: A permitted turn on red requires a complete stop first, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, and a determination that the turn can be completed safely.

sec04-card-f17.front: Under what exact street and lane setup does Georgia allow a left turn on red?
sec04-card-f17.expected_back: A left turn on red is permitted from the left lane of a one-way street to another one-way street carrying traffic to the left, unless a posted sign prohibits it. Stop, yield and confirm a safe opening first.

sec04-card-f18.front: What do flashing yellow lights on a school bus warn drivers to do?
sec04-card-f18.expected_back: Flashing yellow school-bus lights warn approaching drivers to slow and prepare to stop, watching particularly for children beside or crossing the road.

sec04-card-f19.front: Who must stop for a school bus flashing red lights with extended stop arms, and when is oncoming traffic exempt?
sec04-card-f19.expected_back: When a school bus displays red flashing lights and its extended stop arms while loading or unloading, passing it is prohibited. Opposite-direction traffic across a dividing median need not stop, but must watch for children.

sec04-card-f20.front: What two options satisfy Georgia's Move Over law when passing covered roadside vehicles?
sec04-card-f20.expected_back: For the roadside emergency, sanitation or utility vehicles covered by the Move Over law, change to the next lane when safe. If a safe lane change is unavailable, drive below the posted limit and be ready to stop.

sec04-card-f21.front: Which emergency and service operations receive protection under Georgia's Move Over law?
sec04-card-f21.expected_back: The described Move Over protection includes authorized emergency vehicles displaying flashing warning lights, and active sanitation or utility workers using cones or flashing-light vehicles.

sec04-card-r01.front: Where may you begin passing on a two-lane road, and how much room must remain ahead?
sec04-card-r01.expected_back: On a two-lane road, begin passing only in a marked passing zone and only with enough space to return fully to the right before the zone ends or an intersection is reached.

sec04-card-r02.front: Before an oncoming vehicle closes within how many feet must you finish a two-lane pass?
sec04-card-r02.expected_back: A two-lane passing maneuver must be completed before an approaching vehicle is within two hundred feet of your vehicle.

sec04-card-r03.front: What visual checks must happen before pulling into the left lane to pass?
sec04-card-r03.expected_back: Before pulling out to pass, check rear and side mirrors and look over the shoulder for the blind spot; make sure another vehicle is not already passing you.

sec04-card-r04.front: How do you use your mirrors and turn signals to pull out and return during a pass?
sec04-card-r04.expected_back: Signal left before passing. Return right only when safely clear and able to see the passed vehicle in the rearview mirror; signal right for the return and cancel the signal afterward.

sec04-card-r05.front: Which centerline markings and signs prohibit passing on a two-lane road?
sec04-card-r05.expected_back: Do not pass on a two-lane road where the line on your side is solid yellow, where double yellow lines prohibit the move, or where a no-passing sign is posted.

sec04-card-r06.front: Within what distance of tracks, bridges, viaducts, or tunnels is two-lane passing prohibited?
sec04-card-r06.expected_back: On a two-lane road, passing is prohibited within one hundred feet of a railroad crossing, bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

sec04-card-r07.front: Which four traffic, terrain, surface, or bus situations always ban passing?
sec04-card-r07.expected_back: Do not pass where an oncoming vehicle makes the move unsafe, where a hill or curve hides approaching traffic, on the shoulder, or past a school bus stopped for passengers.

sec04-card-r08.front: When may you cross left of the centerline to steer around a roadway obstruction?
sec04-card-r08.expected_back: Driving left of the centerline to get around an obstruction is allowed only after yielding to oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-r09.front: On a multilane two-way highway, when are you allowed to cross left of the centerline?
sec04-card-r09.expected_back: On a multilane two-way highway, do not cross left of the centerline except when signs or signals authorize it or when turning left into a private road, alley or driveway.

sec04-card-r10.front: In which two roadway situations does Georgia allow passing another vehicle on the right?
sec04-card-r10.expected_back: Passing on the right is allowed beside a vehicle turning or preparing to turn left when the pavement has room for both vehicles, or on a highway with at least two same-direction lanes.

sec04-card-r11.front: How should you manage your speed while another vehicle is overtaking you?
sec04-card-r11.expected_back: When being passed, do not accelerate until the passing vehicle has completely cleared you. A slight speed reduction can help it finish; remain alert for unsafe actions.

sec04-card-r12.front: May you overtake a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian at a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
sec04-card-r12.expected_back: Do not pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian at a marked crosswalk or an unmarked intersection crosswalk.

sec04-card-r13.front: How far back should you stop for someone in a crosswalk?
sec04-card-r13.expected_back: When stopping for a person in a crosswalk, leave enough space for other approaching drivers to see the entire crossing.

sec04-card-r14.front: How should you approach an intersection when cars in neighboring lanes stay stopped despite a green light?
sec04-card-r14.expected_back: Approach an intersection with stopped vehicles slowly and ready to stop even if their signal permits travel; those vehicles may be screening a pedestrian from view.

sec04-card-r15.front: What is Georgia's preferred way to overtake a bicycle when road and traffic conditions allow?
sec04-card-r15.expected_back: Approach a bicycle cautiously and, when road and traffic conditions permit, change to a lane that is not adjacent to it before passing.

sec04-card-r16.front: If you cannot change lanes to pass a bicycle in Georgia, what speed and clearance rules apply?
sec04-card-r16.expected_back: When changing lanes to pass a bicycle is impossible, unlawful, or unsafe, slow to a reasonable speed for traffic that is at least ten miles per hour under the posted limit or twenty-five miles per hour, whichever is higher, while keeping at least three feet of clearance at all times.

sec04-card-r17.front: How much of a traffic lane belongs to a motorcyclist, and how must you pass one?
sec04-card-r17.expected_back: A motorcyclist is entitled to the entire lane. Pass in a neighboring lane rather than sharing the motorcycle's lane.

sec04-card-r18.front: How does Georgia law distinguish unlawful lane weaving from lawful highway passing?
sec04-card-r18.expected_back: Weaving between lanes merely to outrun traffic is unlawful. Pass slower traffic only through safe lane changes with clear signals.

sec04-card-r19.front: How early and steadily must you signal before making a left or right turn?
sec04-card-r19.expected_back: Signal continuously far enough before each left or right turn to warn other drivers; avoid abrupt last-moment turns.

sec04-card-r20.front: Should you ever flash your turn signal to tell a driver behind you that passing is clear?
sec04-card-r20.expected_back: Do not flash a turn signal to tell a following driver that it is safe to pass.

sec04-card-r21.front: How should you position for a right turn, and who has priority in a curbside bicycle lane?
sec04-card-r21.expected_back: For a right turn, give advance notice, approach in the right lane near the curb or road edge, and yield to bicyclists continuing straight in a bicycle lane.

sec04-card-r22.front: Which lane must you finish a single-lane or multi-lane right turn inside?
sec04-card-r22.expected_back: Finish a right turn in the right lane. Where several marked lanes turn together, finish in the corresponding receiving lane.

sec04-card-r23.front: From which lane do you start a left turn, and how must your wheels point while waiting?
sec04-card-r23.expected_back: For a left turn, signal early and approach from the far-left lane in your direction or the provided turn lane. Keep the wheels straight until the turn begins.

sec04-card-r24.front: Which road users must you yield to before starting a left turn?
sec04-card-r24.expected_back: Before a left turn, yield to opposing vehicles, including bicycles, and to pedestrians crossing either road.

sec04-card-r25.front: Which receiving lane should you enter when completing a single-lane or multi-lane left turn?
sec04-card-r25.expected_back: When signs, signals and a safe opening permit the left turn, finish in the receiving lane nearest the centerline or center lanes. With multiple turn lanes, use the corresponding receiving lane.

sec04-card-r26.front: May you switch lanes inside the intersection after starting a left turn?
sec04-card-r26.expected_back: After entering the intersection for a left turn, do not switch lanes within the intersection.

sec04-card-r27.front: How long must you remain stopped when turning into a street where pedestrians are in the crosswalk?
sec04-card-r27.expected_back: When turning into a road with pedestrians in its crosswalk, stop and remain stopped until they clear the lanes you will travel through.

sec06-card-f01.front: What roadway areas and rolling operations can a Georgia work zone cover?
sec06-card-f01.expected_back: A work zone may cover work on the road, its shoulders or nearby areas, including moving operations such as utility work, surveying or snow removal.

sec06-card-f02.front: Which three guides direct traffic through roadwork or detours, and which background color warns of work?
sec06-card-f02.expected_back: Work-zone signs, pavement markings and flaggers direct traffic through the work area or a marked detour. Orange warns of road work.

sec06-card-f03.front: What text or symbol color and background color appear on work-zone warning signs?
sec06-card-f03.expected_back: Work-zone warning signs use a black legend or symbol on an orange background.

sec06-card-f04.front: Which speed limit governs a work zone when a reduced limit is posted versus when none is posted?
sec06-card-f04.expected_back: Obey a reduced posted work-zone limit. If no reduced limit is posted, obey the road's normal limit while taking extra care for workers, lane position and road conditions.

sec06-card-f05.front: How do work zones distinguish an advisory speed for a specific condition from a mandatory speed-limit drop?
sec06-card-f05.expected_back: An orange advisory-speed sign identifies a suitable speed for a particular work-zone condition; a regulatory reduction is shown by the standard black-and-white speed-limit sign.

sec06-card-f06.front: What legal standing do a work-zone flagger's directions carry?
sec06-card-f06.expected_back: A work-zone flagger has regulatory authority. Follow the flagger's traffic directions.

sec06-card-f07.front: How should you respond to work vehicles displaying flashing or rotating amber warning lights?
sec06-card-f07.expected_back: Yield to work vehicles displaying flashing or rotating amber warning lights, and slow as you approach the work area.

sec06-card-f08.front: How should you create buffer near workers when lanes narrow—if you can change lanes versus if you cannot?
sec06-card-f08.expected_back: When lanes narrow or close near workers, move to another lane if possible. Otherwise create more separation within your own lane without crossing its boundaries.

sec06-card-f09.front: What should you expect from moving maintenance vehicles in a travel lane, and how must you react?
sec06-card-f09.expected_back: Moving work vehicles may travel extremely slowly or stop in the traffic lane. Slow, yield and follow their displayed arrows or directions.

sec06-card-f10.front: What three habits keep you prepared as you enter any highway work zone?
sec06-card-f10.memory_hook: Watch speeds, buffer workers, expect shifts
sec06-card-f10.expected_back: When entering a work zone, watch speed signs, position the vehicle away from workers where possible and prepare for unexpected changes.

sec06-card-f11.front: Where may you enter or leave a controlled-access highway, and what vehicle signs must you watch?
sec06-card-f11.expected_back: Enter or leave a controlled-access road only through an authorized entrance or exit, and obey signs excluding particular vehicle types.

sec06-card-f12.front: Is backing up ever permitted on a controlled-access roadway?
sec06-card-f12.expected_back: Reversing on a controlled-access roadway is prohibited.

sec06-card-f13.front: When must you stay out of a reversible express lane?
sec06-card-f13.expected_back: Do not enter a reversible express lane when its access gates are already closed or are closing.

sec06-card-f14.front: What transmission mistake is prohibited when driving down a hill?
sec06-card-f14.expected_back: When descending a hill, do not coast with the transmission or gears in neutral.

sec06-card-f15.front: Does holding a valid doctor's prescription make it legal to drive while impaired by medication?
sec06-card-f15.expected_back: Driving is unlawful when alcohol, an illegal or prescribed drug, or another substance impairs safe vehicle operation. A prescription does not excuse driving impairment.

sec06-card-f16.front: How does Georgia define reckless driving, and what three behaviors illustrate it?
sec06-card-f16.expected_back: Reckless driving means operating with disregard for the safety of people or property; the handbook gives unsafe speed, weaving and improper passing as examples.

sec06-card-f17.front: Which competitive driving acts count as illegal street racing in Georgia?
sec06-card-f17.expected_back: Street racing includes competing with other vehicles, accelerating or maneuvering to keep a competing driver from passing, or competing against a clock.

sec06-card-f18.front: What intent defines aggressive driving in Georgia, and what on-road acts show it?
sec06-card-f18.expected_back: Aggressive driving involves operating with an intent to harass, intimidate, injure or obstruct another person. Examples include tailgating, cutting someone off and blocking a pass or lane change.

sec06-card-f19.front: Where does Georgia's reckless-stunt-driving law ban drag racing or laying drags?
sec06-card-f19.expected_back: The handbook's reckless-stunt-driving description includes drag racing or laying drags in disregard of safety on a highway or on private property without the owner's express permission.

sec06-card-f20.front: Outside town districts, what spacing must trucks and vehicles pulling trailers maintain behind similar rigs?
sec06-card-f20.expected_back: Outside business and residential districts, trucks and vehicles towing trailers must leave enough space between similar vehicles for an overtaking vehicle to enter safely; closely grouped caravanning is prohibited.

sec06-card-f21.front: What is the maximum trailer width allowed on Georgia highways without special authorization?
sec06-card-f21.expected_back: The handbook prohibits trailers wider than eight feet six inches on Georgia highways.

sec06-card-f22.front: May passengers ride inside a house trailer or any other towed trailer while moving?
sec06-card-f22.expected_back: Passengers may not ride inside a house trailer or another towed trailer while it is moving on a street or highway.

sec06-card-f23.front: Where is it legal to cross the median, barrier, or grass strip of a divided road?
sec06-card-f23.expected_back: Cross a divided-road median, barrier or unpaved separating strip only at an authorized opening or crossover.

sec06-card-f24.front: What worn items affecting your ears or eyes are prohibited while driving?
sec06-card-f24.expected_back: Do not use a headset or another device that impairs hearing while driving, or wear anything that blocks vision.

sec06-card-f25.front: When does carrying passengers or cargo make operating a vehicle unlawful?
sec06-card-f25.expected_back: Do not drive an overloaded vehicle when passengers or freight obstruct the driver's view or interfere with vehicle operation. Passengers must not occupy a position that hinders the view or control.

sec06-card-f26.front: Under what condition may you swing open a vehicle door next to moving traffic?
sec06-card-f26.memory_hook: Only when clear of cars, bikes
sec06-card-f26.expected_back: Open a door beside moving traffic only when safe and without interfering with passing vehicles or bicycles.

sec06-card-f27.front: When may traffic deviate from the posted arrow direction of a one-way street?
sec06-card-f27.expected_back: Follow the posted direction of a one-way road unless a traffic-control device or authorized traffic director directs otherwise; the handbook also recognizes official emergency-vehicle exceptions.

sec06-card-f28.front: How must you warn trailing traffic when slowing down or stopping suddenly?
sec06-card-f28.expected_back: Give the appropriate hand, arm or brake-light signal when slowing or stopping suddenly.

sec06-card-r01.front: In what surroundings and traffic spacing should high-beam headlights be used?
sec06-card-r01.expected_back: Use high beams only in rural surroundings when other vehicles are not nearby.

sec06-card-r02.front: At what exact evening-to-morning window and weather conditions does Georgia require headlights?
sec06-card-r02.expected_back: Headlights are required beginning half an hour after sunset through half an hour before sunrise, whenever it rains, and whenever visibility is limited.

sec06-card-r03.front: Within how many feet must you dim high beams for an oncoming car versus a vehicle you are following?
sec06-card-r03.expected_back: Dim the headlights within five hundred feet of an approaching vehicle and when following another vehicle within two hundred feet.

sec06-card-r04.front: Under which lighting, weather, and sightline conditions must you choose low beams over high beams?
sec06-card-r04.expected_back: Use low beams on illuminated roads, in rain, fog, snow or smoke, and when the visible distance falls below two hundred feet.

sec06-card-r05.front: What three maintenance habits keep your headlights working properly?
sec06-card-r05.expected_back: Keep headlight lenses clean, make sure the lamps work, and periodically have their aim checked.

sec06-card-r06.front: How should your headlight beam reach limit your nighttime driving speed?
sec06-card-r06.expected_back: At night, choose a speed that permits stopping within the road distance your headlights illuminate.

sec06-card-r07.front: When should you slow down at night, and which painted line guides your lane in terrible visibility?
sec06-card-r07.expected_back: Slow at night when approaching a curve or oncoming traffic. With greatly reduced visibility, use the edge line as a lane guide, or the centerline if no edge line is present.

sec06-card-r08.front: What glass care and roadside scanning habits improve safety at night?
sec06-card-r08.expected_back: For night driving, keep the windshield clean and look carefully for signs, pedestrians and vehicles stopped along the road's edge.

sec06-card-r09.front: What two nighttime mistakes—involving fatigue and stopping—must you avoid?
sec06-card-r09.expected_back: Do not continue driving when tired, and do not stop on the roadway at night.

sec06-card-r10.front: Who must wear safety belts in the front seat versus any seat of a passenger vehicle in Georgia?
sec06-card-r10.expected_back: Each front-seat occupant of a passenger vehicle must use the lap-and-shoulder belt. All passenger-vehicle occupants younger than eighteen must use a safety belt wherever seated.

sec06-card-r11.front: What does primary enforcement mean for Georgia's safety-belt law?
sec06-card-r11.expected_back: The handbook describes Georgia's belt law as primary enforcement, allowing an officer to stop and cite a belt violation without first seeing another offense.

sec06-card-r12.front: Which three physical protections does wearing a seat belt properly provide during a crash?
sec06-card-r12.expected_back: Correct belt use helps retain the occupant in the vehicle, distribute crash force over stronger body areas, and prevent contact with the interior or other occupants.

sec06-card-r13.front: Until what age must children ride in an approved height-and-weight-matched child restraint in Georgia?
sec06-card-r13.expected_back: A driver carrying a child younger than eight ordinarily must use an approved child restraint matched to the child's height and weight. The handbook excludes taxis and public transit and notes additional limited exemptions.

sec06-card-r14.front: Beyond phones, what everyday tasks or cabin factors count as dangerous in-car distractions in Georgia?
sec06-card-r14.expected_back: Distracted driving diverts attention from operating the vehicle. The handbook's examples include phone use, reading, eating, grooming, navigation-device use and adjusting audio; passengers and animals can also distract.

sec06-card-r15.front: What broad rule does Georgia's due-care statute enforce behind the wheel?
sec06-card-r15.expected_back: Georgia's described due-care rule prohibits activities that distract from safe vehicle operation.

sec06-card-r16.front: How far back must you stay when following a responding fire truck, and how far when parking near an active fire scene?
sec06-card-r16.memory_hook: Two hundred following, five hundred parked
sec06-card-r16.expected_back: Unless on official business, do not follow a responding fire vehicle or other emergency vehicle closer than two hundred feet, and do not park within five hundred feet of fire apparatus stopped for an alarm.

sec06-card-r17.front: Who does Georgia hold responsible when trash is tossed or dropped out of a motor vehicle?
sec06-card-r17.expected_back: When litter is thrown, dropped or deposited from a motor vehicle, the handbook assigns responsibility to the vehicle's operator.

sec06-card-r18.front: Which land and water areas does Georgia's litter-control prohibition protect?
sec06-card-r18.expected_back: The litter-control prohibition covers discarding waste on public or private property and in the state's waters; discarded materials and rubbish fall within the stated definition.

sec06-card-r19.front: What physical contact with a phone or standalone device does Georgia's Hands-Free Law forbid?
sec06-card-r19.expected_back: The handbook's hands-free rule prohibits holding or supporting a phone or standalone electronic device with any part of the body while operating on a highway.

sec06-card-r20.front: Through which four hands-free setups may Georgia drivers legally use a phone?
sec06-card-r20.expected_back: Under Georgia's Hands-Free Law, drivers may never hold or support a phone for any reason and may use one only through headphones, wireless equipment, a phone holder, or a mounted device.

sec06-card-r21.front: Which text-based electronic activities are illegal while driving under Georgia's Hands-Free Law?
sec06-card-r21.expected_back: The hands-free section prohibits writing, reading or sending text communications, including messages, email and internet data, while driving.

sec06-card-r22.front: What three video-related phone actions does Georgia's Hands-Free Law prohibit while driving?
sec06-card-r22.expected_back: The hands-free section also prohibits watching, recording or broadcasting a movie or video while driving.

sec06-card-r23.front: What is your first choice when approaching a flashing-light postal vehicle or active sanitation truck?
sec06-card-r23.expected_back: Approach a flashing-light postal-service vehicle or a vehicle with active sanitation workers cautiously. Unless an officer directs otherwise, change into a lane not beside it when safety and traffic allow.

sec06-card-r24.front: If you cannot safely change lanes away from a flashing postal or active sanitation vehicle, what speed rule applies?
sec06-card-r24.expected_back: When changing lanes away from a flashing-light postal vehicle or active sanitation vehicle is impossible, unlawful, or unsafe, slow to a reasonable speed for road and traffic conditions that is at least ten miles per hour under the posted limit or twenty-five miles per hour, whichever is higher, and prepare to stop.

sec11-card-f01.front: How should you apply the Georgia manual's safety guidelines when real-world conditions unfold on the road?
sec11-card-f01.expected_back: The handbook's safety guidance consists of general statements; the driver must assess the actual circumstances rather than treat the list as instructions for every possible situation.

sec11-card-f02.front: What tool and vehicle reference point tell you the right air pressure for your tires?
sec11-card-f02.expected_back: Check tire pressure with a gauge against the vehicle's door-label recommendation and adjust pressure to that recommendation.

sec11-card-f03.front: At what two times should you inspect your tires for tread wear and sidewall damage?
sec11-card-f03.expected_back: Inspect tires for wear and damage monthly and before a long trip.

sec11-card-f04.front: Which side should you board from when parked on a street — and what rule applies if you must use the street side?
sec11-card-f04.expected_back: When parked on a street, enter from the curb side if possible. If entry must be from traffic's side, wait until it can be done safely without interfering with passing traffic.

sec11-card-f05.front: How should you carry your keys and walk toward a street-parked car, and what cabin adjustments come before rolling?
sec11-card-f05.expected_back: Have the keys ready, approach while facing traffic, and adjust the seat and mirrors before beginning the trip.

sec11-card-f06.front: Before shifting out of park, what two checks should you run on your passengers?
sec11-card-f06.expected_back: Check that passengers are properly seated without blocking the view, and have everyone fasten the belt before starting.

sec11-card-f07.front: Which road users and hazards must you scan for — and what signal step applies — before pulling into traffic?
sec11-card-f07.expected_back: Before entering traffic, check for hazards, bicycles and pedestrians, signal appropriately and move out cautiously.

sec11-card-f08.front: How does upright driving posture help, and when is taking one hand off the steering wheel acceptable?
sec11-card-f08.expected_back: Good driving posture improves the view and vehicle control. Keep both hands on the wheel except while safely performing another driving task.

sec11-card-f09.front: Which general steering-wheel clock grip does Georgia list, what alternative protects wrists near airbags, and whose advice wins?
sec11-card-f09.expected_back: The handbook gives a general steering grip of left hand at nine and right at three on a clock face, while noting some manufacturers recommend eight and four for airbag-equipped vehicles. Use the vehicle maker's guidance.

sec11-card-f10.front: What is the best trip choice in heavy fog — and what speed and beam rules apply if you must drive?
sec11-card-f10.expected_back: Avoid heavy fog if possible. If driving is necessary, reduce speed and use low beams because high-beam glare makes fog visibility worse.

sec11-card-f11.front: Why should you slow down even further in fog as soon as you spot another vehicle's headlights or taillights?
sec11-card-f11.expected_back: Slow further in fog when another vehicle's headlights or taillights become visible, because its distance can be hard to judge.

sec11-card-f12.front: Which two vehicle light modes does the Georgia manual warn against using while driving through fog?
sec11-card-f12.expected_back: The handbook instructs drivers not to travel through fog with parking lights or hazard flashers on.

sec11-card-f13.front: What separates your tire from the pavement during hydroplaning, and which three controls suffer?
sec11-card-f13.expected_back: Hydroplaning occurs when standing water separates a tire from the roadway, reducing the tire's ability to steer, accelerate or brake.

sec11-card-f14.front: How do you recover once hydroplaning starts, and what two factors help prevent it beforehand?
sec11-card-f14.expected_back: If hydroplaning begins, release the accelerator and let the vehicle slow. Good tire tread and lower speed on water-covered pavement help prevent it.

sec11-card-f15.front: What defines a skid, and what combination of road surface and driver inputs makes one likely?
sec11-card-f15.expected_back: A skid occurs when tire grip is lost. Slick pavement and abrupt steering or braking can make a skid more likely.

sec11-card-f16.front: What sequence of throttle, steering, and light braking brings your car safely out of a skid?
sec11-card-f16.expected_back: When a skid begins, ease off the accelerator, steer in the direction of the skid, and once vehicle control returns, brake lightly and steer toward a safe path.

sec11-card-f17.front: During what opening window of a rainstorm does Georgia warn pavement is especially slick, and why?
sec11-card-f17.expected_back: During the first half hour of rain, water mixing with road oil and other material makes the surface particularly slippery.

sec11-card-f18.front: What do yellow advisory speed signs before a curve tell you compared with the highway's regular posted speed?
sec11-card-f18.expected_back: Curves require extra care, particularly on slick pavement. Advisory curve-speed signs identify a recommended reduction that may be below the regular posted limit.

sec11-card-f19.front: When should you slow for a curve — and how should you recover if you realize mid-curve you entered too fast?
sec11-card-f19.expected_back: Reduce speed before a curve. If already too fast within it, avoid a forceful brake application; release the accelerator, brake carefully and continue steering within the lane.

sec11-card-f20.front: If your wheels run off the pavement edge, what four immediate habits prevent a rollover or spin?
sec11-card-f20.expected_back: If the vehicle leaves the pavement, stay calm, release the accelerator, grip the wheel firmly and avoid sudden hard braking or an immediate sharp return.

sec11-card-f21.front: After drifting off the road, what speed and traffic checks belong before re-entering — including stopping if needed?
sec11-card-f21.expected_back: After leaving the road, let speed decrease, check traffic and choose a safe place to merge back. Stop completely first if necessary.

sec11-card-f22.front: Right when a tire blows out, what must you do with the steering wheel, gas pedal, and brakes?
sec11-card-f22.expected_back: After a sudden tire rupture, hold the wheel firmly and release the accelerator; use light braking only if necessary and safe.

sec11-card-f23.front: How slow should you get after a blowout before steering onto the shoulder — and what if you already swerved off-road?
sec11-card-f23.expected_back: Following a blowout, wait until the vehicle has slowed substantially before moving onto the shoulder. If it has already swerved off the road, let it stop rather than jerking back onto the pavement.

sec11-card-f24.front: Whose instructions must you follow when fitting snow tires or tire chains for winter driving?
sec11-card-f24.expected_back: In winter conditions, use appropriate snow tires or chains only in accordance with the vehicle, tire and chain manufacturers' instructions.

sec11-card-f25.front: How much window glass must be cleared of snow and ice before driving?
sec11-card-f25.expected_back: Remove snow and ice from all vehicle windows before driving.

sec11-card-f26.front: When safe, how can you feel out winter road traction, and how should you handle stops, turns, and gaps?
sec11-card-f26.expected_back: When safe, gently assess winter traction with light braking and small steering adjustments. Avoid abrupt braking, reduce speed gradually before turns or stops and increase following space.

sec11-card-f27.front: Which seven vehicle items — including inside the footwell — should you inspect alongside route and supply prep before winter trips?
sec11-card-f27.expected_back: Before winter travel, check the battery, cooling system, washer fluid, wipers, defrosters, tires and floor mats, and plan the route and necessary supplies.

sec11-card-f28.front: Why can't your senses detect carbon monoxide, and which two garage or mechanical mistakes risk poisoning?
sec11-card-f28.expected_back: Carbon monoxide from a vehicle is colorless, odorless and dangerous. Do not run the engine in a garage or drive with a defective exhaust system.

sec11-card-f29.front: Why shouldn't you sit inside a parked, running vehicle with all windows rolled shut to run heat or AC?
sec11-card-f29.expected_back: Avoid leaving a parked vehicle running with its windows closed, including when using its heater or air conditioning.

sec11-card-f30.front: Why must you never twist the ignition key into the lock position while your vehicle is rolling?
sec11-card-f30.expected_back: Do not turn an ignition into the steering-lock position while moving, because a steering lock can prevent steering.

sec11-card-f31.front: What count does the Georgia manual's reference-point following method use under ordinary conditions?
sec11-card-f31.expected_back: Leave enough following distance to stop safely if the vehicle ahead suddenly slows or stops. The handbook's reference-point method uses a count of about two seconds.

sec11-card-f32.front: In which four lighting, weather, roadwork, or traffic situations must you add space beyond Georgia's ordinary interval?
sec11-card-f32.expected_back: Increase following space beyond the ordinary reference-point interval at night and in bad weather, construction or heavy traffic.

sec11-card-f33.front: Which seven speed, human, mechanical, and wind variables shape stopping distance — making printed charts guides only?
sec11-card-f33.expected_back: Stopping distance depends on speed, the driver's reaction, pavement, tires, chassis, brakes and wind; a chart is only a guide rather than a guarantee.

sec11-card-f34.front: How does higher impact speed affect the force of a collision?
sec11-card-f34.expected_back: Higher impact speed increases collision force.

sec11-card-r01.front: Where are drivers legally allowed to enter and leave a controlled-access expressway?
sec11-card-r01.expected_back: An expressway controls access through designated interchanges; drivers may enter and leave only at those authorized points.

sec11-card-r02.front: What is the job of an expressway acceleration lane, and who holds right-of-way during the merge?
sec11-card-r02.expected_back: The entrance ramp leads to an acceleration lane where a driver adjusts speed before merging safely. Vehicles already on the expressway have priority.

sec11-card-r03.front: How should you position early for an expressway exit, and where should you shed highway speed?
sec11-card-r03.expected_back: Prepare early for an exit by choosing the lane on the exit's side; use the deceleration lane to reduce speed and follow the exit's posted speed.

sec11-card-r04.front: If a short ramp forces you to begin slowing inside a main travel lane before exiting, how must you warn traffic behind?
sec11-card-r04.expected_back: If slowing in a travel lane in preparation for exiting, use the appropriate signal or brake-light indication to warn following drivers.

sec11-card-r05.front: On which side of a divided highway's median must you drive unless signs, controls, or an officer direct otherwise?
sec11-card-r05.expected_back: Keep to the right of a divided highway's median unless signs, a traffic-control device or an officer directs otherwise, and obey its lane striping.

sec11-card-r06.front: What is the painted gore area where an acceleration lane meets a travel lane, and may you drive across its solid white lines?
sec11-card-r06.expected_back: The gore is the marked area where an acceleration lane and a travel lane converge, usually bounded by solid white lines. Do not cross those solid boundaries; continue in the acceleration lane until the solid line ends.

sec11-card-r07.front: What pavement symbol and roadside signage identify high-occupancy-vehicle lanes in Georgia?
sec11-card-r07.expected_back: The handbook identifies HOV lanes with a diamond marking and posted hours of restriction.

sec11-card-r08.front: What three expressway trip points — plus live road updates — should you plan before setting out?
sec11-card-r08.expected_back: Plan expressway entrances, exits and stops before the trip, and check current road-closure and construction information.

sec11-card-r09.front: Why should you check fuel, water, oil, and tires before entering an expressway?
sec11-card-r09.expected_back: Before expressway travel, check fuel, water, oil and tires because opportunities to leave the road are less frequent.

sec11-card-r10.front: How do mirrors and direct head checks work together before an expressway lane change?
sec11-card-r10.expected_back: Use the mirrors to monitor surrounding traffic, and make a direct visual check before changing lanes.

sec11-card-r11.front: What two positioning choices keep you out of another vehicle's blind spot — especially alongside a large truck?
sec11-card-r11.expected_back: Avoid remaining in another driver's blind spot, especially beside a large truck; either stay far enough behind to be visible or complete a safe pass.

sec11-card-r12.front: When must your turn signal start flashing for a lane change?
sec11-card-r12.expected_back: Signal a lane change before starting the movement.

sec11-card-r13.front: What rear check starts an expressway pass, and what visual cue confirms it is safe to return right?
sec11-card-r13.expected_back: Before passing on an expressway, check the left lane behind. Return right only after there is safe separation and the passed vehicle is clearly visible in the rearview mirror.

sec11-card-r14.front: Which two posted speed boundaries must expressway drivers obey?
sec11-card-r14.expected_back: Obey both posted maximum and minimum expressway speeds.

sec11-card-r15.front: Which three habits keep you safe inside dense commuting traffic?
sec11-card-r15.expected_back: In heavy commuting traffic, drive defensively, maintain safe spacing and obey the traffic controls.

sec11-card-r16.front: When is backing up permitted on an expressway?

sec11-card-r17.front: Where should you pull off for routine breaks, and which three non-emergencies never justify stopping on an expressway shoulder?
sec11-card-r17.expected_back: Do not stop on the expressway's traveled roadway. Use rest or service areas; the shoulder is for an actual emergency, not for changing drivers, stretching or collecting an item.

sec11-card-r18.front: If an actual breakdown forces an expressway shoulder stop, what two trouble signals apply and what walking warning holds?
sec11-card-r18.expected_back: If an emergency stop is necessary, the handbook calls for the hood raised and hazard lamps operating to indicate trouble, and warns against walking along the expressway to seek help.

sec11-card-r19.front: What must you do when drowsiness sets in, and why shouldn't you trust caffeine or stimulant products?
sec11-card-r19.expected_back: Stop driving when drowsy. The handbook warns against relying on stimulant products to keep driving.

sec11-card-r20.front: How do you fight monotony on long expressway drives so your awareness stays sharp?
sec11-card-r20.expected_back: Monotony can reduce awareness on long expressway trips. Keep the eyes moving among near and far road areas and continue checking traffic rather than staring at one point.

sec11-card-r21.front: Which three directions around your vehicle must defensive drivers monitor while keeping an escape path in mind?
sec11-card-r21.expected_back: Defensive driving requires monitoring ahead, beside and behind the vehicle and considering an escape path if another driver creates a hazard.

sec11-card-r22.front: Why shouldn't you pull out in front of an approaching car just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec11-card-r22.expected_back: Do not assume another driver will perform the expected action merely because a turn signal is flashing.

sec11-card-r23.front: What two maintenance and driving-volume habits help lower your vehicle's exhaust emissions?
sec11-card-r23.expected_back: Routine maintenance to the manufacturer's instructions and fewer vehicle trips help reduce vehicle emissions.

sec11-card-r24.front: What is the legal status of removing or disabling factory emission-control equipment?
sec11-card-r24.expected_back: Removing or disabling emission-control equipment violates the laws described by the handbook.

sec11-card-r25.front: Which three travel habits cut traffic congestion, and how should you handle idling and engine warm-ups?
sec11-card-r25.expected_back: Combining errands, sharing rides and using transit reduce driving and congestion. Minimize unnecessary idling and follow the manufacturer's warm-up guidance.

sec12-card-f01.front: When must you stop and remain stopped for a pedestrian in a Georgia crosswalk, and how is your half defined?
sec12-card-f01.expected_back: For a pedestrian in a crosswalk, stop and stay stopped when the person is on your half of the road or approaching within one lane of that half. The handbook defines the half as the lanes carrying one direction of traffic.

sec12-card-f02.front: Does a green light, a completed stop sign halt, or a permitted turn excuse you from stopping for crosswalk pedestrians?
sec12-card-f02.expected_back: The crosswalk stopping duty applies during left and right turns, before moving from a stop sign, and even with a green light when pedestrians are still crossing.

sec12-card-f03.front: What must you do for sidewalk pedestrians before pulling onto a street from a driveway, alley, or private road?
sec12-card-f03.expected_back: Stop for a pedestrian before entering the road from an alley, driveway or private road.

sec12-card-f04.front: Which two mobility aids signal that a crossing pedestrian is blind and holds full right-of-way?
sec12-card-f04.expected_back: Give a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog the right of way when crossing the road.

sec12-card-f05.front: Where do legal crosswalks exist even without white paint, and where else can painted crosswalks appear?
sec12-card-f05.expected_back: An intersection crosswalk may exist without painted markings, following the extension of the sidewalk across the street. A marked crosswalk can also be located midblock.

sec12-card-f06.front: Where must your vehicle stop relative to the crosswalk at a red light or stop sign?
sec12-card-f06.expected_back: Do not block a crosswalk; stop before it at a red light or stop sign so pedestrians can cross safely.

sec12-card-f07.front: When a crosswalk has no traffic lights, what pedestrian position triggers your duty to stop?
sec12-card-f07.expected_back: At an unsignalized crosswalk, stop for a pedestrian on your directional half of the road or approaching within one lane of it.

sec12-card-f08.front: At which high-activity zones should you scan both curbs for walkers, and where must you look before backing?
sec12-card-f08.expected_back: Check both roadsides for pedestrians near intersections, turns, schools, parks and bus stops, and look behind for people before backing in a driveway or parking area.

sec12-card-f09.front: What two-direction scan sequence prevents hitting pedestrians during a permitted right turn on red?
sec12-card-f09.expected_back: Before a permitted right turn on red, stop fully before the crosswalk. After checking left for traffic, also check the passenger side for someone crossing ahead.

sec12-card-f10.front: Why is passing a stopped vehicle near a crosswalk on a multilane street so dangerous?
sec12-card-f10.expected_back: A stopped vehicle on a multilane road may hide a pedestrian in a crosswalk. Approach with extreme caution rather than assuming the next lane is clear.

sec12-card-f11.front: How far back from a multilane crosswalk does Georgia recommend stopping so adjacent-lane drivers can spot the pedestrian?
sec12-card-f11.expected_back: When stopping for a crosswalk on a multilane road, the handbook recommends at least ten feet of space before the crossing so drivers in adjacent lanes can see the pedestrian.

sec12-card-f12.front: Where must you stop when pulling into or out of a driveway, alley, or parking garage?
sec12-card-f12.expected_back: Entering or leaving a driveway, alley or parking garage requires stopping before the sidewalk and waiting until pedestrians have passed.

sec12-card-f13.front: Which two conflicts must both be clear before turning left across traffic into a driveway?
sec12-card-f13.expected_back: Before turning left into a driveway, wait for pedestrians crossing its sidewalk portion as well as an opening in oncoming traffic.

sec12-card-f14.front: Why does even a modest rise in vehicle speed sharply worsen the outcome of a pedestrian crash?
sec12-card-f14.expected_back: Pedestrians lack the vehicle occupants' protection, and higher vehicle speed increases the risk of a serious or fatal pedestrian injury.

sec12-card-f15.front: During what hours and across how much of the road network should you expect bicycle traffic?
sec12-card-f15.expected_back: Bicyclists can travel on any road at any hour, so motorists must stay continually alert for bicycle traffic.

sec12-card-f16.front: Which Georgia roadways ban bicycles, and how much lane space may cyclists use everywhere else?
sec12-card-f16.expected_back: The handbook allows bicyclists on Georgia roads other than interstates and similar limited-access highways, and gives them use of a full lane.

sec12-card-f17.front: Must a Georgia bicyclist stay inside an adjacent painted bike lane if one is present?
sec12-card-f17.expected_back: A bicyclist is not required to use an available bicycle lane. Yield to the rider as you would to another driver.

sec12-card-f18.front: What visual connection helps prevent misunderstandings with a bicyclist near an intersection?
sec12-card-f18.expected_back: When possible, establish eye contact with a bicyclist, especially near an intersection.

sec12-card-f19.front: What is Georgia's minimum passing clearance around a bicycle, and why do riders need that lateral space?
sec12-card-f19.expected_back: Allow room for a bicycle rider to avoid potholes or other defects; the handbook states a minimum passing clearance of three feet.

sec12-card-f20.front: When road layout and traffic permit, what is Georgia's preferred lane maneuver for passing a bicyclist?
sec12-card-f20.expected_back: When approaching a bicycle, act cautiously and move to a lane that is not adjacent to the rider when road and traffic conditions make that possible.

sec12-card-f21.front: If you cannot change lanes to pass a bicycle in Georgia, what exact speed reduction and clearance rule must you follow?
sec12-card-f21.expected_back: If changing lanes around a bicycle is impossible, unlawful, or unsafe, reduce speed to a reasonable level at least ten miles per hour below the posted limit or twenty-five miles per hour, whichever is higher, and keep at least three feet between your vehicle and the bicycle throughout the pass.

sec12-card-f22.front: Why might a cyclist make an unexpected lateral move near an intersection?
sec12-card-f22.expected_back: Be ready for a bicycle rider to move unexpectedly, including when traffic has prevented the rider from reaching the usual left-turn position.
