sec12-card-f23.front: How should you use your headlights when meeting an oncoming bicyclist at night?
sec12-card-f23.expected_back: A rider at night may lack lights or reflectors. Dim the vehicle headlights for an oncoming bicycle rider to avoid glare.

sec12-card-f24.front: May motorists use a painted bicycle lane for driving or curbside parking?
sec12-card-f24.expected_back: Do not drive or park in a bicycle lane; that infrastructure is for bicycles.

sec12-card-f25.front: When is a bicyclist allowed to pass motor vehicles on the right side?
sec12-card-f25.expected_back: A bicycle may pass a motor vehicle on the right when there is a dedicated lane or enough shared-lane space and the move is safe.

sec12-card-f26.front: How do bicyclists communicate upcoming turns, slowing down, or stopping to surrounding drivers?
sec12-card-f26.expected_back: Bicyclists use arm signals to indicate a turn, slowing or stopping.

sec12-card-r01.front: How do a motorcyclist's legal traffic status and crash vulnerability compare with car occupants?
sec12-card-r01.expected_back: Motorcyclists share the traffic rights and responsibilities of other drivers but are more physically exposed in a collision.

sec12-card-r02.front: How does a motorcycle's narrow silhouette trick your depth perception, and what two checks counter it?
sec12-card-r02.expected_back: A motorcycle's smaller outline can make it appear farther away or slower than it is. Check again at intersections and check blind spots directly before changing lanes.

sec12-card-r03.front: May a car squeeze alongside a motorcycle within the same traffic lane to pass or ride beside it?
sec12-card-r03.expected_back: Give a motorcycle the full lane; do not share that lane while driving beside or passing it.

sec12-card-r04.front: If a motorcyclist shifts from the left side of their lane to the right side, does that mean they are preparing to turn?
sec12-card-r04.expected_back: A rider may change position within the lane to improve visibility or avoid a hazard. That position change alone does not establish an intention to turn.

sec12-card-r05.front: Which road-surface conditions can force a motorcyclist to slow down or shift lane position without warning?
sec12-card-r05.expected_back: Potholes, gravel, slippery surfaces, seams, rail crossings and grooved pavement may cause a rider to change speed or lane position suddenly.

sec12-card-r06.front: Why must you wait until a signaling motorcyclist visibly begins turning before pulling into their path?
sec12-card-r06.expected_back: Before entering a motorcycle's path, make sure the rider's maneuver has actually begun. A motorcycle's flashing signal may have been left on rather than indicating the next turn.

sec12-card-r07.front: What following time gap does the Georgia handbook recommend behind a motorcycle?
sec12-card-r07.expected_back: The handbook recommends a following interval of three or four seconds behind a motorcycle, with additional space to avoid abrupt braking.

sec12-card-r08.front: How should you handle your speed and steering while a motorcyclist is overtaking you?
sec12-card-r08.expected_back: When a motorcycle passes your vehicle, maintain lane position and speed to let the rider complete the pass and regain a normal lane position.

sec12-card-r09.front: How should you execute a pass around a motorcycle from start to finish?
sec12-card-r09.expected_back: When passing a motorcycle, use a full adjacent lane and leave enough room before returning so the rider is not forced to swerve.

sec12-card-r10.front: When is oncoming traffic excused from stopping for a loading school bus in Georgia—and who must always stop?
sec12-card-r10.expected_back: Traffic approaching a school bus stopped for loading or unloading generally must stop. With a dividing median, opposite-side traffic is excepted, while traffic following or beside the bus in its direction must stop.

sec12-card-r11.front: When may you start driving again after stopping for a school bus?
sec12-card-r11.expected_back: After stopping for a school bus, wait until it resumes moving or deactivates the warnings, and until all passengers loading or unloading have cleared the roadway.

sec12-card-r12.front: Why do large trucks need extra room at corners compared with passenger cars?
sec12-card-r12.expected_back: Large trucks are longer, heavier and harder to maneuver than cars and require additional room for turning.

sec12-card-r13.front: What term does the Georgia handbook use for the large blind areas on all four sides of a truck or bus?
sec12-card-r13.expected_back: The handbook calls a truck or bus's enlarged blind areas the no-zones, including areas beside, behind and in front of it.

sec12-card-r14.front: What four load and hitch checks must you handle before towing a trailer?
sec12-card-r14.expected_back: Before towing, use suitable equipment, stay within the towing capacity, distribute weight appropriately and secure the load.

sec12-card-r15.front: Beyond weight and tie-downs, how should you prepare your vehicles, visibility, and skills before towing?
sec12-card-r15.expected_back: Inspect and maintain both tow vehicle and trailer, become familiar with handling through practice, and consider tow mirrors or other needed safety equipment.

sec12-card-r16.front: What mindset and response advice does the handbook emphasize for safe trailering and handling lost control?
sec12-card-r16.expected_back: The handbook's safe trailering tips advise drivers to take their time and stay calm if they lose control.

sec12-card-r17.front: How can you tell when riding beside a truck or bus whether you are sitting in a side blind spot?
sec12-card-r17.expected_back: A truck or bus has large blind areas on both sides. If its driver's face is not visible in the side mirror, do not assume the driver can see your vehicle.

sec12-card-r18.front: Why is lingering in a truck's or bus's right-side blind spot especially dangerous?
sec12-card-r18.expected_back: The right-side blind area is especially hazardous because large vehicles may need a wide right turn.

sec12-card-r19.front: What double visibility problem happens when you tailgate inside a truck's rear blind spot?
sec12-card-r19.expected_back: Avoid following closely in a large vehicle's rear blind area; you may be unseen and unable to see traffic conditions ahead of it.

sec12-card-r20.front: Why must you never merge close in front of a truck or bus and immediately slow down?
sec12-card-r20.expected_back: Large vehicles need extra stopping room. Do not merge closely in front of a truck or bus and then reduce speed.

sec12-card-r21.front: What visual check in your rearview mirror confirms enough space to return ahead of a truck or bus?
sec12-card-r21.expected_back: Before moving into the lane ahead of a truck or bus, make sure its entire front is visible in your rearview mirror.

sec12-card-r22.front: How should you behave around commercial trucks and buses at highway entrance ramps and merge zones?
sec12-card-r22.expected_back: Give a commercial vehicle ample space during highway entry and merging, and avoid cutting it off, tailgating or speeding around it.

sec13-card-f01.front: When may Georgia DDS pull your driving privileges based on your overall safety pattern?
sec13-card-f01.expected_back: DDS may withdraw driving privileges when evidence establishes that a driver is habitually dangerous or negligent.

sec13-card-f02.front: What triggers a Georgia license cancellation, and what can a resident do once eligible again?
sec13-card-f02.expected_back: Cancellation may follow missing or incorrect application information or later ineligibility. A resident may reapply after meeting the requirements and becoming eligible.

sec13-card-f03.front: How does revocation affect your driving privilege, and how does a Georgia resident return afterward?
sec13-card-f03.expected_back: Revocation terminates driving privileges for the period established by DDS's formal action; a resident may apply for a new license after that period.

sec13-card-f04.front: After a Georgia revocation period ends, what does an out-of-state driver apply to restore?
sec13-card-f04.expected_back: After revocation, a nonresident may apply to have Georgia driving privileges reinstated rather than seeking return of a Georgia resident's license.

sec13-card-f05.front: What does a Georgia license suspension do, and how long does that withdrawal stay active?
sec13-card-f05.expected_back: Suspension temporarily withdraws driving privileges for a specified period or until the reinstatement conditions are met.

sec13-card-f06.front: Once a required suspension period finishes, what may residents versus nonresidents seek to reinstate?
sec13-card-f06.expected_back: After the required suspension period, a resident may seek reinstatement of the license or licensing eligibility; a nonresident may seek reinstatement of Georgia driving privileges.

sec13-card-f07.front: Which convictions do courts send in, and when does DDS update your permanent driving record?
sec13-card-f07.expected_back: Courts report convictions affecting driving privileges or requiring an entry in the permanent driving record; DDS updates the record when a conviction arrives.

sec13-card-f08.front: What does Georgia do when someone licensed or living elsewhere gets convicted here?
sec13-card-f08.expected_back: For a person licensed or residing elsewhere, Georgia forwards conviction information to that jurisdiction's licensing authority.

sec13-card-f09.front: How can a qualifying Georgia conviction affect a nonresident or someone who has no license yet?
sec13-card-f09.expected_back: A qualifying conviction can suspend a nonresident's Georgia driving privilege or an unlicensed person's eligibility to obtain a Georgia license.

sec13-card-f10.front: How does Georgia treat reported traffic convictions that you receive in another state or country?
sec13-card-f10.expected_back: Reported convictions from another state or country can be placed on a Georgia driver's record and treated like Georgia convictions for withdrawal purposes.

sec13-card-f11.front: Which four test-refusal, court-no-show, or unpaid-obligation triggers can withdraw your license without a conviction?
sec13-card-f11.expected_back: A nonconviction withdrawal can arise from refusing required chemical testing, failing to appear or respond to a citation, unpaid child support or an unpaid Super Speeder charge.

sec13-card-f12.front: Besides unpaid obligations or missed court, what three nonconviction actions can withdraw a credential?
sec13-card-f12.expected_back: The handbook also lists safety-responsibility action, medical action and an adult's request to revoke a minor's credential among nonconviction withdrawal grounds.

sec13-card-f13.front: Which five major roadway or criminal convictions trigger mandatory license suspension in Georgia?
sec13-card-f13.expected_back: A conviction for impaired driving, a vehicle-related felony, fleeing an officer, hit-and-run or racing is among the handbook's mandatory-suspension grounds.

sec13-card-f14.front: Which three insurance, registration, or license-status offenses are listed grounds for suspension?
sec13-card-f14.expected_back: Driving without insurance, driving with withdrawn registration, or driving while the license is suspended, revoked or canceled are also listed suspension grounds.

sec13-card-f15.front: Which three crash-harm crimes involving death, an unborn child, or severe injury cause suspension?
sec13-card-f15.expected_back: The handbook lists vehicular homicide, first-degree vehicular feticide and serious injury by vehicle as offenses causing suspension.

sec13-card-f16.front: What penalty may a court impose if you violate a restriction printed on your license?
sec13-card-f16.expected_back: A court may impose suspension for violating a license restriction.

sec13-card-f17.front: Which reckless, school-bus, and blind-passing convictions trigger extra suspension rules under age twenty-one?
sec13-card-f17.expected_back: For a driver younger than twenty-one at conviction, the additional listed suspension offenses include reckless or aggressive driving, unlawfully passing a school bus and improper passing on a hill or curve.

sec13-card-f18.front: How much speeding over the limit—or what point value on a single ticket—suspends a driver under twenty-one?
sec13-card-f18.expected_back: The handbook also lists speeding at least twenty-four miles per hour over the limit or another four-point offense as suspension grounds for a driver younger than twenty-one.

sec13-card-f19.front: How many points within what timeframe will suspend a Georgia driver younger than eighteen?
sec13-card-f19.expected_back: Accumulating at least four points during twelve months before age eighteen is listed as an additional suspension ground.

sec13-card-f20.front: What does Georgia's implied-consent rule cover regarding chemical tests and your driver's license?
sec13-card-f20.expected_back: The implied-consent section describes state chemical testing to determine alcohol or drug impairment and possible license consequences for refusal or a result at the legal limit.

sec13-card-f21.front: When are you entitled to an extra chemical test by qualified personnel of your own choice, and who pays?
sec13-card-f21.expected_back: After submitting to the required state tests, the handbook describes an entitlement to additional chemical testing by qualified personnel chosen by the driver, at the driver's expense.

sec13-card-f22.front: How many serious convictions within what time window trigger a habitual-violator license revocation?
sec13-card-f22.expected_back: A habitual-violator declaration can cause revocation based on a third conviction within five years for a combination of the specified serious offenses.

sec13-card-f23.front: Which major offenses—including stunt driving, racing, fleeing, and impaired driving—count toward habitual-violator status?
sec13-card-f23.expected_back: The habitual-violator list includes impaired driving, vehicular homicide or serious injury, hit-and-run, racing, fleeing, reckless stunt driving, withdrawn-registration operation and a felony using a motor vehicle.

sec13-card-f24.front: What can happen if you refuse a notified DDS reexamination backed by reasonable grounds or cannot drive safely?
sec13-card-f24.expected_back: Refusing a notified reexamination supported by reasonable grounds can cause revocation; the handbook also permits action when evidence establishes that a person cannot drive safely.

sec13-card-r01.front: How do points land on a Georgia driving record, including tickets earned outside the state?
sec13-card-r01.expected_back: Points arise from designated convictions, including out-of-state violations that would carry points if committed in Georgia.

sec13-card-r02.front: What is Georgia's standard point total and month window that triggers a license suspension?
sec13-card-r02.expected_back: The handbook's general points threshold is at least fifteen points accumulated within twenty-four months.

sec13-card-r03.front: How do Georgia's four-point suspension rules differ between drivers under twenty-one and drivers under eighteen?
sec13-card-r03.memory_hook: Single four under twenty-one, accumulated eighteen
sec13-card-r03.expected_back: Georgia suspends the license of any driver younger than twenty-one convicted of a four-point violation, and of any driver younger than eighteen who accumulates four points within twelve months.

sec13-card-r04.front: Which date controls the points-accumulation window, and which date controls single high-point suspensions at ages eighteen to twenty?
sec13-card-r04.expected_back: The violation date determines the handbook's points-accumulation window. For a single high-point offense at ages eighteen through twenty, the conviction date determines the age-based suspension.

sec13-card-r05.front: What happens to your accumulated point total after you serve a points-based suspension?
sec13-card-r05.expected_back: After suspension for accumulated points, the handbook says the points total returns to zero.

sec13-card-r06.front: How is a no-contest plea treated for Georgia's license suspensions applying under age twenty-one?
sec13-card-r06.expected_back: For the handbook's suspensions applying below age twenty-one, a no-contest plea is treated as a conviction.

sec13-card-r07.front: How many points can a licensed Georgia resident ask to remove, and how often is that allowed?
sec13-card-r07.expected_back: A licensed Georgia resident may request removal of up to seven points once every five years under the handbook's points-reduction program.

sec13-card-r08.front: What course length and certificate delivery are required to request Georgia's points reduction?
sec13-card-r08.expected_back: The points-reduction request requires successful completion of a certified six-hour driver-improvement course and the original completion certificate submitted to DDS in person or by mail.

sec13-card-r09.front: When must you complete a certified six-hour course to use Georgia's separate points-avoidance process?
sec13-card-r09.expected_back: The separate points-avoidance process uses a certified six-hour improvement course completed after the citation and before the court appearance, or as the court orders.

sec13-card-r10.front: Where does the original certificate go in a points-avoidance plea, what benefits apply, and how often?
sec13-card-r10.expected_back: For the described points-avoidance plea, the original certificate goes to the court; the handbook describes a twenty-percent fine reduction and no assessed points, with acceptance available once every five years.

sec13-card-r11.front: What can happen to your license if a crash-damage claim goes unsatisfied under the safety-responsibility law?
sec13-card-r11.expected_back: An unsatisfied crash-damage claim under the safety-responsibility law can lead to an order suspending the license.

sec13-card-r12.front: How can your insurer stop a safety-responsibility suspension when you had active liability coverage during the crash?
sec13-card-r12.expected_back: For a safety-responsibility claim, one listed way to avoid suspension is having the insurer file SR-twenty-one showing liability coverage at the time of the crash.

sec13-card-r13.front: What signed document from the claimant can be filed with DDS to answer a safety-responsibility claim?
sec13-card-r13.expected_back: Another listed safety-responsibility response is a general or conditional release signed by the claimant and filed with DDS.

sec13-card-r14.front: If you post security for claimed damages plus financial-responsibility proof, how long does DDS hold that security?
sec13-card-r14.expected_back: The handbook also permits qualifying security for the claimed damages together with the required financial-responsibility filing; DDS holds security for a year and then until the required proof concerning a lawsuit is provided.

sec13-card-r15.front: How many days do you have to request a hearing after receiving a safety-responsibility suspension order?
sec13-card-r15.expected_back: A person receiving the safety-responsibility suspension order may request a hearing within ten days of receiving it.

sec13-card-r16.front: What essential trip purposes can an eligible Georgia limited driving permit authorize?
sec13-card-r16.expected_back: An eligible limited permit restricts driving to approved purposes such as work, scheduled medical care or prescriptions, education, treatment meetings, court or probation duties, community service and specified trips for unlicensed immediate family.

sec13-card-r17.front: How narrowly can DDS tailor a limited permit, and does it ever allow commercial vehicle operation?
sec13-card-r17.expected_back: DDS may further limit a permit by destinations, routes, times or vehicle. A limited permit does not authorize commercial-vehicle operation.

sec13-card-r18.front: What happens if you get convicted of a moving violation or break the rules of your limited permit?
sec13-card-r18.expected_back: A conviction for a moving violation or violation of the permit's own restrictions results in revocation of the limited permit; the handbook also describes extending the underlying suspension.

sec13-card-r19.front: What factors shape limited-permit eligibility, and who makes the final call on issuing one?
sec13-card-r19.expected_back: Eligibility for a limited driving permit depends on the applicable offense, age and conviction record. DDS makes the final eligibility decision; the handbook's examples do not guarantee a permit.

sec02-card-f01.question_text: When does applying for a first Class C instructional permit trigger Georgia's secure-identity paperwork?
sec02-card-f01.teaching_text: Unless you already satisfied secure-identity rules on a prior Georgia ID, your permit trip requires full proof.

sec02-card-f02.question_text: What is the earliest age you can apply for a Georgia Class C instructional permit?
sec02-card-f02.teaching_text: Turning fifteen opens the door to your learner permit so you can log supervised practice hours early.

sec02-card-f03.question_text: Which four personal or status proofs must every Georgia instructional-permit applicant establish or know?
sec02-card-f03.teaching_text: Applicants ineligible for a Social Security number must bring official documentation proving that ineligibility instead.

sec02-card-f04.question_text: What two extra items must a permit applicant under eighteen bring beyond standard identity paperwork?
sec02-card-f04.teaching_text: Minors cannot get a learner permit without verified school attendance and a consenting parent or guardian signature.

sec02-card-f05.question_text: What authority does the adult signer keep over a minor's instructional permit before age eighteen?
sec02-card-f05.teaching_text: Parental consent stays conditional until adulthood, allowing the signing adult to cancel driving privileges for any reason.

sec02-card-f06.question_text: Which two screenings or examinations must you pass to earn a Class C instructional permit?
sec02-card-f06.teaching_text: Before practicing on public roads, every learner must clear the eye check plus both sign and rule questions.

sec02-card-f07.question_text: How much is the testing fee, when is it paid, and what happens if you fail?
sec02-card-f07.teaching_text: Missing either knowledge section forfeits that ten-dollar fee, and retesting requires a fresh payment before starting.

sec02-card-f08.question_text: Who must sit right beside a Class C permit holder whenever the learner drives?
sec02-card-f08.teaching_text: A supervisor in the back seat or impaired by alcohol cannot legally or physically take emergency control.

sec02-card-f09.question_text: At what age and after how long holding a valid permit can most teens seek Class D?
sec02-card-f09.teaching_text: Exam questions love catching teens who stop at one year; Georgia adds one extra day onto that wait.

sec02-card-f10.question_text: What booking and old-permit step must a Class D applicant handle for the road exam?
sec02-card-f10.teaching_text: Show up with a scheduled road appointment and either hand over your learner card or sign an inability affirmation.

sec02-card-f11.question_text: What school, awareness, consent, and testing steps are required when applying for Class D?
sec02-card-f11.teaching_text: Missing your ADAP certificate, enrollment proof, or adult signature stops your provisional upgrade before road testing begins.

sec02-card-f12.question_text: Can the consenting adult cancel a minor's Class D provisional license after it is issued?
sec02-card-f12.teaching_text: Upgrading from a learner permit to Class D does not end the signing adult's revocation power before eighteen.

sec02-card-f13.question_text: Which two educational programs must every sixteen- or seventeen-year-old complete to get Class D?
sec02-card-f13.teaching_text: Waiting until seventeen does not waive Joshua's Law driver education; only turning eighteen skips the Class D tier.

sec02-card-f14.question_text: What classroom and behind-the-wheel options make up an approved Georgia driver-education course?
sec02-card-f14.teaching_text: Teens pair thirty classroom or online hours with either six certified instructor hours or the DDS parent-teen guide.

sec02-card-f15.question_text: How many extra driving hours—including night driving—must Class D applicants certify by affidavit?
sec02-card-f15.teaching_text: Night glare and depth-perception hazards demand at least six after-dark hours inside your forty-hour signed affidavit.

sec02-card-f16.question_text: What extra paperwork is needed at road testing when a certified instructor taught your on-road hours?
sec02-card-f16.teaching_text: Classroom completion alone will not verify behind-the-wheel training when a certified instructor handled the six road hours.

sec02-card-f17.question_text: Can a teen earn Class D without approved driver education, and where is ADAP offered?
sec02-card-f17.teaching_text: Skipping approved driver education blocks Class D completely, while ADAP can be finished at school or online.

sec02-card-f18.question_text: When may an active-duty military parent's teen use an out-of-state driver-education certificate?
sec02-card-f18.teaching_text: Military families relocating to Georgia get credit for out-of-state driver ed timed within nine months of birthday sixteen.

sec02-card-f19.question_text: What permit-holding exemption and license class apply to a seventeen-year-old who documents military enlistment?
sec02-card-f19.teaching_text: Verified military enlistment at seventeen waives the year-and-a-day learner wait and issues a full Class C card.

sec02-card-f20.question_text: During which overnight hours is a Class D driver barred from driving, and what exceptions exist?
sec02-card-f20.teaching_text: Exam questions bait you with work or school excuses, yet Georgia's Class D curfew allows zero exceptions.

sec02-card-f21.question_text: Who may ride as a passenger during the first six months on a Class D license?
sec02-card-f21.teaching_text: Banning non-family peers early cuts fatal teen distraction while new solo drivers build independent street judgment.

sec02-card-f22.question_text: How many non-family passengers under twenty-one may ride during months seven through twelve of Class D?
sec02-card-f22.teaching_text: After half a year of solo driving, Georgia permits at most one non-family peer younger than twenty-one.

sec02-card-f23.question_text: Once a driver holds Class D past twelve months, how many non-family passengers under twenty-one are allowed?
sec02-card-f23.teaching_text: Even experienced Class D teens never get unlimited young friends; non-family riders under twenty-one cap at three.

sec02-card-f24.question_text: What conviction record must a Class D holder keep for twelve months before upgrading to Class C?
sec02-card-f24.teaching_text: Any suspension-mandating major traffic conviction resets your twelve-month clean-record countdown toward an unrestricted Class C license.

sec02-card-r01.question_text: When must an applicant for a first Class C license present REAL ID documentation?
sec02-card-r01.teaching_text: First-time Class C applicants must satisfy federal REAL ID standards unless DDS already verified them earlier.

sec02-card-r02.question_text: When may an eighteen-year-old Class D holder upgrade to Class C?
sec02-card-r02.teaching_text: Hold valid Class D until eighteen or for a year and a day with twelve major-free months.

sec02-card-r03.question_text: What must a qualified U.S. citizen surrender or take when exchanging Class D for Class C?
sec02-card-r03.teaching_text: Qualified citizens simply turn in their Class D card—or affirm inability—without bringing extra paperwork or retaking exams.

sec02-card-r04.question_text: What age, permit step, and exam are required to swap an instructional permit directly for Class C?
sec02-card-r04.teaching_text: Skipping Class D straight from a learner permit requires being eighteen, surrendering that permit, and passing road skills.

sec02-card-r05.question_text: What driving-experience affidavit must an adult sign when upgrading from a permit to Class C?
sec02-card-r05.teaching_text: Turning eighteen skips driver-ed classes, yet permit-to-Class-C applicants still attest to forty supervised hours including six at night.

sec02-card-r06.question_text: How can an unlicensed adult aged eighteen or older earn Class C without holding a Georgia permit first?
sec02-card-r06.teaching_text: Unlicensed adults still must attest to forty supervised hours—six at night—alongside full documents and passing both exams.

sec02-card-r07.question_text: What credential may an adult get first if they want supervised on-road practice before full licensing?
sec02-card-r07.teaching_text: Adults building behind-the-wheel confidence need a Class C learner permit before practicing on public Georgia streets.

sec02-card-r08.question_text: Within how many days of establishing Georgia residency must a non-exempt new resident apply to drive?
sec02-card-r08.teaching_text: Waiting past one month after moving into Georgia leaves your out-of-state driving privilege invalid unless an exemption applies.

sec02-card-r09.question_text: Which licensing track applies when someone moves to Georgia holding no valid out-of-state driving card?
sec02-card-r09.teaching_text: Without a valid out-of-state card to transfer, newcomers start at square one under Georgia's age-appropriate licensing track.

sec02-card-r10.question_text: What three Georgia teen conditions must a transfer applicant under eighteen usually satisfy despite holding another state's card?
sec02-card-r10.teaching_text: Moving in with another state's teen license still triggers Georgia school enrollment, driver education, and ADAP checks.

sec02-card-r11.question_text: What surrender rule and expiration limit govern an adult's out-of-state license transfer?
sec02-card-r11.teaching_text: Once an out-of-state license sits expired for two full years, you lose the straightforward adult transfer shortcut.

sec02-card-r12.question_text: What substitutes if an adult transfer applicant cannot physically surrender their valid out-of-state license?
sec02-card-r12.teaching_text: Lost your prior state's plastic card? Bring an official certified driving record issued within the past thirty days.

sec02-card-r13.question_text: What is the standard transfer age, and when may a seventeen-year-old transfer an equivalent Class C?
sec02-card-r13.teaching_text: Any time, route, purpose, or passenger restriction on a seventeen-year-old's out-of-state license blocks direct Class C transfer.

sec02-card-r14.question_text: Which documents, number, and screening must an adult state-transfer applicant complete at DDS?
sec02-card-r14.teaching_text: Even when written and road tests waive on transfer, DDS still verifies full REAL ID proofs and eyesight.

sec02-card-r15.question_text: In what physical form must transfer identity and lawful-presence records be presented, and are faxes accepted?
sec02-card-r15.teaching_text: Faxed sheets lack security seals, so DDS turns away anything short of an original or certified copy.

sec02-card-r16.question_text: What record does the handbook call for when an applicant's foreign driving credential is missing?
sec02-card-r16.teaching_text: Bring an English-language driving history issued by that country within the last thirty days when the card is missing.

sec02-card-r17.question_text: How do noncitizens and U.S. citizens differ on keeping foreign driving or ID cards after Georgia issuance?
sec02-card-r17.teaching_text: Most noncitizens retain valid home-country credentials for travel, whereas United States citizens must hand foreign cards over.

sec02-card-r18.question_text: How does Georgia generally process a license issued outside the U.S. states and District of Columbia?
sec02-card-r18.teaching_text: Out-of-country cards generally go through full new-issuance exams plus identity, lawful-presence, Social Security, and residence verification.

sec02-card-r19.question_text: Which three tests do foreign-country applicants ordinarily take, and what exception exists?
sec02-card-r19.teaching_text: Expect all three standard exams unless your issuing country sits on DDS's published reciprocity exemption list.

sec02-card-r20.question_text: What extra rules apply when an applicant younger than eighteen transfers from outside the United States?
sec02-card-r20.teaching_text: Coming from abroad under eighteen never bypasses Georgia's teen school, education, ADAP, and supervision requirements.

sec02-card-r21.question_text: What warning does the handbook give about private websites versus Georgia's government licensing portal?
sec02-card-r21.teaching_text: Look-alike third-party websites often charge extra fees for free public forms, whereas Georgia's DDS site is authoritative.

sec03-card-f01.question_text: How is knowledge testing scheduled at DDS centers, and how early before closing must you start?
sec03-card-f01.teaching_text: Arriving fifteen minutes before the doors lock gets you turned away; begin at least thirty minutes early.

sec03-card-f02.question_text: How should an applicant arrange reading or hearing assistance for a DDS examination?
sec03-card-f02.teaching_text: Reaching out to a service center ahead of time sets up an oral exam or hearing interpreter.

sec03-card-f03.question_text: Which DDS test parts may offer non-English options, and which stay strictly English-only?
sec03-card-f03.teaching_text: Even when road-rule questions run in another language, sign recognition and behind-the-wheel testing stay English-only.

sec03-card-f04.question_text: Which personal items and electronics are banned inside the DDS knowledge-testing area?
sec03-card-f04.teaching_text: Carrying scratch paper, pens, phones, or smartwatches into the testing bay counts as prohibited equipment.

sec03-card-f05.question_text: Whom may you speak with during knowledge testing, and what happens if you break testing rules?
sec03-card-f05.teaching_text: Chatting with another applicant or glancing at banned items triggers a misconduct failure on the spot.

sec03-card-f06.question_text: How many questions must you answer right on the Road Signs section, and what does it cover?
sec03-card-f06.teaching_text: Missing more than five of the twenty sign, signal, and marker questions sinks the Road Signs section.

sec03-card-f07.question_text: What score is required separately on the twenty-question Road Rules component, and what does it test?
sec03-card-f07.teaching_text: Acing Road Signs cannot rescue a weak Road Rules score; each twenty-question half demands fifteen right independently.

sec03-card-f08.question_text: Can you walk in for the road-skills driving test, or how must you set it up?
sec03-card-f08.teaching_text: Unlike walk-in knowledge exams, behind-the-wheel skills testing requires booking an appointment ahead through DDS online services.

sec03-card-f09.question_text: May you bring a car with driver-assistance features to your road test, and under what condition?
sec03-card-f09.teaching_text: Backup cameras or lane-keep features cannot carry you; examiners watch whether you control the vehicle yourself.

sec03-card-f10.question_text: Who provides the vehicle for a Class C or Class D road exam, and what wheel count applies?
sec03-card-f10.teaching_text: DDS never loans out exam cars, and three-wheeled autocycles or motorcycles will not qualify for Class C or D.

sec03-card-f11.question_text: When testing with a temporary tag instead of standard plates, what purchase-date limits apply?
sec03-card-f11.teaching_text: Bring your purchase paperwork dated within thirty days from a dealer or seven days from a private seller.

sec03-card-f12.question_text: What coverage, VIN proof, and check must your road-test vehicle clear before pulling out?
sec03-card-f12.teaching_text: Broken brake lights or insurance paperwork missing your car's VIN ends the appointment at the curb.

sec03-card-f13.question_text: What must you demonstrate if your road-test vehicle does not have illuminated turn signals?
sec03-card-f13.teaching_text: Vintage or unlit-indicator vehicles can still test only when the driver executes proper left, right, and stop hand signals.

sec03-card-f14.question_text: Which four contract, driver, and insurance rules apply if you bring a rental car for road testing?
sec03-card-f14.teaching_text: Most standard rentals omit learner names; examiners review the written contract confirming testing permission, your name, and insurance.

sec03-card-f15.question_text: What does DDS do when severe weather or another hazard makes road testing unsafe?
sec03-card-f15.teaching_text: Heavy storms or icy pavement pause behind-the-wheel exams to protect both applicant and examiner, moving appointments to another day.

sec03-card-f16.question_text: What curb distance and box dimensions govern parallel parking on the Georgia road test?
sec03-card-f16.teaching_text: Center your car cleanly between the standards and park no farther than eighteen inches from the curb.

sec03-card-f17.question_text: How far, how fast, and with what head position must you reverse during the backing exercise?
sec03-card-f17.teaching_text: Staring only at a dashboard screen or creeping outside the lane lines costs points; turn your head and reverse straight.

sec03-card-f18.question_text: Where do you stop and how long do you wait for pedestrians at a road-test stop sign or signal?
sec03-card-f18.teaching_text: Rolling onto the crosswalk stripes or edging forward before walkers clear your half of the street deducts points.

sec03-card-f19.question_text: Which maneuver tests your ability to turn the vehicle around inside a confined space?
sec03-card-f19.teaching_text: Smooth steering, full boundary awareness, and brisk observation checks make a confined three-point turn clean and controlled.

sec03-card-f20.question_text: What two mechanical habits are graded if you take your road test in a manual-transmission car?
sec03-card-f20.teaching_text: Lurching gears, riding the clutch pedal, or stalling at intersections shows weak control of a manual transmission.

sec03-card-f21.question_text: How should you position your vehicle and scan when approaching an intersection or corner?
sec03-card-f21.teaching_text: Drifting wide across lanes or looking only one way invites cross-traffic surprises right in front of the examiner.

sec03-card-f22.question_text: To whom must you yield and wait until clear at intersections during your driving test?
sec03-card-f22.teaching_text: Cutting ahead of a cyclist, pedestrian, or driver already entering the box triggers an immediate right-of-way deduction.

sec03-card-f23.question_text: What two steps must happen well before starting a turn on your road test?
sec03-card-f23.teaching_text: Snapping your blinker on mid-turn or diving across lanes at the corner shows late planning.

sec03-card-f24.question_text: What tech gear and passenger are used during Georgia's remotely examined road test?
sec03-card-f24.teaching_text: Remote examiners score through a dual-facing camera and hands-free call while a licensed adult twenty-one or older rides beside you.

sec03-card-f25.question_text: Where does the DDS examiner sit during a traditional in-person road test?
sec03-card-f25.teaching_text: In standard road exams, only the DDS examiner sits beside you in the front passenger seat scoring maneuvers.

sec03-card-f26.question_text: What must you verify before passing another vehicle during the road test?
sec03-card-f26.teaching_text: Pulling out to pass when oncoming or overtaking traffic has to brake for you ruins a road score fast.

sec03-card-f27.question_text: How much following distance must you keep behind the vehicle ahead on your road exam?
sec03-card-f27.teaching_text: Tailgating leaves nowhere to go when the lead driver slams the brakes or makes a sudden unannounced turn.

sec03-card-f28.question_text: What hand, arm, and conversation habits are expected throughout the road test?
sec03-card-f28.teaching_text: One-handed cruising with an elbow propped on the sill or chatty distractions signals casual, unfocused vehicle control.

sec03-card-f29.question_text: What minimum percentage passes the Class C or D road test, and what happens afterward?
sec03-card-f29.teaching_text: Earning at least seventy-five percent passes, and either way the examiner can walk through your score sheet afterward.

sec03-card-f30.question_text: What credential do you walk out with right after passing all exams, and how arrives the permanent card?
sec03-card-f30.teaching_text: DDS issues an interim credential at the counter so you can drive legally until your permanent card arrives by mail.

sec03-card-f31.question_text: How long must you wait to retry a failed Class C or D test part after the first miss versus later misses?
sec03-card-f31.teaching_text: First-time misses let you retest the very next day, whereas a second or later failure locks in a seven-day wait.

sec03-card-r01.question_text: Which away-from-home groups—and household members—qualify for Georgia's renewal-by-mail route?
sec03-card-r01.teaching_text: Active-duty military personnel and full-time out-of-state students—plus spouses and dependents living with them—can renew by mail.

sec03-card-r02.question_text: Which sole Georgia credential can a physically incapacitated person obtain remotely when unable to visit DDS?
sec03-card-r02.teaching_text: Physical incapacity unlocks remote issuance strictly for a state identification card, never a driving license.

sec03-card-r03.question_text: What three items go into a mail-renewal packet, how long is the term, and what follows next?
sec03-card-r03.teaching_text: After one eight-year mail-renewal cycle, your following renewal must happen face-to-face at a DDS center.

sec03-card-r04.question_text: How long expired disqualifies a Georgia license from renewal by mail?
sec03-card-r04.teaching_text: Letting your license stay expired for two years or longer closes off mail renewal and forces full retesting.

sec03-card-r05.question_text: Can you change your legal name or residential address through Georgia's mail-renewal process?
sec03-card-r05.teaching_text: Name or address updates cannot ride along in a mail-renewal envelope; those edits require an in-person DDS visit.

sec03-card-r06.question_text: Does completing a license renewal by mail produce a federal REAL ID card?
sec03-card-r06.teaching_text: Renewing through the mail never issues a REAL ID credential, which matters for federal boarding and facility rules.

sec03-card-r07.question_text: How does Georgia handle a legacy license or ID whose document number is a Social Security number?
sec03-card-r07.teaching_text: To curb identity theft, Georgia swaps any old Social Security license number for a random number upon issuance or renewal.

sec03-card-r08.question_text: Whom should you notify once DDS replaces your old license or ID document number?
sec03-card-r08.teaching_text: Auto insurers and other organizations matching your old license number need the updated random number on file.

sec03-card-r09.question_text: What two channels can replace a lost or stolen Georgia license or ID?
sec03-card-r09.teaching_text: Eligible holders can authenticate identity online from home, or bring identity proof straight into a DDS service center.

sec03-card-r10.question_text: Which single documents can establish identity by themselves when replacing a lost citizen credential?
sec03-card-r10.teaching_text: One primary record—such as a sealed birth certificate, valid U.S. passport, naturalization paper, or expired Georgia card—suffices.

sec03-card-r11.question_text: Which immigration documents qualify as replacement identity proof for a noncitizen at DDS?
sec03-card-r11.teaching_text: Noncitizens present a valid foreign passport with arrival record, permanent-resident card, or qualifying EAD with pending adjustment proof.

sec03-card-r12.question_text: How many secondary records are required under the alternative replacement route, and what examples count?
sec03-card-r12.teaching_text: Lacking a primary ID? Pair two listed records such as a Social Security card, tax return, pay stub, or voter card.

sec03-card-r13.question_text: On the two-document replacement list, can a wallet insurance card stand in for a current insurance policy?
sec03-card-r13.teaching_text: Glove-box ID cards get rejected on the two-document backup route; bring the actual current insurance policy.

sec03-card-r14.question_text: When replacing a card, what is required to get a brand-new document number—and what is the one exception?
sec03-card-r14.teaching_text: DDS assigns a new license number during replacement only with a theft police report or when retiring an SSN.

sec03-card-r15.question_text: Which everyday transactions run through DDS online services, and do REAL ID eligibility rules still apply?
sec03-card-r15.teaching_text: Online tools handle appointments, renewals, replacements, addresses, and status checks, provided you meet underlying REAL ID rules.

sec03-card-r16.question_text: Why can't you rely on postal mail forwarding instead of updating your address directly with DDS?
sec03-card-r16.teaching_text: USPS mail forwarding will not redirect official DDS notices or plastic cards, risking missed suspension alerts.

sec03-card-r17.question_text: How soon after moving must you update your DDS address, and how do in-person versus online checks differ?
sec03-card-r17.teaching_text: Update within sixty days of moving; center visits inspect physical residence documents while online changes verify through postal records.

sec03-card-r18.question_text: Where and within how many days must you update a legal name change, and what fee perk applies?
sec03-card-r18.teaching_text: Legal name changes require a DDS counter visit within sixty days, with one free replacement allowed per license term.

sec03-card-r19.question_text: Which legal records—including one specific Georgia marriage record—prove a legal name change at DDS?
sec03-card-r19.teaching_text: Bring a court order or certified marriage document; Georgia specifically accepts a certified Georgia marriage application too.

sec03-card-r20.question_text: When does a Georgia marriage allow a hyphenated surname on your license?
sec03-card-r20.teaching_text: Georgia marriages from November first, nineteen eighty-two onward support a hyphenated surname when recorded on the certified application.

sec03-card-r21.question_text: Which three time spans are offered when ordering a Georgia driving-history report?
sec03-card-r21.teaching_text: Employers and insurers pick between three-year, seven-year, and full lifetime motor-vehicle history reports depending on review depth.

sec03-card-r22.question_text: Where do you request a noncertified driving history versus an official certified history?
sec03-card-r22.teaching_text: Quick personal checks download noncertified online, whereas courts or state transfers need a certified copy in person or by mail.

sec03-card-r23.question_text: What form and identification are required to pick up another driver's Georgia driving history?
sec03-card-r23.teaching_text: Privacy rules block third-party record pickups without the licensee's signed Form DDS-eighteen naming you plus your own photo ID.

sec03-card-r24.question_text: What may you mail—and which personal details plus payment are required—to order a driving history by mail?
sec03-card-r24.teaching_text: Mail either Form DDS-eighteen or a signed letter listing report span, full name, license number, birth date, mailing address, and fee.

sec05-card-f01.question_text: What must a turning driver do when a green light runs at the same time as a pedestrian walk signal?
sec05-card-f01.teaching_text: Green balls release turning cars and parallel crosswalks together, so wait until walkers clear the lanes you are entering.

sec05-card-f02.question_text: Where do signs or sightlines make turning around with a U-turn illegal?
sec05-card-f02.teaching_text: Turning across both directions near a crest or curve traps your car broadside where oncoming traffic cannot see you.

sec05-card-f03.question_text: What two rules govern turning left across the centerline of a multilane two-way road?
sec05-card-f03.teaching_text: Crossing multiple opposing lanes takes extra seconds, so verify both legal permission and clear gaps across every oncoming lane.

sec05-card-f04.question_text: Which four pedestrian areas must clear before you complete a left turn?
sec05-card-f04.teaching_text: Watching only oncoming bumpers causes drivers to overlook walkers crossing the target street, sidewalk, or driveway apron.

sec05-card-f05.question_text: Is highway parking legal, and what must you aim for if your vehicle breaks down along one?
sec05-card-f05.teaching_text: Getting clear of travel lanes where drivers can spot your car from two hundred feet both ways prevents secondary collisions.

sec05-card-f06.question_text: Which four everyday street and corner locations ban stopping, standing, and parking completely?
sec05-card-f06.teaching_text: Even a quick stop in any of those four spots blocks active lanes or forces pedestrians out into traffic.

sec05-card-f07.question_text: How do safety zones and street excavations restrict stopping, standing, and parking?
sec05-card-f07.teaching_text: Squeezing between a pedestrian safety island and the curb or pinching traffic beside a trench chokes street flow.

sec05-card-f08.question_text: Which four structures, rail corridors, and highway types forbid stopping, standing, and parking?
sec05-card-f08.teaching_text: Shoulderless spans, enclosed bores, live train tracks, and expressways leave zero safe refuge for parked vehicles.

sec05-card-f09.question_text: May you stop, stand, or park inside a divided-highway median, crossover, or signed no-parking zone?
sec05-card-f09.teaching_text: Divided-highway medians and turnarounds belong strictly to emergency responders, never civilian roadside stops.

sec05-card-f10.question_text: What is the only brief stop the Georgia handbook allows directly in front of a driveway?
sec05-card-f10.teaching_text: Parking or leaving an unattended car across a driveway blocks property access, whereas quick active boarding is allowed.

sec05-card-f11.question_text: Within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant, what lone momentary stop does the Georgia handbook allow?
sec05-card-f11.teaching_text: Parking within fifteen feet blocks fire hoses, though an occupied momentary passenger drop-off lets you clear immediately for engines.

sec05-card-f12.question_text: What rule governs the curb space within twenty feet of an intersection crosswalk?
sec05-card-f12.teaching_text: Keeping parked cars twenty feet back preserves corner sightlines while allowing only an instant passenger hop-in or hop-out.

sec05-card-f13.question_text: Within thirty feet of a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal, what brief stop is permitted?
sec05-card-f13.teaching_text: Parked vehicles closer than thirty feet hide intersection controls, leaving only split-second passenger boarding legal.

sec05-card-f14.question_text: Which two distances—same side and across the street—restrict parking at a fire-station driveway to momentary passenger stops?
sec05-card-f14.teaching_text: Ladder trucks swing wide across both curbs when rolling out, requiring twenty feet beside the apron and seventy-five opposite.

sec05-card-f15.question_text: What brief stop is allowed within fifty feet of a railroad crossing or at a no-standing sign?
sec05-card-f15.teaching_text: Leaving a parked vehicle within fifty feet of tracks blocks train sightlines, so only quick active passenger boarding is allowed.

sec05-card-f17.question_text: In a multilane passing lane, what must you do when faster traffic closes in from behind—even if you are driving the limit?
sec05-card-f17.teaching_text: Georgia's passing-lane law applies regardless of your own speedometer reading, preventing left-lane roadblocks and risky right-side passes.

sec05-card-f18.question_text: Which road or weather conditions excuse staying in the left passing lane?
sec05-card-f18.teaching_text: Congestion, storms, or right-lane debris can make holding the left lane safer than squeezing right.

sec05-card-f19.question_text: Which routing, legal, or toll needs allow remaining in a multilane passing lane?
sec05-card-f19.teaching_text: Left-hand exits, upcoming left turns, HOV or toll plazas, and traffic-control signs justify staying left.

sec05-card-f20.question_text: Which two categories of official or work vehicles are exempt from the passing-lane move-right rule?
sec05-card-f20.teaching_text: Emergency responders on duty and highway maintenance rigs frequently work along inner median lanes.

sec05-card-f16.question_text: How do you position your car beside the forward vehicle to begin parallel parking?
sec05-card-f16.teaching_text: Lining up roughly even and two feet out gives your front bumper safe swing room as you angle backward.

sec05-card-f21.question_text: How do you steer at the start of reversing into a parallel space, and when do you straighten the wheels?
sec05-card-f21.teaching_text: Straightening your tires as your front door passes the forward car's rear bumper sets a clean diagonal glide.

sec05-card-f22.question_text: When do you cut the steering wheel sharply left while backing into a parallel space?
sec05-card-f22.teaching_text: Waiting until your front bumper clears their rear corner prevents scraping fenders as your nose swings curbward.

sec05-card-f23.question_text: How do you straighten and center your vehicle once inside a parallel-parking stall?
sec05-card-f23.teaching_text: Pulling forward slightly with right-angled wheels tucks the car parallel to the curb with even bumper gaps.

sec05-card-f24.question_text: At which two moments of parallel parking must you use your turn signal?
sec05-card-f24.teaching_text: Signaling right warns trailing cars before you stop to back in, and signaling left alerts traffic before pulling out.

sec05-card-f25.question_text: How must you check around the car before backing, and where should you look while moving in reverse?
sec05-card-f25.teaching_text: Mirrors leave huge low blind zones behind the trunk, so physically turning over your right shoulder spots children and obstacles.

sec05-card-f26.question_text: What extra precaution should drivers of buses or large vehicles use when backing up?
sec05-card-f26.teaching_text: Box trucks and buses have massive rear blind zones that require a reliable ground spotter directing from outside.

sec05-card-r01.question_text: Which two speed thresholds trigger Georgia's Super Speeder classification upon conviction?
sec05-card-r01.teaching_text: Georgia sets a lower seventy-five threshold on undivided two-lane roads and hits eighty-five or faster on every highway statewide.

sec05-card-r02.question_text: How much is Georgia's state Super Speeder fee, and what happens if you fail to pay on time?
sec05-card-r02.teaching_text: On top of local court fines, missing the state's separate two-hundred-dollar bill suspends your license and adds fifty dollars.

sec05-card-r03.question_text: Unless posted otherwise, what is Georgia's general maximum speed in an urban or residential district?
sec05-card-r03.teaching_text: Driveways, crosswalks, and neighborhood foot traffic cap unposted city and residential streets at thirty miles per hour.

sec05-card-r04.question_text: What default maximum speed applies on an unpaved Georgia county road without speed signs?
sec05-card-r04.teaching_text: Loose gravel and washboard dirt lengthen stopping distances dramatically compared with paved rural highways.

sec05-card-r05.question_text: What is Georgia's general maximum speed limit on a rural interstate highway?
sec05-card-r05.teaching_text: Wide shoulders, grade-separated ramps, and divided lanes support Georgia's top seventy-mile-per-hour rural interstate tier.

sec05-card-r06.question_text: What general maximum speed applies on Georgia urban interstates and multilane divided highways unless posted otherwise?
sec05-card-r06.teaching_text: Heavier ramp density on city interstates and divided corridors drops the unposted cap five miles below rural interstates.

sec05-card-r07.question_text: What general maximum speed limit governs all other Georgia roads when no different limit is posted?
sec05-card-r07.teaching_text: Standard paved two-lane state and county highways default to fifty-five miles per hour outside special districts.

sec05-card-r08.question_text: When must your speed drop down to match a temporary school-zone or construction-zone sign?
sec05-card-r08.teaching_text: Coasting past the first sign while still shedding highway speed earns tickets inside the protected zone.

sec05-card-r09.question_text: When is driving far below normal traffic speed unlawful versus justified?
sec05-card-r09.teaching_text: Crawling needlessly on dry clear roads triggers rear-end hazards unless bad weather or mechanical safety requires slowing.

sec05-card-r10.question_text: Which lane belongs to slower traffic on multi-lane roads, and when must you vacate the passing lane?
sec05-card-r10.teaching_text: Staying right except to pass or turn left prevents rolling bottlenecks when faster traffic approaches behind.

sec05-card-r11.question_text: What should you do if your vehicle cannot maintain a highway's posted minimum speed?
sec05-card-r11.teaching_text: Underpowered vehicles or limping spares belong on lower-speed surface streets rather than high-speed minimum corridors.

sec05-card-r12.question_text: Between what distances from the nearest rail must you stop when crossing warnings or approaching trains require it?
sec05-card-r12.teaching_text: Stopping inside fifteen feet risks gate strikes, while stopping beyond fifty blocks intersections behind you.

sec05-card-r13.question_text: Is driving around, under, or through a lowered railroad crossing gate ever permitted?
sec05-card-r13.teaching_text: Gates drop seconds before fast trains arrive, making any attempt to zig-zag around them deadly and illegal.

sec05-card-r14.question_text: What four conditions must all be true before moving forward after stopping for a train?
sec05-card-r14.teaching_text: Starting out while bells still ring or gates stay down puts you into a second train hidden behind the first.

sec05-card-r15.question_text: How should you use speed, eyes, and ears as you approach and reach railroad tracks?
sec05-card-r15.teaching_text: Checking both ways on approach and looking a second time right before crossing catches fast quiet trains.

sec05-card-r16.question_text: When may you enter a railroad crossing, and how should you drive once safely committed?
sec05-card-r16.teaching_text: Confirming clear space on the far side first lets you roll continuously across without ever pausing on the rails.

sec05-card-r17.question_text: What immediate actions must you take if your car stalls directly on railroad tracks?
sec05-card-r17.teaching_text: Abandon the car immediately, get clear, and call the crossing's emergency-notification sign so dispatchers can halt trains.

sec07-card-f01.question_text: How many stages does Georgia's graduated licensing program use for ages fifteen through eighteen, and what four factors control moving ahead?
sec07-card-f01.teaching_text: Turning older alone never unlocks your next credential if you skip required prep, fail driving skills, or rack up violations.

sec07-card-f02.question_text: Who must appear with an applicant under age eighteen, and what two actions must that person complete?
sec07-card-f02.teaching_text: Showing up solo under eighteen stops your counter visit cold because DDS requires in-person adult verification and a signed affidavit.

sec07-card-f03.question_text: What three qualifications must the responsible adult meet to sign a minor's license or permit application?
sec07-card-f03.teaching_text: Exam questions test that an adult stranger cannot vouch for you just because they meet the minimum age requirement.

sec07-card-f04.question_text: What types of records must a signing parent or guardian bring to prove their relationship to a minor applicant?
sec07-card-f04.teaching_text: Sharing a last name is not enough at the counter without school, military, tax, or identification paperwork linking you.

sec07-card-f05.question_text: When can a social worker sign as a minor's responsible adult, and what proof must they present?
sec07-card-f05.teaching_text: Foster or agency-supported teens can still get licensed promptly when their assigned caseworker brings official employee ID or agency proof.

sec07-card-f06.question_text: Under what documentation condition may a certified driving instructor act on behalf of a minor's parent, guardian, or responsible adult?
sec07-card-f06.teaching_text: An informal note from home gets rejected at testing because proxy authority for an instructor must be formally notarized.

sec07-card-f07.question_text: How can an employee at the shelter where a teen lives qualify to sign as the responsible adult?
sec07-card-f07.teaching_text: Youth living in a shelter are never locked out of licensing if a staff member brings employee ID or shelter verification.

sec07-card-f08.question_text: Besides a parent, social worker, or shelter employee, who else may serve as a minor's responsible adult with proper records?
sec07-card-f08.teaching_text: Blended families and alternative guardianships clear the counter smoothly when backed by acceptable school or government records.

sec07-card-f09.question_text: Which five standard school-enrollment or completion credentials can satisfy a minor's school-evidence requirement?
sec07-card-f09.teaching_text: Graduating early or earning a GED still satisfies teen licensing rules so you do not need an active high-school attendance form.

sec07-card-f10.question_text: What conditions must a college or vocational transcript meet to count as school evidence for a minor?
sec07-card-f10.teaching_text: Opening the envelope yourself or bringing an outdated printout invalidates the transcript before DDS ever checks your name.

sec07-card-f11.question_text: What two additional alternatives can replace a standard school-enrollment certificate for homeschooled teens or GED learners?
sec07-card-f11.teaching_text: Students studying outside traditional high schools stay eligible by bringing official homeschool intent paperwork or active GED program proof.

sec07-card-f12.question_text: At what ages must a teen complete DDS-approved driver education to earn a Class D provisional license?
sec07-card-f12.teaching_text: Waiting until seventeen does not waive Joshua's Law coursework if you want a provisional license before turning eighteen.

sec07-card-f13.question_text: Which permit begins Georgia's graduated licensing program, and what is the minimum age to apply for it?
sec07-card-f13.teaching_text: Starting your permit clock right at fifteen lets you build supervised experience toward the mandatory holding period early.

sec07-card-f14.question_text: What four categories of identity and residency proof are required for a teen's first Class C instructional permit?
sec07-card-f14.teaching_text: Forgetting even one document folder forces a repeat trip before you are allowed near the permit testing terminal.

sec07-card-f15.question_text: Which screening and two-part written exam must a Class C instructional permit applicant pass?
sec07-card-f15.teaching_text: Test questions split road signs and traffic laws into distinct sections, so neglecting either topic costs you your permit.

sec07-card-f16.question_text: What ongoing authority does the adult who signs a minor's instructional permit application hold until the teen turns eighteen?
sec07-card-f16.teaching_text: Your permit remains tied to adult consent throughout minority, giving your signer legal power to pull driving privileges anytime.
sec07-card-f16.must_match_memory_hook: Signing adult can revoke under eighteen

visual_sync.text_span: Signing adult can revoke under eighteen

sec07-card-f17.question_text: Who must sit right beside a Class C instructional permit holder whenever they drive?
sec07-card-f17.teaching_text: Putting an older friend in the back seat or driving with an impaired adult violates supervision law immediately.

sec07-card-r01.question_text: What minimum age and instructional permit holding period apply to an ordinary Class D provisional license application?
sec07-card-r01.teaching_text: Booking your test exactly on the one-year mark is a classic trap because Georgia adds one extra mandatory day.

sec07-card-r02.question_text: What steps, documents, and exam are required to turn an instructional permit into a Class D license?
sec07-card-r02.teaching_text: Arriving without your awareness certificate, school proof, or adult consent cancels your road test right at check-in.

sec07-card-r03.question_text: What classroom and behind-the-wheel components make up an approved Class D driver-education course?
sec07-card-r03.teaching_text: Know both halves of the formula since online theory still must pair with six certified road hours or the parent-teen guide.

sec07-card-r04.question_text: How many supervised practice hours—and how many at night—are required for Class D preparation, and what can serve as the affidavit?
sec07-card-r04.teaching_text: Night glare and depth-perception hazards catch new drivers off guard without at least six logged hours after dark.

sec07-card-r05.question_text: What extra paperwork is required at road testing when a certified instructor provided your on-road course hours?
sec07-card-r05.teaching_text: Your classroom certificate alone will not clear check-in if a separate document is needed to verify instructor-led driving hours.

sec07-card-r06.question_text: When can a teen with an active-duty United States military parent use an out-of-state driver-education certificate in Georgia?
sec07-card-r06.teaching_text: Military transfers happen fast, so check the certificate date carefully against that nine-month window around age sixteen.

sec07-card-r07.question_text: How do licensing rules change for a seventeen-year-old who documents military enlistment and passes the road test?
sec07-card-r07.teaching_text: Verified enlistment waives the year-and-a-day permit wait and skips provisional status straight to a full Class C license.

sec07-card-r08.question_text: During what overnight hours is a Class D driver barred from driving, and what exceptions does the handbook allow?
sec07-card-r08.teaching_text: Exam traps love offering work, school, or church excuses, yet Georgia's Class D curfew allows no exceptions at all.

sec07-card-r09.question_text: Who may ride with a Class D driver during the first six months, and who counts in that group?
sec07-card-r09.teaching_text: Peer distraction spikes teen crash risk early on, so even one friend in the passenger seat breaks first-stage rules.

sec07-card-r10.question_text: How many non-family passengers under twenty-one may ride with a Class D driver in months seven through twelve versus after one year?
sec07-card-r10.teaching_text: Graduated caps add peer passengers slowly because every extra teen voice in the cabin multiplies distraction risk.

sec07-card-r11.question_text: What clean driving-record rule applies during the twelve months before upgrading from Class D to Class C?
sec07-card-r11.teaching_text: Catching a suspension-level major traffic conviction resets your twelve-month clean window before you can move to Class C.

sec07-card-r12.question_text: What rules apply to a teen who moves to Georgia without holding a valid license or permit from another state?
sec07-card-r12.teaching_text: Expired out-of-state paperwork gives you zero shortcut credit, putting you on the same starting line as Georgia teens.

sec07-card-r13.question_text: What happens when a teen moves to Georgia holding a valid out-of-state permit or license?
sec07-card-r13.teaching_text: State teen rules rarely match one-for-one, so DDS reviews any requirement gaps before issuing an equivalent Georgia card.

sec07-card-r14.question_text: How does the adult who signed a minor's application officially request revocation before the teen's eighteenth birthday?
sec07-card-r14.teaching_text: A phone call will not cancel a minor's license because DDS requires its specific revocation form signed before a notary.

sec07-card-r15.question_text: Which specific violations—and what single-offense point threshold—trigger license suspension for a driver younger than twenty-one?
sec07-card-r15.teaching_text: Adults survive a single four-point ticket, whereas any driver under twenty-one loses their license from one four-point conviction.

sec07-card-r16.question_text: Which three specific traffic violations are highlighted as four-or-more-point offenses that suspend a young driver?
sec07-card-r16.teaching_text: Blowing past a stopped school bus or pushing twenty-four over the limit triggers an immediate suspension under twenty-one.

sec07-card-r17.question_text: How many total points within twelve months will suspend the license of a driver younger than eighteen?
sec07-card-r17.teaching_text: Two minor tickets under eighteen can stack up to four points within a year and bench your license fast.

sec07-card-r18.question_text: Who is the only driver eligible for a limited driving permit during a listed non-DUI under-twenty-one suspension?
sec07-card-r18.teaching_text: Drivers under eighteen or caught thirty-four over cannot get a hardship permit to commute during that suspension.

sec07-card-r19.question_text: Is a limited driving permit available during a young driver's first DUI suspension in Georgia?
sec07-card-r19.teaching_text: Expect zero work or school driving relief on an under-twenty-one first DUI suspension because hardship permits are barred.

sec08-card-f01.question_text: Who must obey official road signs and traffic signals, and who is the only authority that can override them?
sec08-card-f01.teaching_text: When an officer or emergency responder waves you past a red signal or sign, human direction overrides fixed controls.

sec08-card-f02.question_text: How many basic sign shapes does the Georgia handbook teach, and why should you read shape and color early?
sec08-card-f02.teaching_text: Glare, rain, or faded lettering can hide words until late, whereas shape and color reveal the rule immediately.

sec08-card-f03.question_text: What kind of message does a tall rectangular road sign normally carry, and how must drivers treat it?
sec08-card-f03.teaching_text: Speed limits and turn rules use vertical rectangles because every instruction on them carries enforceable legal force.

sec08-card-f04.question_text: What type of helpful road information is generally displayed on a wide rectangular sign?
sec08-card-f04.teaching_text: Recognizing horizontal guide boards early lets you set up lane changes smoothly before reaching highway exits or turns.

sec08-card-f05.question_text: What does a diamond-shaped sign warn about, and what are its standard background and marking colors?
sec08-card-f05.teaching_text: Spotting a yellow-and-black diamond down the road cues you to scan early and ease off the accelerator.

sec08-card-f06.question_text: What does an eight-sided sign require, and where must you stop when a stop line or crosswalk is present?
sec08-card-f06.teaching_text: Rolling past the white line or nosing into a crosswalk fails road tests and blocks pedestrian space.

sec08-card-f07.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a stop when a stop-sign approach has neither a stop line nor a crosswalk?
sec08-card-f07.teaching_text: Stopping blind behind hedges or rolling straight into cross lanes invites collisions when pavement lines are absent.

sec08-card-f08.question_text: After making your full stop, who must you wait for before pulling forward into the intersection?
sec08-card-f08.teaching_text: Completing the stop is only step one because pulling out ahead of crossing pedestrians or close cars breaks right-of-way.

sec08-card-f09.question_text: What hazard ahead does a round warning sign announce, and what actions help you check for a train?
sec08-card-f09.teaching_text: Loud cabin audio masks train horns, so easing off speed and cracking a window sharpens your awareness.

sec08-card-f10.question_text: How must you respond to an approaching train at a rail crossing, and what lane maneuver is banned there?
sec08-card-f10.teaching_text: Large trains look slower than they move, and passing on tracks leaves zero escape room if another train approaches.

sec08-card-f11.question_text: What speed and stopping duties apply when you approach a triangular yield sign?
sec08-card-f11.teaching_text: Treating a yield triangle like a free merge causes crashes whenever cross traffic leaves no safe gap.

sec08-card-f12.question_text: Which vehicles have priority over you after you slow or stop at a yield sign?
sec08-card-f12.teaching_text: Cutting in front of cars already in the junction or closing fast on the cross street triggers right-of-way citations.

sec08-card-f14.question_text: How many feet ahead of school grounds or a school crossing is the school warning sign placed?
sec08-card-f14.teaching_text: Knowing that advance distance window warns you that children and crosswalks appear within seconds down the block.

sec08-card-r01.question_text: What do regulatory signs tell road users, and must bicyclists obey them alongside motor-vehicle drivers?
sec08-card-r01.teaching_text: Bicyclists riding on roadways share the exact same legal duty to follow turn bans, lane rules, and regulatory boards.

sec08-card-r02.question_text: What does a red circle with a diagonal slash from upper-left to lower-right mean on a regulatory sign?
sec08-card-r02.teaching_text: Instant symbol recognition stops you from starting an illegal turn or entry before reading any words.

sec08-card-r03.question_text: What dangerous situation does a wrong-way sign warn you about on a one-way road or ramp?
sec08-card-r03.teaching_text: Continuing past a wrong-way alert puts you nose-to-nose against oncoming highway or ramp traffic.

sec08-card-r04.question_text: How does a one-way regulatory sign restrict your direction of travel?
sec08-card-r04.teaching_text: Checking arrow direction before turning onto city streets prevents turning straight into opposing lanes.

sec08-card-r05.question_text: When does a do-not-enter sign apply, and what must you avoid doing at that approach?
sec08-card-r05.teaching_text: Exit ramps and one-way mouths post do-not-enter boards so drivers never steer into head-on traffic.

sec08-card-r06.question_text: What maneuver is outlawed at an intersection posted with a no-U-turn restriction?
sec08-card-r06.teaching_text: Swinging a U-turn where sightlines or tight lanes forbid it blocks multiple lanes and causes broadside crashes.

sec08-card-r07.question_text: What action is barred at an intersection displaying a no-right-turn regulatory sign?
sec08-card-r07.teaching_text: Turning right into a one-way exit or pedestrian-only corridor is a classic way to fail your road exam.

sec08-card-r08.question_text: Which side of a median island or roadway obstruction must you pass when a keep-right sign appears?
sec08-card-r08.teaching_text: Drifting left of a raised divider sends your car directly into oncoming lanes.

sec08-card-r09.question_text: What change on the road ahead does a reduced-speed-ahead warning sign prepare you for?
sec08-card-r09.teaching_text: Easing off the gas before the new limit post prevents sudden braking or entering town zones too fast.

sec08-card-r10.question_text: Where must slower vehicles position themselves on a multi-lane road with a slower-traffic-keep-right sign?
sec08-card-r10.teaching_text: Campers lingering in left lanes bottleneck faster traffic and trigger unsafe right-side passing.

sec08-card-r11.question_text: What does a posted fifty-five-mile-per-hour speed limit sign establish—and what misconception should you avoid?
sec08-card-r11.teaching_text: Posted speed boards set the maximum for that specific stretch under ideal conditions, never a blanket rule everywhere.

sec08-card-r12.question_text: When does the lower speed limit on a flashing school-zone sign take effect?
sec08-card-r12.teaching_text: Ignoring active yellow beacons in a school zone draws steep fines and endangers children near crosswalks.

sec08-card-r13.question_text: May you turn right after stopping at a red light when a no-right-turn-on-red sign is posted?
sec08-card-r13.teaching_text: Stopping cleanly does not unlock a right-on-red turn wherever a regulatory board explicitly bans it.

sec08-card-r14.question_text: What restriction does a bicycle-prohibition regulatory sign place on riders?
sec08-card-r14.teaching_text: High-speed controlled corridors post bicycle bans where narrow shoulders or fast ramps make pedaling unsafe.

sec08-card-r15.question_text: What restriction does a truck-prohibition regulatory sign enforce on the roadway ahead?
sec08-card-r15.teaching_text: Weight limits, tight residential corners, or weak bridges require commercial trucks to stay off restricted streets.

sec09-card-f01.question_text: What two background-and-marking color pairs appear on warning signs, and what do warning signs announce?
sec09-card-f01.teaching_text: High-contrast yellow or bright fluorescent green grabs your eye early enough to slow or steer smoothly.

sec09-card-f02.question_text: What roadway alignment ahead does a successive right-then-left sharp-turn warning sign announce?
sec09-card-f02.teaching_text: Braking before the first corner keeps your tires planted so the quick opposite bend never whips your car wide.

sec09-card-f03.question_text: How do a sharp-right-turn warning and a right-curve warning compare when reading alignment signs?
sec09-card-f03.teaching_text: Test diagrams pair crisp corner arrows against sweeping arcs because a tight turn demands much deeper speed reduction.

sec09-card-f04.question_text: What pattern of road geometry ahead does a winding-road warning sign alert you to?
sec09-card-f04.teaching_text: Multiple consecutive curves cut forward sightlines and forbid passing until the road straightens out.

sec09-card-f05.question_text: What kind of junction ahead can a side-road warning sign identify?
sec09-card-f05.teaching_text: Drivers pulling out from perpendicular or angled side streets can misjudge your speed if trees hide the corner.

sec09-card-f06.question_text: What intersection layout ahead does a four-way crossroad warning sign indicate?
sec09-card-f06.teaching_text: Scanning both left and right approaches early protects you against cross traffic running a rural stop sign.

sec09-card-f07.question_text: How should you adjust your driving when a warning sign shows your road ending at a junction ahead?
sec09-card-f07.teaching_text: Drivers on the through cross street hold priority, so arriving too fast sends you overshooting the T-intersection.
sec09-card-f07.must_match_memory_hook: Slow, yield, turn left or right

visual_sync.text_span: Slow, yield, turn left or right

sec09-card-f08.question_text: Why does a narrow-bridge warning sign call for extra caution as you approach?
sec09-card-f08.teaching_text: Losing shoulder margin on a tight two-lane span leaves little buffer alongside wide trucks or trailers.

sec09-card-f09.question_text: What road-surface feature does a dip warning sign mark, and what action does it call for?
