sec09-card-f09.teaching_text: Hitting a deep pavement hollow at speed can bottom out your suspension or hide standing rainwater.

sec09-card-f10.question_text: What pavement hazard does a bump warning sign identify, and how should you respond?
sec09-card-f10.teaching_text: Striking a sharp ridge too fast jolts steering control and can bounce tires off the pavement.

sec09-card-f11.question_text: What does a soft-shoulder warning tell you about the road edge, and when may you pull onto it?
sec09-card-f11.teaching_text: Dropping right-side wheels onto soft dirt or gravel at highway speed can tug your vehicle toward the ditch.

sec09-card-f12.question_text: What roadway change ahead does a divided-highway-begins warning sign tell you to prepare for?
sec09-card-f12.teaching_text: Staying alert to the median nose keeps you in the right-hand roadway away from oncoming lanes.

sec09-card-f13.question_text: What transition ahead does a divided-highway-ends warning sign prepare drivers to handle?
sec09-card-f13.teaching_text: Forgetting the median has ended tricks drivers into treating an undivided left lane like a passing lane.

sec09-card-f14.question_text: What does a warning sign showing opposing arrows announce when a separated one-way roadway changes?
sec09-card-f14.teaching_text: Moving into your proper right-hand lane immediately prevents drifting into oncoming cars once separation disappears.

sec09-card-f15.question_text: When must you stay out of an underpass marked with a low-clearance warning sign?
sec09-card-f15.teaching_text: Roof racks, tall vans, or stacked cargo above the posted height wedge violently under bridge beams.

sec09-card-f16.question_text: What two steps should you take when you spot a steep-hill warning sign ahead?
sec09-card-f16.teaching_text: Riding the brake pedal down a long grade overheats pads and triggers dangerous brake fade.

sec09-card-f17.question_text: What driving adjustment does a traffic-signal-ahead warning sign call for?
sec09-card-f17.teaching_text: Curves or hills often hide the signal heads until late, so slowing early prevents panic stops on red.

sec09-card-f18.question_text: What hazard does a slippery-when-wet warning highlight, and which rain window does the handbook call most dangerous?
sec09-card-f18.teaching_text: Fresh raindrops lift road oil and dust into a slick film before heavier downpours wash the surface clean.

sec09-card-f19.question_text: What should you prepare to do when a warning sign shows traffic merging from the right?
sec09-card-f19.teaching_text: Adjusting speed or shifting a lane early keeps ramp cars from running out of pavement beside you.

sec09-card-f20.question_text: Which three groups of road crossers can diamond crossing-warning signs alert you to watch for?
sec09-card-f20.teaching_text: Deer paths, pedestrian trails, and equipment crossings create sudden hazards where crossers rarely wait for traffic gaps.

sec09-card-f21.question_text: How do your responsibilities compare at a yield-ahead warning sign versus a stop-ahead warning sign?
sec09-card-f21.teaching_text: Advance diamonds prevent surprise intersections by cueing a conditional stop for yield versus a mandatory stop ahead.

sec09-card-f22.question_text: What must drivers do whenever pedestrians are occupying a crosswalk?
sec09-card-f22.teaching_text: Rolling around walkers who are still in the crosswalk puts them one misstep away from your bumper.

sec09-card-f23.question_text: Which side of the road holds the no-passing-zone warning sign, and where must any pass be finished?
sec09-card-f23.teaching_text: Mounting the yellow pennant on the left keeps it visible even when a tall truck blocks right-shoulder signs.

sec09-card-f24.question_text: What does a small speed plaque mounted beneath a yellow warning sign tell drivers?
sec09-card-f24.teaching_text: Curves and exit ramps post lower recommended speeds calculated for safe tire grip through that specific hazard.

sec09-card-r01.question_text: What two navigation jobs do guide signs perform, and which five sign types belong in that group?
sec09-card-r01.teaching_text: Grouping route shields, exit boards, and distance panels together helps you navigate smoothly without last-second swerves.

sec09-card-r02.question_text: What shape are guide signs usually, and how can companion plaques help you reach a road or facility?
sec09-card-r02.teaching_text: Reading companion arrows or destination words early tells you which lane turns toward your highway or facility.

sec09-card-r03.question_text: What do the numbers printed on highway route shields or exit guide signs represent?
sec09-card-r03.teaching_text: Confusing a highway shield number like eighty-five for a speed limit invites a major speeding citation.

sec09-card-r04.question_text: What upcoming road connection does a junction guide assembly announce?
sec09-card-r04.teaching_text: Advance junction assemblies give you time to check route numbers and move into the proper turn lane.

sec09-card-r05.question_text: How far apart are roadside mileposts spaced, and where does Georgia start numbering them from zero?
sec09-card-r05.teaching_text: Reporting exact milepost numbers brings emergency crews straight to your breakdown spot on rural interstates.

sec09-card-r06.question_text: Below what speed does a vehicle travel when displaying the slow-moving-vehicle emblem?
sec09-card-r06.teaching_text: Closing on farm tractors or maintenance rigs at highway pace shrinks your gap in seconds unless you brake early.

sec09-card-r07.question_text: What does a designated-bicycle-route guide sign tell motorists about the road?
sec09-card-r07.teaching_text: Expect cyclists sharing lanes or shoulders along signed bike corridors and leave generous passing clearance.

sec09-card-r08.question_text: What does a public-parking guide sign direct drivers toward?
sec09-card-r08.teaching_text: Following green parking arrows keeps drivers from circling blocks slowly or stopping illegally in travel lanes.

sec09-card-r09.question_text: What must you do at a white railroad crossbuck, and what does a numbered plaque below it show?
sec09-card-r09.teaching_text: Multiple tracks hide a second oncoming train right behind the caboose of the first passing train.

sec09-card-r10.question_text: What action is mandatory whenever red warning lights are flashing at a railroad crossing?
sec09-card-r10.teaching_text: Driving around gates or rolling through active red rail flashers is both illegal and potentially fatal.

sec09-card-r11.question_text: What background and marking colors identify construction and maintenance warnings, and why are they posted early?
sec09-card-r11.teaching_text: Spotting bright orange diamonds early lets you drop speed before lanes narrow near roadside crews.

sec09-card-r12.question_text: What color combination marks motorist service signs, and what kinds of stops do they point to?
sec09-card-r12.teaching_text: Knowing blue signals hospitals, fuel, food, lodging, or camping saves highway travelers from guessing exits.

sec09-card-r13.question_text: How does a Georgia express lane work, and how is the toll collected?
sec09-card-r13.teaching_text: Never cross solid buffer lines or enter without a registered toll account since express lanes bill electronically.

sec09-card-r14.question_text: How does a reversible express lane operate across the day, and what do signs show while direction switches?
sec09-card-r14.teaching_text: Entering a reversible corridor while overhead boards show closed risks meeting opposing traffic or barrier gates.

sec10-card-f01.question_text: Who must obey Georgia traffic signals — and what sole human authority overrides a lit signal?
sec10-card-f01.teaching_text: A uniformed law-enforcement officer directing traffic in person always outranks steady green or red signal bulbs.

sec10-card-f02.question_text: How must you treat an intersection when its ordinary traffic signal is completely dark and out of power?
sec10-card-f02.teaching_text: Blowing straight through a powerless intersection causes T-bone wrecks because cross traffic expects everyone to stop.

sec10-card-f03.question_text: When a malfunctioning intersection signal switches into flashing mode, how do flashing yellow and flashing red differ?
sec10-card-f03.teaching_text: Drivers facing flashing yellow often forget cross streets have flashing red, whereas flashing-red approaches must halt completely first.

sec10-card-f04.question_text: Where must you stop for a steady red traffic light, and how long must you wait unless a legal turn-on-red applies?
sec10-card-f04.teaching_text: Rolling across the crosswalk line while hunting a sightline blocks pedestrians and triggers red-light violations.

sec10-card-f05.question_text: What transition does a steady yellow traffic light announce, and what response does Georgia require?
sec10-card-f05.teaching_text: Punching the gas to beat a yellow light invites side-impact crashes when cross-street traffic launches on green.

sec10-card-f06.question_text: Before rolling forward on a fresh green light, which two groups inside the intersection still hold priority?
sec10-card-f06.teaching_text: A green bulb permits motion rather than commanding blind entry into lingering left-turners or late crosswalk walkers.

sec10-card-f07.question_text: What movement does a lit green arrow allow, and whom must you still yield to or stop for?
sec10-card-f07.teaching_text: Even with a protected turn arrow, pedestrians finishing in the crosswalk or vehicles clearing the box come first.

sec10-card-f08.question_text: What warning does a yellow arrow send right after a green arrow turns off?
sec10-card-f08.teaching_text: Your protected turning window is closing, so clear the intersection rather than squeezing in behind slow turners.

sec10-card-f09.question_text: Which roadside sign matches a flashing red traffic light, and what three-step sequence must you follow?
sec10-card-f09.teaching_text: Rolling a flashing red light carries the exact same danger and citation risk as rolling past an octagon stop sign.

sec10-card-f10.question_text: How should you approach and pass through an intersection showing a flashing yellow light?
sec10-card-f10.teaching_text: Easing off the gas lets you scan cross-street approaches without stopping dead in a free-flowing lane and getting rear-ended.

sec10-card-f11.question_text: What does a flashing yellow left-turn arrow allow, and what signal faces oncoming traffic?
sec10-card-f11.teaching_text: Never confuse a flashing yellow arrow with a green arrow — oncoming lanes are flowing at full speed on green.

sec10-card-f12.question_text: What action does a steady WALK pedestrian signal authorize?
sec10-card-f12.teaching_text: Even with the walk symbol lit, smart walkers still glance left and right for turning vehicles before stepping out.

sec10-card-f13.question_text: How does a DO NOT WALK signal govern pedestrians still on the curb versus someone already mid-crosswalk when it flashes?
sec10-card-f13.teaching_text: Countdown flashing warns curb-side walkers to hold back while giving people already in the street time to finish.

sec10-card-f14.question_text: Which turning or combined movement restrictions can overhead lane-control signs assign to a specific lane?
sec10-card-f14.teaching_text: Reading overhead lane arrows a block early stops illegal last-second swerves out of turn-only pockets.

sec10-card-f15.question_text: How is a pedestrian hybrid beacon triggered, and what does it do for people on foot?
sec10-card-f15.teaching_text: Midblock hybrid beacons create a signal-protected crossing gap across busy multilane corridors on demand.

sec10-card-f16.question_text: Why shouldn't you treat an unlit pedestrian hybrid beacon like a broken four-way traffic light?
sec10-card-f16.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily beneath a resting, unpushed hybrid beacon risks getting rear-ended — dark is its normal standby state.

sec10-card-f17.question_text: Right after a pedestrian presses the crossing button, what is the very first light a hybrid beacon shows drivers?
sec10-card-f17.teaching_text: That opening flashing yellow wakes approaching drivers up before the solid yellow and red stop phases appear.

sec10-card-f18.question_text: After flashing yellow, what second phase appears on a pedestrian hybrid beacon and what must drivers do?
sec10-card-f18.teaching_text: Just like an intersection yellow, steady yellow on a hybrid beacon tells traffic that red is moments away.

sec10-card-f19.question_text: What driver action is required when a pedestrian hybrid beacon displays two steady red lights?
sec10-card-f19.teaching_text: Side-by-side solid red lenses lock traffic at the stop line while the pedestrian begins crossing.

sec10-card-f20.question_text: During a hybrid beacon's wig-wag alternating flashing-red phase, what must each driver do before rolling?
sec10-card-f20.teaching_text: Once walkers finish clearing the crosswalk, alternating flashing red acts like a stop sign so traffic need not wait needlessly.

sec10-card-f21.question_text: What display does a pedestrian hybrid beacon show once its crossing cycle finishes?
sec10-card-f21.teaching_text: Going completely dark signals that normal free-flowing traffic resumes until another walker presses the button.

sec10-card-r01.question_text: Which three traffic-control jobs do pavement markings share with roadside signs?
sec10-card-r01.teaching_text: Painted lines carry full legal force just like metal post signs — crossing prohibited stripes earns real citations.

sec10-card-r02.question_text: Where must you halt when a white stop line crosses your lane, and roughly where does it sit in urban areas?
sec10-card-r02.teaching_text: Stopping at the painted white bar — usually four feet shy of city crosswalks — keeps your bumper out of pedestrian paths.

sec10-card-r03.question_text: How may white crosswalk lines be painted across pavement, and who holds right-of-way inside them?
sec10-card-r03.teaching_text: Whether marked by twin lines or high-visibility ladder bars, pedestrians inside the crosswalk outrank motor traffic.

sec10-card-r04.question_text: Do marked crosswalks appear only at street corners, and what extra device sometimes accompanies them?
sec10-card-r04.teaching_text: Stay alert between intersections near campuses, parks, and shopping districts where midblock crosswalks and signals cross mid-street.

sec10-card-r05.question_text: What letters and symbol mark a railroad approach on the asphalt, and what passing and stopping rules apply?
sec10-card-r05.teaching_text: Yellow no-passing lines ahead of tracks stop impatient drivers from swinging blind into oncoming lanes or trains.

sec10-card-r06.question_text: What traffic flows does a centerline divide, and what does a single broken yellow line allow on a two-lane road?
sec10-card-r06.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint permits overtaking from either direction only when clear sightlines confirm no oncoming traffic.

sec10-card-r07.question_text: How does a solid yellow stripe on your side of a two-lane centerline — or double solid yellow — restrict passing?
sec10-card-r07.teaching_text: Engineers paint solid yellow where hills, curves, or junctions hide oncoming cars inside passing distance.

sec10-card-r08.question_text: How do dashed double white lane stripes contrast with solid double white lane stripes?
sec10-card-r08.teaching_text: Solid double white lines wall off express or weave zones where lane changes are prohibited.

sec10-card-r09.question_text: What does a solid white right edge line mark at night, and what can a yellow left edge line warn of?
sec10-card-r09.teaching_text: Yellow paint always sits to your left along one-way divided roadways or narrow raised medians.

sec10-card-r10.question_text: Which traffic direction flows on both sides of broken white lane lines?
sec10-card-r10.teaching_text: Remember the core color split — white separates lanes moving together while yellow separates opposing directions.

sec10-card-r11.question_text: On an undivided road with four or more lanes, when is crossing the double solid yellow centerline legal?
sec10-card-r11.teaching_text: Never cross four-lane double yellows to pass — cross only when turning left into or out of an alley, driveway, or street.

sec10-card-r12.question_text: Which lane position should you hold on a multilane road except when overtaking slower same-direction traffic?
sec10-card-r12.teaching_text: Staying right keeps faster left lanes open for smooth overtaking and reduces aggressive weaving.

sec10-card-r13.question_text: What road feature does diagonal yellow pavement striping mark, and on which side of it must you stay?
sec10-card-r13.teaching_text: Painted yellow chevrons or diagonals act like a virtual concrete island — never drive across them.

sec10-card-r14.question_text: What maneuver is a shared center turn lane reserved for, and what is the maximum distance you may travel inside it?
sec10-card-r14.teaching_text: Using the center turn lane as a through-traffic bypass or merging earlier than three hundred feet causes head-on crashes.

sec10-card-r15.question_text: What specific conflict must you scan for right before pulling into a shared two-direction center turn lane?
sec10-card-r15.teaching_text: Traffic from both directions shares that middle pocket, so an oncoming car may merge into the exact same spot.

sec10-card-r16.question_text: How is a bike lane normally marked near the right edge, and where does it sit beside a right-turn-only lane?
sec10-card-r16.teaching_text: Placing the bike lane to the left of a right-turn pocket keeps straight-through riders from getting hooked by right-turning cars.

sec10-card-r17.question_text: May motorists drive or park in a bicycle lane — and what rule governs crossing it for a turn?
sec10-card-r17.teaching_text: Check your right mirror and blind spot to yield to approaching cyclists before merging across their lane to turn.

sec10-card-r18.question_text: In what direction does roundabout traffic circulate, who holds right-of-way at entry, and which way do you turn to exit?
sec10-card-r18.teaching_text: Vehicles already circling counterclockwise around the central island always have priority over approaching traffic.

sec10-card-r19.question_text: What three speed, pedestrian, and gap steps belong as you approach a single-lane roundabout?
sec10-card-r19.teaching_text: Slowing to the yellow advisory plaque lets you stop cleanly for walkers and slip smoothly into a circulating gap.

sec10-card-r20.question_text: Before exiting a roundabout, what signal and pedestrian precautions are required?
sec10-card-r20.teaching_text: Flashing your right turn signal alerts waiting entrants while keeping you ready to stop at the exit crosswalk.

sec10-card-r21.question_text: When must you pick your lane for a multilane roundabout, and what guides your choice?
sec10-card-r21.teaching_text: Checking overhead lane signs and painted approach arrows early locks in your exit path before entering the ring.

sec10-card-r22.question_text: Which lanes must you yield to when entering a multilane roundabout, and may you change lanes inside the circle?
sec10-card-r22.teaching_text: Wait for a gap across both circulating lanes and stay strictly inside your chosen lane all the way out.

sec10-card-r23.question_text: How should pedestrians cross at a roundabout using splitter refuges, and where must they never walk?
sec10-card-r23.teaching_text: Crossing one direction at a time via the raised splitter island beats cutting dangerously across live lanes to the center island.

sec10-card-r24.question_text: How may experienced cyclists ride a roundabout — and how should children or less comfortable riders cross instead?
sec10-card-r24.teaching_text: Confident cyclists claim the lane center so cars do not squeeze beside them, while unsure riders walk the crosswalks.

sec10-card-r25.question_text: Do the roundabout diagrams in the Georgia manual cover every possible roundabout layout you will encounter?
sec10-card-r25.teaching_text: Real-world roundabouts vary in lane count and spiral arrows, so always read the specific signs and paint ahead.

sec14-card-f01.question_text: What is the very first thing you must do immediately after being involved in a crash?
sec14-card-f01.teaching_text: Driving off turns an ordinary collision into a serious crime, so pull to a safe spot right away.

sec14-card-f02.question_text: When must you immediately notify the nearest law-enforcement agency after a Georgia crash?
sec14-card-f02.teaching_text: Modern bumper repairs cross five hundred dollars quickly, meaning most everyday collisions require calling police immediately.

sec14-card-f03.question_text: What duty do you owe to anyone injured after a collision?
sec14-card-f03.teaching_text: Summoning emergency medics and offering sensible aid fulfills your legal and human obligation at the scene.

sec14-card-f04.question_text: When and how should you warn approaching traffic at a crash scene?
sec14-card-f04.teaching_text: Preventing a secondary pileup matters, yet never stand in live lanes where oncoming cars could strike you.

sec14-card-f05.question_text: Which four pieces of information must you both give and collect after a crash?
sec14-card-f05.teaching_text: Collecting all four details on both sides prevents headaches when police reports and insurance claims begin.

sec14-card-f06.question_text: What must you do—and what details belong on a note—if you damage an unattended parked vehicle?
sec14-card-f06.teaching_text: Borrowing a friend's or parent's car means your note needs both your own info and the vehicle owner's name.

sec14-card-f07.question_text: Why shouldn't you assume crash victims are fine just because they say they aren't hurt?
sec14-card-f07.teaching_text: Adrenaline masks internal trauma right after impact, so getting trained medical help early protects everyone involved.

sec14-card-f08.question_text: Why should you avoid moving an injured person unnecessarily at a crash scene?
sec14-card-f08.teaching_text: Lifting or twisting someone with neck or spinal trauma can cause permanent harm before paramedics arrive.

sec14-card-f09.question_text: When must drivers move crash vehicles to a safe refuge after a multilane highway or expressway collision?
sec14-card-f09.teaching_text: Sitting stopped inside fast highway lanes invites deadly rear-end crashes when cars can still steer and brake safely.

sec14-card-f10.question_text: Under what safety condition should you move a crash-involved vehicle out of traffic?
sec14-card-f10.teaching_text: Leaking fuel, locked wheels, or live traffic hazards mean leaving a crippled car put until responders secure the road.

sec14-card-f11.question_text: If you cannot move your drivable vehicle after a crash, who may you ask to move it for you?
sec14-card-f11.teaching_text: Shaken drivers can hand the wheel to a bystander only when that helper holds the right valid license class.

sec14-card-f12.question_text: Does pulling your vehicle to a safe refuge admit fault or cancel your duty to stop and swap details?
sec14-card-f12.teaching_text: Many motorists freeze in traffic fearing blame, yet relocating for safety neither assigns fault nor erases info duties.

sec14-card-f13.question_text: What reporting option do you still keep after moving a crash vehicle out of traffic for safety?
sec14-card-f13.teaching_text: Clearing travel lanes first never takes away your ability to document the collision formally with local police.

sec14-card-r01.question_text: How can a deer standing quietly beside the roadway react when an approaching car startles it?
sec14-card-r01.teaching_text: Expecting wildlife to retreat into the woods backfires when panic sends an animal straight across your hood.

sec14-card-r02.question_text: Where should your eyes continually scan when driving through areas known for deer?
sec14-card-r02.teaching_text: Spotting movement along grassy edges early buys precious braking distance before an animal steps onto pavement.

sec14-card-r03.question_text: Why must you slow down immediately when you spot one deer cross ahead of you or another car?
sec14-card-r03.teaching_text: Herd animals rarely travel solo, so a second or third deer often darts out right behind the leader.

sec14-card-r04.question_text: What two immediate steps should you take if you spot a deer on or beside the road at night?
sec14-card-r04.teaching_text: Blinding high beams freeze an animal right in your lane instead of letting it bound clear.

sec14-card-r05.question_text: What should you do—and avoid doing—when a deer suddenly runs directly into your path?
sec14-card-r05.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel for wildlife launches cars into oncoming lanes, trees, or rollovers far deadlier than braking straight.

sec14-card-r06.question_text: Who should you notify as soon as possible after a collision involving a deer?
sec14-card-r06.teaching_text: Reporting wildlife strikes promptly helps officers clear roadway hazards and documents the damage properly.

sec14-card-r07.question_text: During which two daily time windows should you stay extra alert for deer, while keeping watch all day?
sec14-card-r07.teaching_text: Low light around sunrise and sunset matches peak wildlife movement, though animals can still cross at noon.

sec01-card-f01.question_text: What legal basis allows a Georgia law-enforcement officer to pull over a vehicle?
sec01-card-f01.teaching_text: Officers do not need certainty of guilt before pulling you over when specific facts suggest a traffic or criminal offense.

sec01-card-f02.question_text: Which four actions should you take right away when an officer signals a traffic stop?
sec01-card-f02.teaching_text: Signaling, clearing travel lanes, killing engine and audio, and staying seated sets a calm, predictable start.

sec01-card-f03.question_text: What cabin lighting and hand rules apply during a nighttime traffic stop?
sec01-card-f03.teaching_text: Illuminating a dark interior while keeping hands in plain sight reassures an approaching officer immediately.

sec01-card-f04.question_text: Which side of your car might an officer walk up to, and which window should you lower?
sec01-card-f04.teaching_text: Officers often walk up the passenger curb side to stay clear of fast highway mirrors, so lower that side's glass.

sec01-card-f05.question_text: What must you disclose at first contact during a stop, and when should you reach for papers?
sec01-card-f05.teaching_text: Telling the officer about a weapon before reaching into a glovebox prevents a routine reach from looking threatening.

sec01-card-f06.question_text: When may a stopped motorist ask an officer to show official identification?
sec01-card-f06.teaching_text: Requesting official credentials politely confirms lawful authority whenever standard uniform markings are absent.

sec01-card-f07.question_text: What does an officer typically explain at a stop, and which three items must you have ready?
sec01-card-f07.teaching_text: Storing all three roadside documents together in one spot prevents frantic digging while the officer explains the stop.

sec01-card-f08.question_text: What should you do if your license, registration, or insurance proof sits beyond easy reach?
sec01-card-f08.teaching_text: Narrating where documents sit and waiting for acknowledgment keeps console or backpack reaches calm and transparent.

sec01-card-f09.question_text: How should you position your hands and yourself if an officer instructs you to exit the vehicle?
sec01-card-f09.teaching_text: Standing clear of passing traffic exactly where instructed keeps both you and the officer protected.

sec01-card-f10.question_text: What three outcomes can conclude a traffic stop?
sec01-card-f10.teaching_text: Officers normally state which enforcement step applies before sending you safely back into traffic.

sec01-card-f11.question_text: Where should you challenge a disputed traffic citation instead of arguing on the shoulder?
sec01-card-f11.teaching_text: Roadside shoulders are dangerous places to debate law, whereas traffic court provides a formal hearing.

sec01-card-f12.question_text: Does signing a Georgia traffic citation admit guilt, and what can happen if you refuse to sign?
sec01-card-f12.teaching_text: Classic exam trap: your signature only acknowledges receipt and court details, while refusing can land you under arrest.

sec01-card-f13.question_text: What does the Georgia handbook advise if you have concerns about an officer's conduct?
sec01-card-f13.teaching_text: Completing the stop peacefully first and requesting a supervisor promptly afterward channels complaints constructively.

sec01-card-f14.question_text: Within how many days must a new Georgia resident obtain a Georgia license or permit to drive?
sec01-card-f14.teaching_text: Your out-of-state card stops covering resident driving once thirty days pass after moving to Georgia.

sec01-card-f15.question_text: How does having a permanent home define Georgia residency when someone travels away?
sec01-card-f15.teaching_text: Temporary trips out of state never end Georgia residency so long as your permanent home base stays here.

sec01-card-f16.question_text: Which three work, school, or stay milestones can establish Georgia residency under the handbook?
sec01-card-f16.teaching_text: Taking Georgia employment, enrolling children locally, or staying thirty days triggers the resident license clock.

sec01-card-f17.question_text: When is a federal employee exempt from needing a Georgia license, and what agency caveat applies?
sec01-card-f17.teaching_text: Driving a federally owned rig or official duty qualifies unless the employing federal agency demands state licensure.

sec01-card-f18.question_text: At what minimum age may a nonresident visitor drive in Georgia with a valid home license?
sec01-card-f18.teaching_text: Even with a valid home-state or foreign card in your pocket, Georgia age and road restrictions still govern.

sec01-card-f19.question_text: Who in a nonresident active-duty military household may drive in Georgia using a valid home-state license?
sec01-card-f19.teaching_text: Military families stationed in Georgia keep home-state licensing privileges across the member, spouse, and dependents.

sec01-card-f20.question_text: How long after returning stateside may active-duty personnel drive on a license issued abroad by the armed forces?
sec01-card-f20.teaching_text: That forty-five-day grace window gives returning service members breathing room to secure a state license.

sec01-card-f21.question_text: When is operating a tractor or farm implement on a Georgia highway exempt from driver licensing?
sec01-card-f21.teaching_text: Moving harvest or tillage machinery briefly between fields for farm work needs no regular driver's license.

sec01-card-f22.question_text: When may a military reserve member drive a government-owned or leased vehicle under the licensing exception?
sec01-card-f22.teaching_text: The reserve licensing exemption applies strictly while operating federal vehicles on official drill or reserve duty.

sec01-card-f23.question_text: Who must accompany an applicant during the driving exam to obtain a license?
sec01-card-f23.teaching_text: Unlicensed applicants cannot legally solo to or through testing without a qualified twenty-one-plus adult or examiner.

sec01-card-f24.question_text: Who qualifies for Georgia's migrant-farm-worker licensing exception?
sec01-card-f24.teaching_text: Seasonal workers holding valid home-state licenses stay exempt only while working fewer than ninety calendar-year days.

sec01-card-f25.question_text: How may an unlicensed fifteen-year-old Georgia resident take in-car driving lessons, and what check comes first?
sec01-card-f25.teaching_text: Before an unlicensed fifteen-year-old touches training pedals, the DDS-licensed instructor must screen their eyesight.

sec01-card-f26.question_text: Where does the personal-transportation-vehicle licensing exception apply?
sec01-card-f26.teaching_text: Driving a personal cart outside dedicated PTV paths or designated crossings triggers normal licensing rules.

sec01-card-f27.question_text: What age, license, and translation rules govern the nonresident-student licensing exception?
sec01-card-f27.teaching_text: Foreign-language home licenses must be paired with an International Driving Permit while obeying Georgia restrictions.

sec01-card-f28.question_text: What enrollment and tuition proof must a student carry to use the nonresident licensing exception?
sec01-card-f28.teaching_text: Paying in-state resident tuition disqualifies you from claiming the out-of-state student license exemption.

sec01-card-r01.question_text: Who must accompany an applicant under eighteen to sign the application and adult affidavit?
sec01-card-r01.teaching_text: Minors cannot self-sign Georgia licensing paperwork without a responsible adult completing the sworn affidavit.

sec01-card-r02.question_text: Which two school and safety-course records must every applicant younger than eighteen document?
sec01-card-r02.teaching_text: Showing up at DDS without both your ADAP completion and school-enrollment verification stalls a teen application.

sec01-card-r03.question_text: What education and supervised driving hours are required for Class D at age sixteen or seventeen?
sec01-card-r03.teaching_text: Sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds need approved driver education plus forty supervised hours including six after dark.

sec01-card-r04.question_text: What generally happens to your previous license, permit, or ID during renewal, replacement, or transfer?
sec01-card-r04.teaching_text: Collecting old cards prevents multiple active credentials from circulating at the same time.

sec01-card-r05.question_text: How do foreign-credential retention rules differ between most noncitizens and United States citizens?
sec01-card-r05.teaching_text: While most noncitizens keep home-country cards for travel abroad, United States citizens cannot retain foreign licenses.

sec01-card-r06.question_text: What minimum visual acuity and horizontal field of view are required for initial noncommercial licensing?
sec01-card-r06.teaching_text: Exams love pairing twenty out of sixty in at least one eye with a one-hundred-forty-degree side-to-side field.

sec01-card-r07.question_text: Which form goes to an eye doctor if you fail the DDS vision screen, and what special lenses can it cover?
sec01-card-r07.teaching_text: A licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist completes DS-two hundred seventy-four so DDS can evaluate eligibility or bioptics.

sec01-card-r08.question_text: What happens when you need glasses or contacts to pass vision screening, and what must you disclose later?
sec01-card-r08.teaching_text: Passing with lenses adds a corrective-lens restriction, and you must report lens use at every future DDS transaction.

sec01-card-r09.question_text: What can happen if you change an earlier answer about needing corrective lenses, such as after eye surgery?
sec01-card-r09.teaching_text: Removing or adding a lens restriction triggers a fresh eye check or eye-doctor report to verify safe sight.

sec01-card-r10.question_text: How often must drivers sixty-four and older screen vision versus drivers using bioptic lenses?
sec01-card-r10.teaching_text: Contrast those two timelines carefully: eight-year vision screens at sixty-four-plus versus two-year medical updates for bioptics.

sec01-card-r11.question_text: What is Georgia's standard minimum age for noncommercial Class C, and which seventeen-year-old is exempted?
sec01-card-r11.teaching_text: Georgia teens hold Class D until eighteen unless transferring in at seventeen with an unrestricted equivalent Class C.

sec01-card-r12.question_text: Which ages hold provisional Class D, and what does adding the letter P to a class mean?
sec01-card-r12.teaching_text: Pairing a class letter with P, such as CP, marks an instructional learner's permit rather than a solo license.

sec01-card-r13.question_text: Which payment methods does DDS accept, and which three paper instruments are rejected?
sec01-card-r13.teaching_text: Bringing a personal check, money order, or cashier's check to a DDS counter leaves you unable to pay.

sec01-card-r14.question_text: How much can eligible online DDS transactions save, and is that reflected in printed fee tables?
sec01-card-r14.teaching_text: Completing eligible renewals online shaves five dollars off the standard amounts shown in handbook fee charts.

sec01-card-r15.question_text: How many free name or address updates do you get per license term, and what do later updates cost?
sec01-card-r15.teaching_text: Bundling name and address updates into your single free transaction avoids paying the full renewal fee later.

sec01-card-r16.question_text: What expiration date does a duplicate keep, and what happens inside one hundred fifty days of expiration?
sec01-card-r16.teaching_text: Within one hundred fifty days of expiring, regular-license holders must complete a full renewal instead of a duplicate.

sec01-card-r17.question_text: Can DDS place more than one safety restriction on a driver, and where do restrictions show?
sec01-card-r17.teaching_text: Equipment, daylight, or corrective-lens codes print directly on the license so officers can verify safe compliance.

sec01-card-r18.question_text: What exams and documents are required to renew a Georgia license expired more than two years?
sec01-card-r18.teaching_text: Letting your license sit expired past two years forces vision, road-sign, road-rule, and behind-the-wheel retesting.

sec01-card-r19.question_text: What must you carry whenever driving and present when law enforcement asks?
sec01-card-r19.teaching_text: Driving with your valid card left at home on the dresser still violates Georgia's immediate-possession rule.

sec01-card-r20.question_text: What standard and document examples satisfy REAL ID primary identity evidence?
sec01-card-r20.teaching_text: Photocopies get rejected at the counter; bring an original or certified birth record, passport, or immigration document.

sec01-card-r21.question_text: What Social Security knowledge and Georgia residence paperwork must a REAL ID applicant bring?
sec01-card-r21.teaching_text: Electronic Social Security verification pairs with two recent residential proofs dated within the past six months.

sec01-card-r22.question_text: What must you bring if your current legal name differs from your birth or identity document?
sec01-card-r22.teaching_text: Even when your existing license already shows your married name, REAL ID requires sealed legal linkage records.

sec01-card-r23.question_text: Why isn't a minor's passport enough by itself to prove adult guardianship at DDS?
sec01-card-r23.teaching_text: A child's passport omits parent names, so DDS requires a birth certificate or court guardianship order.

sec01-card-r24.question_text: How often must an applicant relying on immigration records bring original immigration documents to DDS?
sec01-card-r24.teaching_text: DDS re-verifies lawful status on each required license or ID visit, so bring originals every single trip.

sec01-card-r25.question_text: What does the star on a Georgia card mark, and does it guarantee remote service forever?
sec01-card-r25.teaching_text: The corner star confirms federal REAL ID compliance and opens eligible online options without promising every future visit stays remote.

sec04-card-f01.question_text: Who wins when a police officer or firefighter waves you through a red light or stop sign?
sec04-card-f01.teaching_text: Live human traffic directors see emergency scenes and detours firsthand, overriding automated lights and posted panels.

sec04-card-f02.question_text: May you drive past barricades onto a road officially closed for roadwork or a special event?
sec04-card-f02.teaching_text: Closed corridors often have open trenches, live event crowds, or washed-out pavement right around the bend.

sec04-card-f03.question_text: What does right of way identify, and what must you do if someone ignores your priority?
sec04-card-f03.teaching_text: Having legal priority never justifies letting a crash happen when easing off the gas avoids impact.

sec04-card-f04.question_text: How must you handle a stop sign when cross-street traffic does not have a stop?
sec04-card-f04.teaching_text: Unstopped cross-street cars approach at full cruising speed, so wait until nobody is inside or dangerously close.

sec04-card-f05.question_text: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who yields?
sec04-card-f05.teaching_text: Giving priority to the vehicle on your right resolves simultaneous arrivals cleanly on unsigned residential streets.

sec04-card-f06.question_text: How do pedestrians, arrival order, and simultaneous ties work at an all-way stop?
sec04-card-f06.teaching_text: Clear walkers first, let earlier stops roll in turn, and yield right whenever two bumpers halt together.

sec04-card-f07.question_text: How promptly should you move on your turn at a stop sign—and what if someone jumps ahead?
sec04-card-f07.teaching_text: Hesitating confuses waiting approaches, yet racing out to challenge an impatient line-jumper invites a mid-box collision.

sec04-card-f08.question_text: Who must you yield to when turning left at an intersection or into a driveway or alley?
sec04-card-f08.teaching_text: Midblock driveway lefts cross fast oncoming lanes without traffic lights, catching distracted drivers off guard.

sec04-card-f09.question_text: How should you adjust speed and readiness when approaching a yield sign?
sec04-card-f09.teaching_text: Yield triangles demand braking readiness and waiting for a genuine safe opening rather than forcing cross traffic.

sec04-card-f10.question_text: What should merging drivers do, and how should mainline drivers respond where another road joins?
sec04-card-f10.teaching_text: Moving over a lane when clear—or adjusting speed when boxed in—keeps highway entrance zones flowing smoothly.

sec04-card-f11.question_text: What must you do when your signal turns green while traffic conflict still occupies the intersection?
sec04-card-f11.teaching_text: Driving straight into lingering cross traffic just because your light turned green causes avoidable collisions.

sec04-card-f12.question_text: What two steps apply before pulling out of or crossing from a private road or alley?
sec04-card-f12.teaching_text: Stopping before crossing sidewalks and travel lanes protects both hidden walkers and fast street traffic.

sec04-card-f13.question_text: How must you clear the way for an emergency vehicle using lights and siren without creating new hazards?
sec04-card-f13.teaching_text: Stopping clear of intersections on the right shoulder keeps turning room open for big fire apparatus.

sec04-card-f14.question_text: Who receives right-of-way inside a highway construction or maintenance area?
sec04-card-f14.teaching_text: Dump trucks and paving crews maneuver across coned lanes at low speeds and depend on drivers yielding.

sec04-card-f15.question_text: When is turning right at a steady red traffic light legal in Georgia?
sec04-card-f15.teaching_text: Always scan corners beside the signal head for a NO TURN ON RED plaque before rolling forward.

sec04-card-f16.question_text: What three requirements must you satisfy before completing a permitted turn on red?
sec04-card-f16.teaching_text: Treating a red turn like a rolling yield misses pedestrians stepping off the curb right beside your fender.

sec04-card-f17.question_text: Under what exact street and lane setup does Georgia allow a left turn on red?
sec04-card-f17.teaching_text: Turning left on red is legal only from the far-left lane of a one-way onto a left-flowing one-way without a ban sign.

sec04-card-f18.question_text: What do flashing yellow lights on a school bus warn drivers to do?
sec04-card-f18.teaching_text: Amber bus lights precede red flashers and stop arms, signaling that students are already gathering near the curb.

sec04-card-f19.question_text: Who must stop for a school bus flashing red lights with extended stop arms, and when is oncoming traffic exempt?
sec04-card-f19.teaching_text: Georgia's top bus test trap requires oncoming multi-lane traffic to stop too unless an actual physical median divides the road.

sec04-card-f20.question_text: What two options satisfy Georgia's Move Over law when passing covered roadside vehicles?
sec04-card-f20.teaching_text: Vacate the adjacent lane whenever safe, or drop below the posted limit ready to stop if traffic boxes you in.

sec04-card-f21.question_text: Which emergency and service operations receive protection under Georgia's Move Over law?
sec04-card-f21.teaching_text: Georgia extends move-over protection beyond police and tow trucks to active utility and garbage crews using cones or strobes.

sec04-card-r01.question_text: Where may you begin passing on a two-lane road, and how much room must remain ahead?
sec04-card-r01.teaching_text: Starting late in a passing zone strands you across solid yellow stripes or inside an upcoming intersection.

sec04-card-r02.question_text: Before an oncoming vehicle closes within how many feet must you finish a two-lane pass?
sec04-card-r02.teaching_text: Two cars approaching at fifty-five close two hundred feet in barely over a second, leaving zero room for late cut-ins.

sec04-card-r03.question_text: What visual checks must happen before pulling into the left lane to pass?
sec04-card-r03.teaching_text: Pulling out just as a faster car behind you is already overtaking in the left lane causes high-speed sideswipes.

sec04-card-r04.question_text: How do you use your mirrors and turn signals to pull out and return during a pass?
sec04-card-r04.teaching_text: Waiting until the passed vehicle appears in your rearview mirror prevents clipping their front fender on return.

sec04-card-r05.question_text: Which centerline markings and signs prohibit passing on a two-lane road?
sec04-card-r05.teaching_text: Whether solid yellow sits on your side alone, on both sides, or pairs with a sign, overtaking is illegal.

sec04-card-r06.question_text: Within what distance of tracks, bridges, viaducts, or tunnels is two-lane passing prohibited?
sec04-card-r06.teaching_text: Narrow spans, portals, and railroad crossings restrict sightlines and eliminate escape shoulders inside one hundred feet.

sec04-card-r07.question_text: Which four traffic, terrain, surface, or bus situations always ban passing?
sec04-card-r07.teaching_text: Close oncoming cars, blind crests or curves, unpaved shoulders, and stopped school buses make overtaking reckless and illegal.

sec04-card-r08.question_text: When may you cross left of the centerline to steer around a roadway obstruction?
sec04-card-r08.teaching_text: Oncoming drivers own their lane, so wait behind the obstacle until the opposing lane opens completely.

sec04-card-r09.question_text: On a multilane two-way highway, when are you allowed to cross left of the centerline?
sec04-card-r09.teaching_text: With multiple lanes already in your direction, never cross yellow center stripes to overtake—only for signed controls or left access turns.

sec04-card-r10.question_text: In which two roadway situations does Georgia allow passing another vehicle on the right?
sec04-card-r10.teaching_text: Only full pavement width beside a left-turning car or two-plus lanes going your way makes right-side overtaking legal.

sec04-card-r11.question_text: How should you manage your speed while another vehicle is overtaking you?
sec04-card-r11.teaching_text: Easing off the gas slightly shortens side-by-side exposure and gets the passing car safely back in line.

sec04-card-r12.question_text: May you overtake a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian at a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
sec04-card-r12.teaching_text: A stopped car in the next lane blocks your view of the exact person walking across into your path.

sec04-card-r13.question_text: How far back should you stop for someone in a crosswalk?
sec04-card-r13.teaching_text: Stopping a couple car lengths back lets drivers in adjacent lanes spot the pedestrian early instead of screening them.

sec04-card-r14.question_text: How should you approach an intersection when cars in neighboring lanes stay stopped despite a green light?
sec04-card-r14.teaching_text: Stopped vehicles on green usually mean a slow walker or child is still crossing out of sight ahead of their hoods.

sec04-card-r15.question_text: What is Georgia's preferred way to overtake a bicycle when road and traffic conditions allow?
sec04-card-r15.teaching_text: Changing completely into the next lane gives cyclists maximum buffer from mirror overhang and wind gusts.

sec04-card-r16.question_text: If you cannot change lanes to pass a bicycle in Georgia, what speed and clearance rules apply?
sec04-card-r16.teaching_text: Slowing at least ten under the limit—or to twenty-five, whichever is higher—while keeping three feet protects riders in tight lanes.

sec04-card-r17.question_text: How much of a traffic lane belongs to a motorcyclist, and how must you pass one?
sec04-card-r17.teaching_text: Riders shift across their full lane to dodge potholes and oil slicks, making side-by-side lane squeezing illegal and dangerous.

sec04-card-r18.question_text: How does Georgia law distinguish unlawful lane weaving from lawful highway passing?
sec04-card-r18.teaching_text: Darting across gaps just to outrun traffic creates chain-reaction braking, whereas signaled lane changes keep flow predictable.

sec04-card-r19.question_text: How early and steadily must you signal before making a left or right turn?
sec04-card-r19.teaching_text: Flicking a blinker mid-brake gives trailing drivers zero time to back off your rear bumper.

sec04-card-r20.question_text: Should you ever flash your turn signal to tell a driver behind you that passing is clear?
sec04-card-r20.teaching_text: Trailing drivers could mistake your blinker for a turn intention or pull into an oncoming car you missed.

sec04-card-r21.question_text: How should you position for a right turn, and who has priority in a curbside bicycle lane?
sec04-card-r21.teaching_text: Cutting a right hook across a straight-through cyclist in the bike lane is one of the most common urban bike crashes.

sec04-card-r22.question_text: Which lane must you finish a single-lane or multi-lane right turn inside?
sec04-card-r22.teaching_text: Tracking tight into your matching receiving lane prevents drifting wide into adjacent turning or oncoming cars.

sec04-card-r23.question_text: From which lane do you start a left turn, and how must your wheels point while waiting?
sec04-card-r23.teaching_text: Keeping front tires straight until you actually turn prevents a rear-end bump from shoving you into oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-r24.question_text: Which road users must you yield to before starting a left turn?
sec04-card-r24.teaching_text: Oncoming bicycles move faster than they look and blend against car headlights, requiring a dedicated second glance.

sec04-card-r25.question_text: Which receiving lane should you enter when completing a single-lane or multi-lane left turn?
sec04-card-r25.teaching_text: Finishing in the innermost lane leaves outer curb lanes open for opposing drivers legally turning right.

sec04-card-r26.question_text: May you switch lanes inside the intersection after starting a left turn?
sec04-card-r26.teaching_text: Changing lanes mid-arc cuts across neighboring turners or right-on-red entrants who expect you to hold your line.

sec04-card-r27.question_text: How long must you remain stopped when turning into a street where pedestrians are in the crosswalk?
sec04-card-r27.teaching_text: Inching right behind a pedestrian's heels pressures them and risks contact if someone trips or drops something.

sec06-card-f01.question_text: What roadway areas and rolling operations can a Georgia work zone cover?
sec06-card-f01.teaching_text: Work zones extend beyond fixed orange barrels to include slow-moving utility repairs, surveying, and snowplows.

sec06-card-f02.question_text: Which three guides direct traffic through roadwork or detours, and which background color warns of work?
sec06-card-f02.teaching_text: Spotting bright orange ahead tells you immediately that temporary signs, lines, or flaggers take over.

sec06-card-f03.question_text: What text or symbol color and background color appear on work-zone warning signs?
sec06-card-f03.teaching_text: Bold black icons against fluorescent orange cut through highway dust, sun glare, and twilight.

sec06-card-f04.question_text: Which speed limit governs a work zone when a reduced limit is posted versus when none is posted?
sec06-card-f04.teaching_text: Even when no special lower plaque appears, narrowed lanes and exposed workers still demand extra care inside normal limits.

sec06-card-f05.question_text: How do work zones distinguish an advisory speed for a specific condition from a mandatory speed-limit drop?
sec06-card-f05.teaching_text: Orange speed plaques recommend safe speeds for tight shifts, while standard black-and-white signs set the enforceable legal maximum.

sec06-card-f06.question_text: What legal standing do a work-zone flagger's directions carry?
sec06-card-f06.teaching_text: Disobeying a construction flagger carries the same legal weight as blowing a regulatory traffic signal.

sec06-card-f07.question_text: How should you respond to work vehicles displaying flashing or rotating amber warning lights?
sec06-card-f07.teaching_text: Heavy work trucks merge into and out of coned tapers far slower than passenger traffic.

sec06-card-f08.question_text: How should you create buffer near workers when lanes narrow—if you can change lanes versus if you cannot?
sec06-card-f08.teaching_text: If neighboring traffic blocks a full lane change, edging slightly away within your own lane lines still widens worker clearance.

sec06-card-f09.question_text: What should you expect from moving maintenance vehicles in a travel lane, and how must you react?
sec06-card-f09.teaching_text: Striping and pothole trucks crawl or halt right in live lanes, so slow early and obey their lighted arrow boards.

sec06-card-f10.question_text: What three habits keep you prepared as you enter any highway work zone?
sec06-card-f10.teaching_text: Temporary lane tapers, sudden brake waves, and equipment entries happen without warning inside active roadwork.
sec06-card-f10.must_match_memory_hook: Watch speeds, buffer workers, expect shifts

visual_sync.text_span: Watch speeds, buffer workers, expect shifts

sec06-card-f11.question_text: Where may you enter or leave a controlled-access highway, and what vehicle signs must you watch?
sec06-card-f11.teaching_text: Controlled-access corridors ban shoulder cutoffs and sometimes bar mopeds, bicycles, or oversized loads by sign.

sec06-card-f12.question_text: Is backing up ever permitted on a controlled-access roadway?
sec06-card-f12.teaching_text: Reversing toward sixty-five-mile-per-hour traffic after missing an exit creates devastating closing speeds.

sec06-card-f13.question_text: When must you stay out of a reversible express lane?
sec06-card-f13.teaching_text: Reversible barrier gates shut when express lanes flip direction toward oncoming rush-hour traffic.

sec06-card-f14.question_text: What transmission mistake is prohibited when driving down a hill?
sec06-card-f14.teaching_text: Shifting into neutral eliminates engine braking, overheating wheel brakes and delaying emergency throttle response.

sec06-card-f15.question_text: Does holding a valid doctor's prescription make it legal to drive while impaired by medication?
sec06-card-f15.teaching_text: Georgia DUI law targets impaired driving ability itself, whether caused by alcohol, street drugs, or legal prescriptions.

sec06-card-f16.question_text: How does Georgia define reckless driving, and what three behaviors illustrate it?
sec06-card-f16.teaching_text: Operating without regard for people or property escalates ordinary traffic errors into a serious criminal offense.

sec06-card-f17.question_text: Which competitive driving acts count as illegal street racing in Georgia?
sec06-card-f17.teaching_text: Racing solo against a stopwatch or swerving to block a rival's pass counts as street racing alongside side-by-side drags.

sec06-card-f18.question_text: What intent defines aggressive driving in Georgia, and what on-road acts show it?
sec06-card-f18.teaching_text: Tailgating, cutting someone off, or intentionally blocking lane changes crosses into targeted harassment behind the wheel.

sec06-card-f19.question_text: Where does Georgia's reckless-stunt-driving law ban drag racing or laying drags?
sec06-card-f19.teaching_text: Spinning donuts or laying drags in a shopping-center parking lot without the owner's express permission is just as illegal as on highways.

sec06-card-f20.question_text: Outside town districts, what spacing must trucks and vehicles pulling trailers maintain behind similar rigs?
sec06-card-f20.teaching_text: Bumper-to-bumper trailer convoys force overtaking cars to clear two long rigs in a single dangerous pass.

sec06-card-f21.question_text: What is the maximum trailer width allowed on Georgia highways without special authorization?
sec06-card-f21.teaching_text: Standard highway lanes measure ten to twelve feet across, capping ordinary trailers at eight feet six inches.

sec06-card-f22.question_text: May passengers ride inside a house trailer or any other towed trailer while moving?
sec06-card-f22.teaching_text: Towed trailers have no crash-tested seat belts or airbags and break apart violently in highway collisions.

sec06-card-f23.question_text: Where is it legal to cross the median, barrier, or grass strip of a divided road?
sec06-card-f23.teaching_text: Cutting across unpaved medians damages turf, risks rollovers, and surprises fast left-lane drivers.

sec06-card-f24.question_text: What worn items affecting your ears or eyes are prohibited while driving?
sec06-card-f24.teaching_text: Noise-isolating headsets drown out emergency sirens while vision-blocking headwear hides blind-spot hazards.

sec06-card-f25.question_text: When does carrying passengers or cargo make operating a vehicle unlawful?
sec06-card-f25.teaching_text: Stacking boxes across side windows or crowding passengers near the shifter blocks sightlines and emergency steering.

sec06-card-f26.question_text: Under what condition may you swing open a vehicle door next to moving traffic?
sec06-card-f26.teaching_text: Checking behind before cracking the latch prevents dooring an approaching cyclist or losing your door to passing traffic.
sec06-card-f26.must_match_memory_hook: Only when clear of cars, bikes

visual_sync.text_span: Only when clear of cars, bikes

sec06-card-f27.question_text: When may traffic deviate from the posted arrow direction of a one-way street?
sec06-card-f27.teaching_text: Outside temporary detour signs, traffic officers, or official emergency vehicles, one-way arrows bind every driver.

sec06-card-f28.question_text: How must you warn trailing traffic when slowing down or stopping suddenly?
sec06-card-f28.teaching_text: Early brake-lamp taps—or downward left-arm signals if bulbs fail—give following drivers vital reaction feet.

sec06-card-r01.question_text: In what surroundings and traffic spacing should high-beam headlights be used?
sec06-card-r01.teaching_text: Brights reach far down dark country roads yet blind anyone nearby in city streets or active traffic.

sec06-card-r02.question_text: At what exact evening-to-morning window and weather conditions does Georgia require headlights?
sec06-card-r02.teaching_text: Memorize Georgia's thirty-minute twilight rule—half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise—plus any rain or low visibility.

sec06-card-r03.question_text: Within how many feet must you dim high beams for an oncoming car versus a vehicle you are following?
sec06-card-r03.teaching_text: Head-on glare blinds at five hundred feet, while bright beams in a rearview mirror dazzle drivers inside two hundred feet.

sec06-card-r04.question_text: Under which lighting, weather, and sightline conditions must you choose low beams over high beams?
sec06-card-r04.teaching_text: High beams bounce straight back off fog, heavy rain, snow, and smoke, worsening glare whenever visibility drops below two hundred feet.

sec06-card-r05.question_text: What three maintenance habits keep your headlights working properly?
sec06-card-r05.teaching_text: Road salt film cuts light output in half, and misaligned housings either miss hazards or blind oncoming traffic.

sec06-card-r06.question_text: How should your headlight beam reach limit your nighttime driving speed?
sec06-card-r06.teaching_text: Driving faster than your beams light up means by the time a deer or stalled car appears, stopping in time is impossible.

sec06-card-r07.question_text: When should you slow down at night, and which painted line guides your lane in terrible visibility?
sec06-card-r07.teaching_text: Looking toward the white right-edge stripe avoids oncoming headlight blindness, using the centerline only if no edge line exists.

sec06-card-r08.question_text: What glass care and roadside scanning habits improve safety at night?
sec06-card-r08.teaching_text: Interior film scatters oncoming glare while careful edge scanning catches dark-clothed walkers and unlit breakdowns.

sec06-card-r09.question_text: What two nighttime mistakes—involving fatigue and stopping—must you avoid?
sec06-card-r09.teaching_text: Pushing on drowsy invites microsleep drift, while stopping on dark travel lanes invites high-speed rear-end hits.

sec06-card-r10.question_text: Who must wear safety belts in the front seat versus any seat of a passenger vehicle in Georgia?
sec06-card-r10.teaching_text: Adults must buckle up in the front row, while everyone younger than eighteen must buckle in both front and back seats.

sec06-card-r11.question_text: What does primary enforcement mean for Georgia's safety-belt law?
sec06-card-r11.teaching_text: Police can pull over and ticket an unbuckled violation on its own without needing any other traffic infraction.

sec06-card-r12.question_text: Which three physical protections does wearing a seat belt properly provide during a crash?
sec06-card-r12.teaching_text: Staying inside the cabin while spreading impact across strong bones stops you from slamming into the dash or other riders.

sec06-card-r13.question_text: Until what age must children ride in an approved height-and-weight-matched child restraint in Georgia?
sec06-card-r13.teaching_text: Outside narrow exceptions like taxis and public transit, children under eight need approved car seats or boosters.

sec06-card-r14.question_text: Beyond phones, what everyday tasks or cabin factors count as dangerous in-car distractions in Georgia?
sec06-card-r14.teaching_text: Adjusting audio, eating, grooming, programming navigation, or managing rowdy passengers and pets pulls focus off traffic.

sec06-card-r15.question_text: What broad rule does Georgia's due-care statute enforce behind the wheel?
sec06-card-r15.teaching_text: Even if an activity does not involve a phone, anything that diverts attention from safe operation violates due care.

sec06-card-r16.question_text: How far back must you stay when following a responding fire truck, and how far when parking near an active fire scene?
sec06-card-r16.teaching_text: Keep those two exam numbers straight so trailing cars stay two hundred feet back and parked cars stay five hundred feet away.
sec06-card-r16.must_match_memory_hook: Two hundred following, five hundred parked

visual_sync.text_span: Two hundred following, five hundred parked

sec06-card-r17.question_text: Who does Georgia hold responsible when trash is tossed or dropped out of a motor vehicle?
sec06-card-r17.teaching_text: Even if a passenger drops waste out a window, accountability lands on the person operating the vehicle.

sec06-card-r18.question_text: Which land and water areas does Georgia's litter-control prohibition protect?
sec06-card-r18.teaching_text: Dumping rubbish violates state law everywhere—along roadsides, on private lots, and into rivers or lakes.

sec06-card-r19.question_text: What physical contact with a phone or standalone device does Georgia's Hands-Free Law forbid?
sec06-card-r19.teaching_text: Cradling a phone on your lap, thigh, or shoulder counts as supporting it with your body and earns a hands-free ticket.

sec06-card-r20.question_text: Through which four hands-free setups may Georgia drivers legally use a phone?
sec06-card-r20.teaching_text: Keeping the phone clipped in a mount or linked through wireless gear leaves both hands on the wheel.

sec06-card-r21.question_text: Which text-based electronic activities are illegal while driving under Georgia's Hands-Free Law?
sec06-card-r21.teaching_text: Reading incoming texts, checking email, or browsing web pages violates the law even if you never type a reply.

sec06-card-r22.question_text: What three video-related phone actions does Georgia's Hands-Free Law prohibit while driving?
sec06-card-r22.teaching_text: Streaming shows, filming road clips, or livestreaming behind the wheel pulls eyes completely off live traffic.

sec06-card-r23.question_text: What is your first choice when approaching a flashing-light postal vehicle or active sanitation truck?
sec06-card-r23.teaching_text: Mail carriers and sanitation workers step around blind truck corners repeatedly, so vacating the adjacent lane gives vital margin.

sec06-card-r24.question_text: If you cannot safely change lanes away from a flashing postal or active sanitation vehicle, what speed rule applies?
sec06-card-r24.teaching_text: Drop at least ten below the limit—or to twenty-five, whichever is higher—while covering the brake to stop immediately.

sec11-card-f01.question_text: How should you apply the Georgia manual's safety guidelines when real-world conditions unfold on the road?
sec11-card-f01.teaching_text: No printed checklist covers every surprise, so smart drivers constantly evaluate actual traffic, road, and weather conditions.

sec11-card-f02.question_text: What tool and vehicle reference point tell you the right air pressure for your tires?
sec11-card-f02.teaching_text: Match the driver door-jamb sticker with a pressure gauge rather than inflating to the tire sidewall's maximum limit.

sec11-card-f03.question_text: At what two times should you inspect your tires for tread wear and sidewall damage?
sec11-card-f03.teaching_text: Monthly checks plus a pre-trip walkaround catch nails, bulges, or bald inner edges before highway heat triggers blowouts.

sec11-card-f04.question_text: Which side should you board from when parked on a street — and what rule applies if you must use the street side?
sec11-card-f04.teaching_text: Swinging a street-side door open in front of passing cars or cyclists causes serious collisions.

sec11-card-f05.question_text: How should you carry your keys and walk toward a street-parked car, and what cabin adjustments come before rolling?
sec11-card-f05.teaching_text: Walking toward oncoming cars lets you see drifting bumpers instead of turning your back to live traffic.

sec11-card-f06.question_text: Before shifting out of park, what two checks should you run on your passengers?
sec11-card-f06.teaching_text: Making sure nobody blocks mirror sightlines and every buckle clicks before moving protects the entire cabin.

sec11-card-f07.question_text: Which road users and hazards must you scan for — and what signal step applies — before pulling into traffic?
sec11-card-f07.teaching_text: Checking mirrors and blind spots for cyclists and pedestrians before signaling prevents curbside pull-out crashes.

sec11-card-f08.question_text: How does upright driving posture help, and when is taking one hand off the steering wheel acceptable?
sec11-card-f08.teaching_text: Sitting tall widens road visibility and leverage while keeping two hands steady except for brief gear or wiper tasks.

sec11-card-f09.question_text: Which general steering-wheel clock grip does Georgia list, what alternative protects wrists near airbags, and whose advice wins?
sec11-card-f09.teaching_text: Lower nine-and-three or eight-and-four grips keep arms clear of deploying steering-hub airbags compared with high hand positions.

sec11-card-f10.question_text: What is the best trip choice in heavy fog — and what speed and beam rules apply if you must drive?
sec11-card-f10.teaching_text: High beams bounce blinding white glare off dense fog droplets, making visibility worse instead of better.

sec11-card-f11.question_text: Why should you slow down even further in fog as soon as you spot another vehicle's headlights or taillights?
sec11-card-f11.teaching_text: Fog distorts depth perception so severely that faint taillights ahead may belong to a car completely stopped.

sec11-card-f12.question_text: Which two vehicle light modes does the Georgia manual warn against using while driving through fog?
sec11-card-f12.teaching_text: Driving on dim parking lamps hides you, and rolling with hazard flashers makes trailing drivers think you stopped.

sec11-card-f13.question_text: What separates your tire from the pavement during hydroplaning, and which three controls suffer?
sec11-card-f13.teaching_text: Once a film of standing water lifts rubber off asphalt, steering, braking, and acceleration fade together.

sec11-card-f14.question_text: How do you recover once hydroplaning starts, and what two factors help prevent it beforehand?
sec11-card-f14.teaching_text: Deep tire tread grooves plus slower wet-road speeds pump water out before it wedges under your footprint.

sec11-card-f15.question_text: What defines a skid, and what combination of road surface and driver inputs makes one likely?
sec11-card-f15.teaching_text: Jerking the steering wheel or stabbing the brakes overloads reduced wet or icy tire friction.

sec11-card-f16.question_text: What sequence of throttle, steering, and light braking brings your car safely out of a skid?
sec11-card-f16.teaching_text: Wait until steering in the skid's direction restores rolling grip before applying light brake pressure.

sec11-card-f17.question_text: During what opening window of a rainstorm does Georgia warn pavement is especially slick, and why?
sec11-card-f17.teaching_text: Remember Georgia's half-hour benchmark — fresh rain mixes with dripped road oil before sustained showers wash it away.

sec11-card-f18.question_text: What do yellow advisory speed signs before a curve tell you compared with the highway's regular posted speed?
sec11-card-f18.teaching_text: Sharp bends can throw cars wide at highway speed, especially when rain cuts cornering grip.

sec11-card-f19.question_text: When should you slow for a curve — and how should you recover if you realize mid-curve you entered too fast?
sec11-card-f19.teaching_text: Stomping the brake pedal mid-turn shifts weight violently and breaks rear tires into a spin.

sec11-card-f20.question_text: If your wheels run off the pavement edge, what four immediate habits prevent a rollover or spin?
sec11-card-f20.teaching_text: Wrenching the wheel immediately back up a dropped shoulder lip flings vehicles sideways across oncoming traffic.

sec11-card-f21.question_text: After drifting off the road, what speed and traffic checks belong before re-entering — including stopping if needed?
sec11-card-f21.teaching_text: Slowing way down — or stopping completely on the shoulder — lets you pick a clean traffic gap.

sec11-card-f22.question_text: Right when a tire blows out, what must you do with the steering wheel, gas pedal, and brakes?
sec11-card-f22.teaching_text: Holding the wheel firmly counters the blown tire's drag while releasing throttle lets speed bleed safely.

sec11-card-f23.question_text: How slow should you get after a blowout before steering onto the shoulder — and what if you already swerved off-road?
sec11-card-f23.teaching_text: Turning onto soft gravel too fast — or yanking a swerved car back onto asphalt — flips rims sideways.

sec11-card-f24.question_text: Whose instructions must you follow when fitting snow tires or tire chains for winter driving?
sec11-card-f24.teaching_text: Wrong-sized chains tear brake lines or fenders if they violate vehicle, tire, or chain manufacturer clearances.

sec11-card-f25.question_text: How much window glass must be cleared of snow and ice before driving?
sec11-card-f25.teaching_text: Peeking through a small scraped windshield slot leaves side and rear windows completely blind at intersections.

sec11-card-f26.question_text: When safe, how can you feel out winter road traction, and how should you handle stops, turns, and gaps?
sec11-card-f26.teaching_text: Gentle test taps and tiny wheel inputs reveal hidden ice early so you slow gradually with extra space.

sec11-card-f27.question_text: Which seven vehicle items — including inside the footwell — should you inspect alongside route and supply prep before winter trips?
sec11-card-f27.teaching_text: Checking thick winter floor mats alongside batteries, antifreeze, and tires stops bunched rubber from pinning your gas pedal.

sec11-card-f28.question_text: Why can't your senses detect carbon monoxide, and which two garage or mechanical mistakes risk poisoning?
sec11-card-f28.teaching_text: Colorless, odorless exhaust builds lethal concentrations rapidly inside garages or cabins above rusted mufflers.

sec11-card-f29.question_text: Why shouldn't you sit inside a parked, running vehicle with all windows rolled shut to run heat or AC?
sec11-card-f29.teaching_text: Stationary idling lets tailpipe fumes pool beneath the car and seep into a sealed cabin.

sec11-card-f30.question_text: Why must you never twist the ignition key into the lock position while your vehicle is rolling?
sec11-card-f30.teaching_text: Turning into lock clicks a mechanical pin into the steering shaft, freezing your wheel straight toward roadside hazards.

sec11-card-f31.question_text: What count does the Georgia manual's reference-point following method use under ordinary conditions?
sec11-card-f31.teaching_text: Note Georgia's specific handbook benchmark — its baseline reference-point count starts around two seconds before weather adjustments.

sec11-card-f32.question_text: In which four lighting, weather, roadwork, or traffic situations must you add space beyond Georgia's ordinary interval?
sec11-card-f32.teaching_text: Darkness, slick rain, orange construction barrels, and packed commuter lanes all demand longer reaction buffers.

sec11-card-f33.question_text: Which seven speed, human, mechanical, and wind variables shape stopping distance — making printed charts guides only?
sec11-card-f33.teaching_text: Tired reflexes, tailwinds, worn shocks, or damp asphalt stretch real stops well past ideal textbook tables.

sec11-card-f34.question_text: How does higher impact speed affect the force of a collision?
sec11-card-f34.teaching_text: Crash energy climbs dramatically as speed rises, overwhelming crumple zones and seat belts in severe hits.

sec11-card-r01.question_text: Where are drivers legally allowed to enter and leave a controlled-access expressway?
sec11-card-r01.teaching_text: Cutting across grassy medians or unpaved shoulders onto expressways is illegal and invites high-speed broadside wrecks.

sec11-card-r02.question_text: What is the job of an expressway acceleration lane, and who holds right-of-way during the merge?
sec11-card-r02.teaching_text: Through traffic already cruising on the expressway holds priority, so ramp drivers adjust speed to slip into gaps.

sec11-card-r03.question_text: How should you position early for an expressway exit, and where should you shed highway speed?
sec11-card-r03.teaching_text: Moving to the exit-side lane early and braking inside the deceleration ramp obeys ramp signs without jamming main lanes.

sec11-card-r04.question_text: If a short ramp forces you to begin slowing inside a main travel lane before exiting, how must you warn traffic behind?
sec11-card-r04.teaching_text: Early turn signals and light brake-lamp flashes alert fast highway traffic before your gap closes.

sec11-card-r05.question_text: On which side of a divided highway's median must you drive unless signs, controls, or an officer direct otherwise?
sec11-card-r05.teaching_text: Keeping right of physical medians and obeying lane striping prevents deadly wrong-way entries onto divided highways.

sec11-card-r06.question_text: What is the painted gore area where an acceleration lane meets a travel lane, and may you drive across its solid white lines?
sec11-card-r06.teaching_text: Stay inside the acceleration lane until its solid white gore boundary ends instead of cutting early across paint.

sec11-card-r07.question_text: What pavement symbol and roadside signage identify high-occupancy-vehicle lanes in Georgia?
sec11-card-r07.teaching_text: Check both the white lane diamond and posted restriction plaques before entering HOV lanes solo.

sec11-card-r08.question_text: What three expressway trip points — plus live road updates — should you plan before setting out?
sec11-card-r08.teaching_text: Knowing your entrance, exit, and rest stops plus construction detours beforehand eliminates panicked ramp dives.

sec11-card-r09.question_text: Why should you check fuel, water, oil, and tires before entering an expressway?
sec11-card-r09.teaching_text: Long stretches between interchanges mean running dry or overheating traps you along fast highway shoulders.

sec11-card-r10.question_text: How do mirrors and direct head checks work together before an expressway lane change?
sec11-card-r10.teaching_text: Mirrors track ongoing traffic flow, while a direct glance over your shoulder clears the adjacent blind spot.

sec11-card-r11.question_text: What two positioning choices keep you out of another vehicle's blind spot — especially alongside a large truck?
sec11-card-r11.teaching_text: Hovering beside trailer wheels hides your car completely, so either hang back in mirror sight or pass briskly.

sec11-card-r12.question_text: When must your turn signal start flashing for a lane change?
sec11-card-r12.teaching_text: Flicking the blinker after your tires already touch the lane stripe steals warning time from nearby drivers.

sec11-card-r13.question_text: What rear check starts an expressway pass, and what visual cue confirms it is safe to return right?
sec11-card-r13.teaching_text: Waiting until the overtaken vehicle appears clearly in your inside rearview mirror prevents clipping its front bumper.

sec11-card-r14.question_text: Which two posted speed boundaries must expressway drivers obey?
sec11-card-r14.teaching_text: Driving below an expressway's posted minimum speed creates rear-end hazards nearly as dangerous as speeding.

sec11-card-r15.question_text: Which three habits keep you safe inside dense commuting traffic?
sec11-card-r15.teaching_text: Holding steady buffers and obeying ramp meters or lane signals prevents accordion chain-reaction fender-benders.

sec11-card-r16.question_text: When is backing up permitted on an expressway?
sec11-card-r16.teaching_text: Missing an exit means continuing to the next interchange — backing up on lanes or shoulders is always forbidden.

sec11-card-r17.question_text: Where should you pull off for routine breaks, and which three non-emergencies never justify stopping on an expressway shoulder?
sec11-card-r17.teaching_text: Pull into rest areas to swap drivers, stretch legs, or grab dropped items rather than parking beside fast traffic.
