sec11-card-r18.question_text: If an actual breakdown forces an expressway shoulder stop, what two trouble signals apply and what walking warning holds?
sec11-card-r18.teaching_text: Raising your hood and running four-way flashers signals distress clearly while staying off fast shoulders saves lives.

sec11-card-r19.question_text: What must you do when drowsiness sets in, and why shouldn't you trust caffeine or stimulant products?
sec11-card-r19.teaching_text: Energy drinks or coffee mask tiredness only briefly before sudden microsleep snaps your eyes shut at speed.

sec11-card-r20.question_text: How do you fight monotony on long expressway drives so your awareness stays sharp?
sec11-card-r20.teaching_text: Shifting your gaze actively between far horizon, close lanes, and mirrors breaks glazed highway tunnel vision.

sec11-card-r21.question_text: Which three directions around your vehicle must defensive drivers monitor while keeping an escape path in mind?
sec11-card-r21.teaching_text: Tracking all sides continuously ensures you already know where to steer if another driver cuts across your nose.

sec11-card-r22.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out in front of an approaching car just because its turn signal is blinking?
sec11-card-r22.teaching_text: Wait until the approaching vehicle visibly slows and begins turning, since drivers often forget a flashing blinker.

sec11-card-r23.question_text: What two maintenance and driving-volume habits help lower your vehicle's exhaust emissions?
sec11-card-r23.teaching_text: Keeping spark, air, and fuel systems tuned per factory schedules plus cutting solo trips trims tailpipe pollution.

sec11-card-r24.question_text: What is the legal status of removing or disabling factory emission-control equipment?
sec11-card-r24.teaching_text: Stripping off catalytic converters or factory emission sensors directly violates state and federal vehicle-equipment laws.

sec11-card-r25.question_text: Which three travel habits cut traffic congestion, and how should you handle idling and engine warm-ups?
sec11-card-r25.teaching_text: Bundling errands, carpooling, or riding transit cuts road volume while skipping needless warm-up idling saves fuel.

sec12-card-f01.question_text: When must you stop and remain stopped for a pedestrian in a Georgia crosswalk, and how is your half defined?
sec12-card-f01.teaching_text: Georgia law requires a full stop—not merely slowing or swerving around—whenever walkers enter your directional lanes or the adjacent lane.

sec12-card-f02.question_text: Does a green light, a completed stop sign halt, or a permitted turn excuse you from stopping for crosswalk pedestrians?
sec12-card-f02.teaching_text: Turning cars and fresh green-light traffic must still hold back until every crossing pedestrian clears their directional lanes.

sec12-card-f03.question_text: What must you do for sidewalk pedestrians before pulling onto a street from a driveway, alley, or private road?
sec12-card-f03.teaching_text: Rolling straight to the street curb to check traffic cuts right across pedestrians walking along the sidewalk.

sec12-card-f04.question_text: Which two mobility aids signal that a crossing pedestrian is blind and holds full right-of-way?
sec12-card-f04.teaching_text: Never honk or rev your engine near a blind pedestrian—stay completely stopped until they finish crossing.

sec12-card-f05.question_text: Where do legal crosswalks exist even without white paint, and where else can painted crosswalks appear?
sec12-card-f05.teaching_text: Missing painted stripes at a residential corner never cancels pedestrian crosswalk rights where sidewalks extend across.

sec12-card-f06.question_text: Where must your vehicle stop relative to the crosswalk at a red light or stop sign?
sec12-card-f06.teaching_text: Parking your hood across crosswalk lines forces walkers out into live cross-street traffic.

sec12-card-f07.question_text: When a crosswalk has no traffic lights, what pedestrian position triggers your duty to stop?
sec12-card-f07.teaching_text: Unsignalized midblock or neighborhood crossings carry the exact same stop-and-stay-stopped protection as busy signalized intersections.

sec12-card-f08.question_text: At which high-activity zones should you scan both curbs for walkers, and where must you look before backing?
sec12-card-f08.teaching_text: Foot traffic clusters unpredictably around schools, parks, transit stops, and parking lots where distracted drivers overlook curbs.

sec12-card-f09.question_text: What two-direction scan sequence prevents hitting pedestrians during a permitted right turn on red?
sec12-card-f09.teaching_text: Drivers staring left for a gap often roll forward into a pedestrian stepping off the right-side curb.

sec12-card-f10.question_text: Why is passing a stopped vehicle near a crosswalk on a multilane street so dangerous?
sec12-card-f10.teaching_text: Breezing past a halted SUV in the next lane causes classic multiple-threat pedestrian strikes inside crosswalks.

sec12-card-f11.question_text: How far back from a multilane crosswalk does Georgia recommend stopping so adjacent-lane drivers can spot the pedestrian?
sec12-card-f11.teaching_text: Leaving a ten-foot sightline cushion opens an angle for neighboring lanes to see walkers before passing you.

sec12-card-f12.question_text: Where must you stop when pulling into or out of a driveway, alley, or parking garage?
sec12-card-f12.teaching_text: Blind garage walls and hedges hide joggers and strollers until your bumper reaches the sidewalk edge.

sec12-card-f13.question_text: Which two conflicts must both be clear before turning left across traffic into a driveway?
sec12-card-f13.teaching_text: Rushing through a brief gap in oncoming cars can trap you nose-first across a busy sidewalk.

sec12-card-f14.question_text: Why does even a modest rise in vehicle speed sharply worsen the outcome of a pedestrian crash?
sec12-card-f14.teaching_text: Without steel crumple zones, airbags, or belts, human bodies absorb exponentially greater impact force as speed climbs.

sec12-card-f15.question_text: During what hours and across how much of the road network should you expect bicycle traffic?
sec12-card-f15.teaching_text: Commuters and shift workers ride well before dawn and after dark, not just on sunny weekend afternoons.

sec12-card-f16.question_text: Which Georgia roadways ban bicycles, and how much lane space may cyclists use everywhere else?
sec12-card-f16.teaching_text: Outside controlled-access interstates, cyclists hold full-lane rights whenever narrow lanes, debris, or turns require it.

sec12-card-f17.question_text: Must a Georgia bicyclist stay inside an adjacent painted bike lane if one is present?
sec12-card-f17.teaching_text: Broken glass, parked car doors, or upcoming left turns legally justify a cyclist riding in the main lane.

sec12-card-f18.question_text: What visual connection helps prevent misunderstandings with a bicyclist near an intersection?
sec12-card-f18.teaching_text: Confirming mutual awareness before turning or pulling out prevents right-of-way surprises at busy corners.

sec12-card-f19.question_text: What is Georgia's minimum passing clearance around a bicycle, and why do riders need that lateral space?
sec12-card-f19.teaching_text: Sudden grates, cracks, or potholes force cyclists to swerve inches away from curb edges without warning.

sec12-card-f20.question_text: When road layout and traffic permit, what is Georgia's preferred lane maneuver for passing a bicyclist?
sec12-card-f20.teaching_text: Moving all the way into a neighboring lane gives cyclists maximum buffer rather than skimming past.

sec12-card-f21.question_text: If you cannot change lanes to pass a bicycle in Georgia, what exact speed reduction and clearance rule must you follow?
sec12-card-f21.teaching_text: Drop at least ten below the limit—or to twenty-five, whichever is higher—while holding three feet throughout.

sec12-card-f22.question_text: Why might a cyclist make an unexpected lateral move near an intersection?
sec12-card-f22.teaching_text: Fast multilane traffic can block a cyclist from merging left early, forcing late positioning near corners.

sec12-card-f23.question_text: How should you use your headlights when meeting an oncoming bicyclist at night?
sec12-card-f23.teaching_text: Blinding high-beam glare washes out a night rider's view of potholes and pavement edges just like oncoming drivers.

sec12-card-f24.question_text: May motorists use a painted bicycle lane for driving or curbside parking?
sec12-card-f24.teaching_text: Blocking dedicated bike lanes forces vulnerable cyclists to swerve abruptly into faster motor-vehicle traffic.

sec12-card-f25.question_text: When is a bicyclist allowed to pass motor vehicles on the right side?
sec12-card-f25.teaching_text: Check your right mirror and blind spot before turning right because cyclists legally filter past slowed cars.

sec12-card-f26.question_text: How do bicyclists communicate upcoming turns, slowing down, or stopping to surrounding drivers?
sec12-card-f26.teaching_text: Because bicycles lack bright brake lamps and amber blinkers, extended left or right arms serve as legal signals.

sec12-card-r01.question_text: How do a motorcyclist's legal traffic status and crash vulnerability compare with car occupants?
sec12-card-r01.teaching_text: With zero surrounding steel cage, even a low-speed fender-bender throws a motorcyclist directly onto asphalt.

sec12-card-r02.question_text: How does a motorcycle's narrow silhouette trick your depth perception, and what two checks counter it?
sec12-card-r02.teaching_text: Slim profiles fool human eyes into underestimating closing speed, causing left-turn cutoffs and blind-spot sideswipes.

sec12-card-r03.question_text: May a car squeeze alongside a motorcycle within the same traffic lane to pass or ride beside it?
sec12-card-r03.teaching_text: Riders need full lane width to lean into curves and dodge wind blasts or debris.

sec12-card-r04.question_text: If a motorcyclist shifts from the left side of their lane to the right side, does that mean they are preparing to turn?
sec12-card-r04.teaching_text: Experienced riders constantly adjust lane tracks to escape blind spots and oil streaks without intending to turn.

sec12-card-r05.question_text: Which road-surface conditions can force a motorcyclist to slow down or shift lane position without warning?
sec12-card-r05.teaching_text: Two narrow contact patches react sharply to bridge grates, angled tracks, and milled grooves that cars barely feel.

sec12-card-r06.question_text: Why must you wait until a signaling motorcyclist visibly begins turning before pulling into their path?
sec12-card-r06.teaching_text: Many motorcycle blinkers require manual thumb cancellation, so an old forgotten flasher can lure you into a crash.

sec12-card-r07.question_text: What following time gap does the Georgia handbook recommend behind a motorcycle?
sec12-card-r07.teaching_text: Generous spacing prevents panic stops when a rider engine-brakes without lighting up the rear brake lamp.

sec12-card-r08.question_text: How should you handle your speed and steering while a motorcyclist is overtaking you?
sec12-card-r08.teaching_text: Speeding up or drifting toward the centerline traps an overtaking rider in wind wash or oncoming traffic.

sec12-card-r09.question_text: How should you execute a pass around a motorcycle from start to finish?
sec12-card-r09.teaching_text: Cutting back in tightly blasts the rider with bumper turbulence and forces dangerous shoulder swerves.

sec12-card-r10.question_text: When is oncoming traffic excused from stopping for a loading school bus in Georgia—and who must always stop?
sec12-card-r10.teaching_text: Only a dividing median relieves opposite-side drivers, while every lane moving with the bus must still halt.

sec12-card-r11.question_text: When may you start driving again after stopping for a school bus?
sec12-card-r11.teaching_text: Even if red flashers click off, stay put until every student steps safely clear of the pavement.

sec12-card-r12.question_text: Why do large trucks need extra room at corners compared with passenger cars?
sec12-card-r12.teaching_text: Extended trailer length and heavy mass make sharp cornering impossible without wide swing clearance.

sec12-card-r13.question_text: What term does the Georgia handbook use for the large blind areas on all four sides of a truck or bus?
sec12-card-r13.teaching_text: Lingering in any of those four hidden pockets leaves the commercial driver completely unaware your car is there.

sec12-card-r14.question_text: What four load and hitch checks must you handle before towing a trailer?
sec12-card-r14.teaching_text: Overloading hitch limits or stacking cargo tail-heavy triggers violent trailer sway at highway speed.

sec12-card-r15.question_text: Beyond weight and tie-downs, how should you prepare your vehicles, visibility, and skills before towing?
sec12-card-r15.teaching_text: Practicing wide turns and backing in an empty lot—with extended mirrors—prevents jackknifes in tight traffic.

sec12-card-r16.question_text: What mindset and response advice does the handbook emphasize for safe trailering and handling lost control?
sec12-card-r16.teaching_text: Panic steering or slamming brakes amplifies trailer fishtailing, whereas calm patience keeps combinations stable.

sec12-card-r17.question_text: How can you tell when riding beside a truck or bus whether you are sitting in a side blind spot?
sec12-card-r17.teaching_text: Commercial drivers rely entirely on cab mirrors for flank visibility, so losing sight of their face makes you invisible.

sec12-card-r18.question_text: Why is lingering in a truck's or bus's right-side blind spot especially dangerous?
sec12-card-r18.teaching_text: Right-side no-zones stretch deeper across lanes right where wide-turning trailers sweep inward toward curbs.

sec12-card-r19.question_text: What double visibility problem happens when you tailgate inside a truck's rear blind spot?
sec12-card-r19.teaching_text: Hugging a trailer bumper hides your car from cab mirrors while walling off brake lights and hazards ahead.

sec12-card-r20.question_text: Why must you never merge close in front of a truck or bus and immediately slow down?
sec12-card-r20.teaching_text: Heavy rigs need far longer stopping distance and cannot shed highway momentum when a car cuts in.

sec12-card-r21.question_text: What visual check in your rearview mirror confirms enough space to return ahead of a truck or bus?
sec12-card-r21.teaching_text: Waiting until the whole cab grille frames inside your mirror leaves a safe braking buffer behind you.

sec12-card-r22.question_text: How should you behave around commercial trucks and buses at highway entrance ramps and merge zones?
sec12-card-r22.teaching_text: Heavy rigs accelerate slowly onto highways and cannot dodge aggressive cutoffs, tailgaters, or last-second ramp sprints.

sec13-card-f01.question_text: When may Georgia DDS pull your driving privileges based on your overall safety pattern?
sec13-card-f01.teaching_text: Repeatedly careless or risky behavior gives the state authority to step in before a preventable crash happens.

sec13-card-f02.question_text: What triggers a Georgia license cancellation, and what can a resident do once eligible again?
sec13-card-f02.teaching_text: Test questions contrast administrative cancellation over missing facts or lost eligibility against punitive suspensions and revocations.

sec13-card-f03.question_text: How does revocation affect your driving privilege, and how does a Georgia resident return afterward?
sec13-card-f03.teaching_text: Unlike a temporary pause, formal termination wipes out the old credential and demands a brand-new application later.

sec13-card-f04.question_text: After a Georgia revocation period ends, what does an out-of-state driver apply to restore?
sec13-card-f04.teaching_text: Because Georgia never issued their home plastic card, out-of-state motorists seek restored permission to drive on state roads.

sec13-card-f05.question_text: What does a Georgia license suspension do, and how long does that withdrawal stay active?
sec13-card-f05.teaching_text: Waiting out the calendar is rarely enough on its own if required reinstatement steps remain unfinished.

sec13-card-f06.question_text: Once a required suspension period finishes, what may residents versus nonresidents seek to reinstate?
sec13-card-f06.teaching_text: Knowledge checks pair resident credential or eligibility restoration against a visiting motorist's local roadway permission.

sec13-card-f07.question_text: Which convictions do courts send in, and when does DDS update your permanent driving record?
sec13-card-f07.teaching_text: Every qualifying traffic judgment flows straight into your permanent state history as soon as the court transmits it.

sec13-card-f08.question_text: What does Georgia do when someone licensed or living elsewhere gets convicted here?
sec13-card-f08.teaching_text: Picking up a ticket away from home will still follow you straight back to your own licensing agency.

sec13-card-f09.question_text: How can a qualifying Georgia conviction affect a nonresident or someone who has no license yet?
sec13-card-f09.teaching_text: Even without a Georgia card in your wallet today, a serious offense can freeze future licensing eligibility.

sec13-card-f10.question_text: How does Georgia treat reported traffic convictions that you receive in another state or country?
sec13-card-f10.teaching_text: Crossing state lines never shields your Georgia driving history when outside courts report violations back.

sec13-card-f11.question_text: Which four test-refusal, court-no-show, or unpaid-obligation triggers can withdraw your license without a conviction?
sec13-card-f11.teaching_text: Ignoring a citation, skipping Super Speeder fees, refusing chemical tests, or owing child support pulls privileges fast.

sec13-card-f12.question_text: Besides unpaid obligations or missed court, what three nonconviction actions can withdraw a credential?
sec13-card-f12.teaching_text: Minors often forget that the responsible adult who backed their credential can ask to pull it back.

sec13-card-f13.question_text: Which five major roadway or criminal convictions trigger mandatory license suspension in Georgia?
sec13-card-f13.teaching_text: High-danger choices like street racing, running from police, or leaving a crash carry automatic loss of privileges.

sec13-card-f14.question_text: Which three insurance, registration, or license-status offenses are listed grounds for suspension?
sec13-card-f14.teaching_text: Getting caught behind the wheel without active coverage, valid registration, or an active license compounds penalties fast.

sec13-card-f15.question_text: Which three crash-harm crimes involving death, an unborn child, or severe injury cause suspension?
sec13-card-f15.teaching_text: Catastrophic harm caused with a motor vehicle triggers mandatory loss of driving privileges alongside criminal prosecution.

sec13-card-f16.question_text: What penalty may a court impose if you violate a restriction printed on your license?
sec13-card-f16.teaching_text: Treating corrective lenses, passenger limits, or curfew codes as optional lets a judge pull your card.

sec13-card-f17.question_text: Which reckless, school-bus, and blind-passing convictions trigger extra suspension rules under age twenty-one?
sec13-card-f17.teaching_text: Younger motorists lose their license immediately on high-risk moves that might only add points for older adults.

sec13-card-f18.question_text: How much speeding over the limit—or what point value on a single ticket—suspends a driver under twenty-one?
sec13-card-f18.teaching_text: One heavy lead-foot ticket or any four-point conviction sidelines an under-twenty-one driver right away.

sec13-card-f19.question_text: How many points within what timeframe will suspend a Georgia driver younger than eighteen?
sec13-card-f19.teaching_text: Teen drivers have a tiny margin for error because even two minor tickets in a year can hit four.

sec13-card-f20.question_text: What does Georgia's implied-consent rule cover regarding chemical tests and your driver's license?
sec13-card-f20.teaching_text: Using Georgia roads carries built-in testing rules where refusing state tests or hitting the legal limit threatens privileges.

sec13-card-f21.question_text: When are you entitled to an extra chemical test by qualified personnel of your own choice, and who pays?
sec13-card-f21.teaching_text: Demanding your own private test before completing the officer's required state test counts as an unlawful refusal.

sec13-card-f22.question_text: How many serious convictions within what time window trigger a habitual-violator license revocation?
sec13-card-f22.teaching_text: Stacking three major roadway crimes inside a five-year span escalates punishment all the way to revocation.

sec13-card-f23.question_text: Which major offenses—including stunt driving, racing, fleeing, and impaired driving—count toward habitual-violator status?
sec13-card-f23.teaching_text: Combining any three listed severe crimes—from hit-and-run or impaired driving to reckless stunt driving—triggers revocation.

sec13-card-f24.question_text: What can happen if you refuse a notified DDS reexamination backed by reasonable grounds or cannot drive safely?
sec13-card-f24.teaching_text: Skipping a required safety recheck leaves DDS clear authority to revoke privileges when safe driving is in doubt.

sec13-card-r01.question_text: How do points land on a Georgia driving record, including tickets earned outside the state?
sec13-card-r01.teaching_text: Any out-of-state violation that carries points under Georgia rules adds up on your home record just the same.

sec13-card-r02.question_text: What is Georgia's standard point total and month window that triggers a license suspension?
sec13-card-r02.teaching_text: Test questions frequently pair fifteen points with two years to check whether you mix up adult and teen caps.

sec13-card-r03.question_text: How do Georgia's four-point suspension rules differ between drivers under twenty-one and drivers under eighteen?
sec13-card-r03.teaching_text: Watch the distinction: one four-point ticket suspends anyone under twenty-one, while totaling four in twelve months suspends under eighteen.

sec13-card-r04.question_text: Which date controls the points-accumulation window, and which date controls single high-point suspensions at ages eighteen to twenty?
sec13-card-r04.teaching_text: Delaying court past a birthday can matter for age-eighteen-to-twenty single offenses, yet violation dates still lock point windows.

sec13-card-r05.question_text: What happens to your accumulated point total after you serve a points-based suspension?
sec13-card-r05.teaching_text: Serving out an accumulated-points suspension wipes the active point tally clean, though convictions remain on record.

sec13-card-r06.question_text: How is a no-contest plea treated for Georgia's license suspensions applying under age twenty-one?
sec13-card-r06.teaching_text: Entering a no-contest plea will not shield a driver under twenty-one from an age-triggered license suspension.

sec13-card-r07.question_text: How many points can a licensed Georgia resident ask to remove, and how often is that allowed?
sec13-card-r07.teaching_text: Knowing both numbers—up to seven points and once per five years—is a classic Georgia knowledge check.

sec13-card-r08.question_text: What course length and certificate delivery are required to request Georgia's points reduction?
sec13-card-r08.teaching_text: Photocopies or sending paperwork to the wrong office fails because DDS needs the original certificate by mail or in person.

sec13-card-r09.question_text: When must you complete a certified six-hour course to use Georgia's separate points-avoidance process?
sec13-card-r09.teaching_text: Unlike post-conviction reduction with DDS, points avoidance happens between receiving the ticket and appearing in court, or by court order.

sec13-card-r10.question_text: Where does the original certificate go in a points-avoidance plea, what benefits apply, and how often?
sec13-card-r10.teaching_text: Giving the court your original certificate skips points and trims the fine by one-fifth once every five years.

sec13-card-r11.question_text: What can happen to your license if a crash-damage claim goes unsatisfied under the safety-responsibility law?
sec13-card-r11.teaching_text: Leaving collision damages unresolved under financial-responsibility rules can cost you your driving privileges.

sec13-card-r12.question_text: How can your insurer stop a safety-responsibility suspension when you had active liability coverage during the crash?
sec13-card-r12.teaching_text: Having your insurance carrier submit the official coverage verification proves active liability protection existed at impact.

sec13-card-r13.question_text: What signed document from the claimant can be filed with DDS to answer a safety-responsibility claim?
sec13-card-r13.teaching_text: Settling directly or setting payment terms works when the other party signs a general or conditional release for DDS.

sec13-card-r14.question_text: If you post security for claimed damages plus financial-responsibility proof, how long does DDS hold that security?
sec13-card-r14.teaching_text: DDS keeps posted damage security for twelve months and until required proof regarding any lawsuit is supplied.

sec13-card-r15.question_text: How many days do you have to request a hearing after receiving a safety-responsibility suspension order?
sec13-card-r15.teaching_text: Missing that tight ten-day window after receiving notice forfeits your chance to contest the order beforehand.

sec13-card-r16.question_text: What essential trip purposes can an eligible Georgia limited driving permit authorize?
sec13-card-r16.teaching_text: Restricted permits cover strictly approved necessities—like jobs, classes, prescriptions, treatment, probation, community service, or unlicensed immediate family.

sec13-card-r17.question_text: How narrowly can DDS tailor a limited permit, and does it ever allow commercial vehicle operation?
sec13-card-r17.teaching_text: Even when granted for work, a limited permit never lets anyone operate a commercial motor vehicle.

sec13-card-r18.question_text: What happens if you get convicted of a moving violation or break the rules of your limited permit?
sec13-card-r18.teaching_text: Any moving ticket or off-route trip wipes out the hardship permit and lengthens the underlying license suspension.

sec13-card-r19.question_text: What factors shape limited-permit eligibility, and who makes the final call on issuing one?
sec13-card-r19.teaching_text: Meeting general textbook examples never guarantees approval because DDS weighs your age, offense, and full record.
